verses.sanskrit: यन्महोपनिषद्वेद्यं चिदाकाशतया स्थितम् । परमाद्वैतसाम्राज्यं तद्रामब्रह्म मे गतिः
verses.transliteration: yanmahopaniṣadvedyaṃ cidākāśatayā sthitam | paramādvaitasāmrājyaṃ tadrāmabrahma me gatiḥ
verses.translation: That Rama-Brahman, the empire of supreme non-duality, which is to be known through the Mahopanishad and abides as the space of consciousness, is my refuge.

verses.sanskrit: ॐ आप्यायन्तु मामाङ्गानि वाक्प्राणश्चक्षुः श्रोत्रमथो बलमिन्द्रियाणि च
verses.transliteration: oṃ āpyāyantu māmāṅgāni vākprāṇaścakṣuḥ śrotramatho balamindriyāṇi ca
verses.translation: Om. May my limbs, speech, breath, eye, ear, strength and all my faculties grow strong.

verses.sanskrit: सर्वाणि सर्वं ब्रह्मोपनिषदं माहं ब्रह्म निराकुर्यां मा मा ब्रह्म निराकरोदनिरकरणमस्त्वनिराकारणं मेस्तु तदात्मनि निरते य उपनिषत्सु धर्मास्ते मयि सन्तु ते मयि सन्तु
verses.transliteration: sarvāṇi sarvaṃ brahmopaniṣadaṃ māhaṃ brahma nirākuryāṃ mā mā brahma nirākarodanirakaraṇamastvanirākāraṇaṃ mestu tadātmani nirate ya upaniṣatsu dharmāste mayi santu te mayi santu
verses.translation: All is Brahman, the Upanishad. May I never reject Brahman, and may Brahman never reject me; may there be no rejection, no rejection for me. Let the truths taught in the Upanishads abide in me, who delight in the Self; let them abide in me.

verses.sanskrit: ॐ शान्तिः शान्तिः शान्तिः
verses.transliteration: oṃ śāntiḥ śāntiḥ śāntiḥ
verses.translation: Om. Peace, peace, peace.

verses.sanskrit: अथातो महोपनिषदं व्याख्यास्यमस्तदाहुरेको ह वै नारायण आसीन्न ब्रह्मा नेशानो नापो नाग्नीषोमौ नेमे द्यावापृथिवी न नक्षत्राणि न सूर्यो न चन्द्रमाः । स एकाकी न रमते । तस्य ध्यानान्तःस्थस्य यज्ञस्तोममुच्यते
verses.transliteration: athāto mahopaniṣadaṃ vyākhyāsyamastadāhureko ha vai nārāyaṇa āsīnna brahmā neśāno nāpo nāgnīṣomau neme dyāvāpṛthivī na nakṣatrāṇi na sūryo na candramāḥ | sa ekākī na ramate | tasya dhyānāntaḥsthasya yajñastomamucyate
verses.translation: Now we shall explain the Mahopanishad. They say: In the beginning there was only Narayana — not Brahma, not Ishana, not the waters, not Agni and Soma, not these heaven and earth, not the stars, not the sun, not the moon. He alone found no delight. As he rested in meditation, the sacrificial hymn was uttered.

verses.sanskrit: तस्मिन्पुरुषाश्चतुर्दश जायन्ते । एका कन्या । दशेन्द्रियाणि मन एकादशं तेजः । द्वादशोऽहङ्कारः । त्रयोदशकः प्राणः । चतुर्दश आत्मा । पञ्चदशी बुद्धिः । भूतानि पञ्च तन्मात्राणि । पञ्च महाभूतानि
verses.transliteration: tasminpuruṣāścaturdaśa jāyante | ekā kanyā | daśendriyāṇi mana ekādaśaṃ tejaḥ | dvādaśo'haṅkāraḥ | trayodaśakaḥ prāṇaḥ | caturdaśa ātmā | pañcadaśī buddhiḥ | bhūtāni pañca tanmātrāṇi | pañca mahābhūtāni
verses.translation: In him fourteen persons arise, and one maiden: the ten senses, the mind as the eleventh, radiance as the twelfth, egoism as the thirteenth, life-breath as the fourteenth, the Self as the fifteenth, intellect, the five elements, the five subtle elements, and the five great elements.

verses.sanskrit: स एकः पञ्चविंशतिः पुरुषः । तत्पुरुषं पुरुषो निवेश्य नास्य प्रधानसंवत्सरा जायन्ते । संवत्सरादधिजायन्ते । अथ पुनरेव नारायणः सोऽन्यत्कामो मनसाध्यायत । तस्य ध्यानान्तःस्थस्य ललाटात्त्र्यक्षः शूलपाणिः पुरुषो जायते
verses.transliteration: sa ekaḥ pañcaviṃśatiḥ puruṣaḥ | tatpuruṣaṃ puruṣo niveśya nāsya pradhānasaṃvatsarā jāyante | saṃvatsarādadhijāyante | atha punareva nārāyaṇaḥ so'nyatkāmo manasādhyāyata | tasya dhyānāntaḥsthasya lalāṭāttryakṣaḥ śūlapāṇiḥ puruṣo jāyate
verses.translation: He is the one, the twenty-fifth Person. Having set that Person within him, no years arise for him from Prakriti; years arise afterward. Then Narayana again, desiring another, meditated with the mind. As he rested in meditation, from his forehead a three-eyed Person with a trident in his hand was born.

verses.sanskrit: बिभ्रच्छ्रियं यशः सत्यं ब्रह्मचर्यं तपो वैराग्यं मन ऐश्वर्यं सप्रणवा व्याहृतय ऋग्यजुःसामाथर्वाङ्गिरसः सर्वाणि छन्दांसि तान्यङ्गे समाश्रितानि । तस्मादीशानो महादेवो महादेवः । अथ पुनरेव नारायणः सोऽन्यत्कामो मनसाध्यायत
verses.transliteration: bibhracchriyaṃ yaśaḥ satyaṃ brahmacaryaṃ tapo vairāgyaṃ mana aiśvaryaṃ sapraṇavā vyāhṛtaya ṛgyajuḥsāmātharvāṅgirasaḥ sarvāṇi chandāṃsi tānyaṅge samāśritāni | tasmādīśāno mahādevo mahādevaḥ | atha punareva nārāyaṇaḥ so'nyatkāmo manasādhyāyata
verses.translation: Bearing glory, fame, truth, celibacy, austerity, dispassion, mind, and lordship, with the sacred syllable and the utterances, the Rik, Yajus, Saman and Atharvangirasa, and all the meters, which rest on his limbs — therefore he is Ishana, Mahadeva, Mahadeva. Then Narayana again, desiring another, meditated with the mind.

verses.sanskrit: तस्य ध्यानान्तःस्थस्य ललाटात्स्वेदोऽपपत् । ता इमाः प्रतता आपः । ततस्तेजो हिरण्मयमण्डलम् । तत्र ब्रह्मा चतुर्मुखोऽजायत । सोऽध्याय्त् । पूर्वाभिमुखो भूत्वा भूरिति व्याहृतिर्गायत्रं छन्द ऋग्वेदोऽग्निर्देवता
verses.transliteration: tasya dhyānāntaḥsthasya lalāṭātsvedo'papat | tā imāḥ pratatā āpaḥ | tatastejo hiraṇmayamaṇḍalam | tatra brahmā caturmukho'jāyata | so'dhyāyt | pūrvābhimukho bhūtvā bhūriti vyāhṛtirgāyatraṃ chanda ṛgvedo'gnirdevatā
verses.translation: As he rested in meditation, sweat fell from his forehead. Those are these spread waters. From them arose a golden orb of light. In it Brahma the four-faced was born. He meditated. Facing east: the utterance Bhuh, the Gayatri meter, the Rigveda, Agni the deity.

verses.sanskrit: पश्चिमाभिमुखो भूत्वा भुवरिति व्याहृतिस्त्रैष्टुभं छन्दो यजुर्वेदो वायुर्देवता । उत्तराभिमुखो भूत्वा स्वरिति व्याहृतिर्जाग्रतं छन्दः सामवेदः सूर्यो देवता । दक्षिणाभिमुखो भूत्वा महरितिव्याहृतिरानुष्टभ छन्दोऽथर्ववेदाः सोमो देवता
verses.transliteration: paścimābhimukho bhūtvā bhuvariti vyāhṛtistraiṣṭubhaṃ chando yajurvedo vāyurdevatā | uttarābhimukho bhūtvā svariti vyāhṛtirjāgrataṃ chandaḥ sāmavedaḥ sūryo devatā | dakṣiṇābhimukho bhūtvā maharitivyāhṛtirānuṣṭabha chando'tharvavedāḥ somo devatā
verses.translation: Facing west: the utterance Bhuvah, the Trishtubh meter, the Yajurveda, Vayu the deity. Facing north: the utterance Svah, the Jagati meter, the Samaveda, Surya the deity. Facing south: the utterance Mahah, the Anushtubh meter, the Atharvaveda, Soma the deity.

verses.sanskrit: सहस्रशीर्षं देवं सहस्राक्षं विश्वसम्भुवम् । विश्वतः परमं नित्यं विश्वं नारायणं हरिम् । विश्वमेवेदं पुरुषस्तद्विश्वमुपजीवति । पतिं विश्वेश्वरं देवं समुद्रे विश्वरूपिणम् । पद्मकोशप्रतीकाशं लम्बत्याकोशसंनिभम्
verses.transliteration: sahasraśīrṣaṃ devaṃ sahasrākṣaṃ viśvasambhuvam | viśvataḥ paramaṃ nityaṃ viśvaṃ nārāyaṇaṃ harim | viśvamevedaṃ puruṣastadviśvamupajīvati | patiṃ viśveśvaraṃ devaṃ samudre viśvarūpiṇam | padmakośapratīkāśaṃ lambatyākośasaṃnibham
verses.translation: The thousand-headed god, thousand-eyed, source of the universe, supreme and eternal on all sides, the all, Narayana Hari. The Person is indeed all this, and the universe lives on him; lord of the universe, the god of universal form in the ocean. Resembling a lotus bud, it hangs like a bud.

verses.sanskrit: हृदयं चाप्यधोमुखं सन्तत्यै सीत्कराभीश्च । तस्य मध्ये महानर्चिर्विश्वर्चिर्विश्वतोमुखम् । तस्य मध्ये वह्निशिखा अणीयोर्ध्वा व्यवस्थिता । तस्याः शिखाया मध्ये परमात्मा व्यवस्थिता । स ब्रह्मा स ईशानः सेन्द्रः सोऽक्षरः परमः स्वराडिति महोपनिषत्
verses.transliteration: hṛdayaṃ cāpyadhomukhaṃ santatyai sītkarābhīśca | tasya madhye mahānarcirviśvarcirviśvatomukham | tasya madhye vahniśikhā aṇīyordhvā vyavasthitā | tasyāḥ śikhāyā madhye paramātmā vyavasthitā | sa brahmā sa īśānaḥ sendraḥ so'kṣaraḥ paramaḥ svarāḍiti mahopaniṣat
verses.translation: The heart too, facing downward, for the sake of continuity. In its middle is a great flame, universal and facing every direction. In its middle a fire-flame, subtle and upright, is established. In the middle of that flame is established the Supreme Self. He is Brahma, he is Ishana, with Indra, he is the imperishable, the supreme, the self-luminous: thus the Mahopanishad.

verses.sanskrit: शुको नाम महातेजाः स्वरूपानन्दतत्परः । जातमात्रेण मुनिराड् यत्सत्यं तदवाप्तवान्
verses.transliteration: śuko nāma mahātejāḥ svarūpānandatatparaḥ | jātamātreṇa munirāḍ yatsatyaṃ tadavāptavān
verses.translation: There was one named Shuka, of great radiance, devoted to the bliss of his own nature, king of sages; from the moment of birth he attained the truth.

verses.sanskrit: तेनासौ स्वविवेकेन स्वयमेव महामनाः । प्रविचार्य चिरं साधु स्वात्मनिश्चयमाप्तवान्
verses.transliteration: tenāsau svavivekena svayameva mahāmanāḥ | pravicārya ciraṃ sādhu svātmaniścayamāptavān
verses.translation: By his own discernment, that great-minded one himself reflected well for a long time and reached certainty of his Self.

verses.sanskrit: अनाख्यत्वादगम्यत्वान्मनःषष्ठेन्द्रियस्थितेः । चिन्मात्रमेवमात्माणुराकाशादपि सूक्ष्मकः
verses.transliteration: anākhyatvādagamyatvānmanaḥṣaṣṭhendriyasthiteḥ | cinmātramevamātmāṇurākāśādapi sūkṣmakaḥ
verses.translation: Because it cannot be described or reached, and because the mind is the sixth sense, the Self is mere consciousness — an atom, subtler even than space.

verses.sanskrit: चिदणोः परमस्यान्तः कोटिब्रह्माण्डरेणवः । उत्पत्तिस्थितिमभ्येत्य लीयन्ते शक्तिपर्ययात्
verses.transliteration: cidaṇoḥ paramasyāntaḥ koṭibrahmāṇḍareṇavaḥ | utpattisthitimabhyetya līyante śaktiparyayāt
verses.translation: Within the supreme atom of consciousness, crores of universes are like specks of dust; they arise, abide, and dissolve by the turning of power.

verses.sanskrit: आकाशं बाह्यशून्यत्वादनाकाशं तु चित्त्वतः । न किंचिद्यदनिर्देश्यं वस्तु सत्तेति किंचन
verses.transliteration: ākāśaṃ bāhyaśūnyatvādanākāśaṃ tu cittvataḥ | na kiṃcidyadanirdeśyaṃ vastu satteti kiṃcana
verses.translation: It is space because outside it is void, yet not space because it is consciousness; there is nothing that cannot be pointed to, which is called existence.

verses.sanskrit: चेतनोऽसौ प्रकाशत्वाद्वेद्याभावाच्छिलोपमः । स्वात्मनि व्योमनि स्वस्थे जगदुन्मेषचित्रकृत्
verses.transliteration: cetano'sau prakāśatvādvedyābhāvācchilopamaḥ | svātmani vyomani svasthe jagadunmeṣacitrakṛt
verses.translation: This conscious one, being luminous and having no object to know, is like a rock; yet in its own sky-like Self, established in itself, it paints the wonder of the world's unfolding.

verses.sanskrit: तद्भामात्रमिदं विश्वमिति न स्यात्ततः पृथक् । जगद्भेदोऽपि तद्भानमिति भेदोऽपि तन्मयः
verses.transliteration: tadbhāmātramidaṃ viśvamiti na syāttataḥ pṛthak | jagadbhedo'pi tadbhānamiti bhedo'pi tanmayaḥ
verses.translation: This universe is only its radiance, so it is not apart from it; even the world's difference is its appearance, so difference too is made of it.

verses.sanskrit: सर्वगः सर्वसम्बन्धो गत्यभावान्न गच्छति । नास्त्यसावश्रयाभावात्सद्रूपत्वादथास्ति च
verses.transliteration: sarvagaḥ sarvasambandho gatyabhāvānna gacchati | nāstyasāvaśrayābhāvātsadrūpatvādathāsti ca
verses.translation: All-pervading, related to all, it does not go, for lack of motion; it does not exist, for lack of support — and yet it exists, being of the nature of being.

verses.sanskrit: विज्ञानमानन्दं ब्रह्म रातेर्दातुः परायणम् । सर्वसंकल्पसंन्यासश्चेतसा यत्परिग्रहः
verses.transliteration: vijñānamānandaṃ brahma rāterdātuḥ parāyaṇam | sarvasaṃkalpasaṃnyāsaścetasā yatparigrahaḥ
verses.translation: Knowledge-bliss is Brahman, the supreme refuge of the giver of gifts; it is the renunciation of all intention, which the mind clings to.

verses.sanskrit: जाग्रतः प्रत्ययाभावं यस्याहुः प्रत्ययं बुधाः । यत्संकोचविकासाभ्यां जगत्प्रलयसृष्टयः
verses.transliteration: jāgrataḥ pratyayābhāvaṃ yasyāhuḥ pratyayaṃ budhāḥ | yatsaṃkocavikāsābhyāṃ jagatpralayasṛṣṭayaḥ
verses.translation: The wise say that its cognition is the absence of the waking cognitions; by its contraction and expansion the world's dissolution and creation occur.

verses.sanskrit: निष्ठा वेदान्तवाक्यानामथ वाचामगोचरः । अहं सच्चित्परानन्दब्रह्मैवास्मि न चेतरः
verses.transliteration: niṣṭhā vedāntavākyānāmatha vācāmagocaraḥ | ahaṃ saccitparānandabrahmaivāsmi na cetaraḥ
verses.translation: It is the culmination of the Vedanta sayings and beyond the reach of speech: "I am Brahman, being-consciousness-supreme bliss, and nothing else."

verses.sanskrit: स्वयैव सूक्ष्मया बुद्ध्या सर्वं विज्ञातवाञ्छुकः । स्वयं प्राप्ते परे वस्तुन्यविश्रान्तमनाः स्थितः
verses.transliteration: svayaiva sūkṣmayā buddhyā sarvaṃ vijñātavāñchukaḥ | svayaṃ prāpte pare vastunyaviśrāntamanāḥ sthitaḥ
verses.translation: By his own subtle intellect Shuka understood everything; having himself reached the supreme reality, his mind remained settled, unwavering.

verses.sanskrit: इदं वस्त्विति विश्वासं नासावात्मन्युपाययौ । केवलं विररामास्य चेतो विषयचापलम् । भोगेभ्यो भूरिभङ्गेभ्यो धाराभ्य इव चातकः
verses.transliteration: idaṃ vastviti viśvāsaṃ nāsāvātmanyupāyayau | kevalaṃ virarāmāsya ceto viṣayacāpalam | bhogebhyo bhūribhaṅgebhyo dhārābhya iva cātakaḥ
verses.translation: He did not attain the belief in himself that "this is a thing." His mind simply ceased its restless attachment to objects, to many broken pleasures, as the chataka bird turns from streams of water.

verses.sanskrit: एकदा सोऽमलप्रज्ञो मेरावेकान्तसंस्थितः । पप्रच्छ पितरं भक्त्या कृष्णद्वैपायनं मुनिम्
verses.transliteration: ekadā so'malaprajño merāvekāntasaṃsthitaḥ | papraccha pitaraṃ bhaktyā kṛṣṇadvaipāyanaṃ munim
verses.translation: Once, that one of pure insight, abiding in solitude on Meru, devoutly asked his father, the sage Krishna Dvaipayana.

verses.sanskrit: संसाराडम्बरमिदं कथमभ्युत्थितं मुने । कथं च प्रशमं याति किं यत्कस्य कदा वद
verses.transliteration: saṃsārāḍambaramidaṃ kathamabhyutthitaṃ mune | kathaṃ ca praśamaṃ yāti kiṃ yatkasya kadā vada
verses.translation: "O sage, how has this pageantry of the world arisen? How does it come to rest? What is it, whose is it, and when? Tell me."

verses.sanskrit: एवं पृष्टेन मुनिना व्यासेनाखिलमात्मजे । यथावदखिलं प्रोक्तं वक्तव्यं विदितात्मना
verses.transliteration: evaṃ pṛṣṭena muninā vyāsenākhilamātmaje | yathāvadakhilaṃ proktaṃ vaktavyaṃ viditātmanā
verses.translation: Thus asked, the sage Vyasa told his son everything, as it should be told by one who knows the Self.

verses.sanskrit: अज्ञासिषं पूर्वमेवमहमित्यथ तत्पितुः । स शुकः स्वकया बुद्ध्या न वाक्यं बहु मन्यते
verses.transliteration: ajñāsiṣaṃ pūrvamevamahamityatha tatpituḥ | sa śukaḥ svakayā buddhyā na vākyaṃ bahu manyate
verses.translation: "I have known it before," thought Shuka; and by his own understanding he did not value his father's words much.

verses.sanskrit: व्यासोऽपि भगवान्बुद्ध्वा पुत्राभिप्रायमीदृशम् । प्रत्युवाच पुनः पुत्रं नाहं जानामि तत्त्वतः
verses.transliteration: vyāso'pi bhagavānbuddhvā putrābhiprāyamīdṛśam | pratyuvāca punaḥ putraṃ nāhaṃ jānāmi tattvataḥ
verses.translation: Even the revered Vyasa, understanding his son's intention, replied again: "I do not know it truly.

verses.sanskrit: जनको नाम भूपालो विद्यते मिथिलापुरे । यथावद्वेत्त्यसौ वेद्यं तस्मात्सर्वमवाप्स्यसि
verses.transliteration: janako nāma bhūpālo vidyate mithilāpure | yathāvadvettyasau vedyaṃ tasmātsarvamavāpsyasi
verses.translation: There is a king named Janaka in the city of Mithila. He knows what is to be known as it is; from him you will obtain everything."

verses.sanskrit: पित्रेत्युक्तः शुकः प्रायात्सुमेरोर्वसुधातलम् । विदेहनगरीं प्राप जनकेनाभिपालिताम्
verses.transliteration: pitretyuktaḥ śukaḥ prāyātsumerorvasudhātalam | videhanagarīṃ prāpa janakenābhipālitām
verses.translation: Told thus by his father, Shuka set out from Sumeru to the earth and reached the city of Videha, ruled by Janaka.

verses.sanskrit: आवेदितोऽसौ याष्टीकैर्जनकाय महात्मने । द्वारि व्याससुतो राजञ्छुकोऽत्र स्थितवानिति
verses.transliteration: āvedito'sau yāṣṭīkairjanakāya mahātmane | dvāri vyāsasuto rājañchuko'tra sthitavāniti
verses.translation: The mace-bearers informed the great Janaka: "O king, Vyasa's son Shuka stands at the door."

verses.sanskrit: जिज्ञासार्थं शुकस्यासावास्तामेवेत्यवज्ञया । उक्त्वा बभूव जनकस्तूष्णीं सप्त दिनान्यथ
verses.transliteration: jijñāsārthaṃ śukasyāsāvāstāmevetyavajñayā | uktvā babhūva janakastūṣṇīṃ sapta dinānyatha
verses.translation: Saying carelessly "Let him stay there," to test Shuka, Janaka remained silent for seven days.

verses.sanskrit: ततः प्रवेशयामास जनकः शुकमङ्गणे । तत्राहानि स सप्तैव तथैवावसदुन्मनाः
verses.transliteration: tataḥ praveśayāmāsa janakaḥ śukamaṅgaṇe | tatrāhāni sa saptaiva tathaivāvasadunmanāḥ
verses.translation: Then Janaka had Shuka enter the courtyard; there he stayed seven days in the same way, unmoved.

verses.sanskrit: ततः प्रवेशयामास जनकोऽन्तःपुराजिरे । राजा न दृश्यते तावदिति सप्तदिनानि तम्
verses.transliteration: tataḥ praveśayāmāsa janako'ntaḥpurājire | rājā na dṛśyate tāvaditi saptadināni tam
verses.translation: Then Janaka had him enter the inner palace court; "the king is not seen," so for seven days.

verses.sanskrit: तत्रोन्मदाभिः कान्ताभिर्भोजनैर्भोगसंचयैः । जनको लालयामास शुकं शशिनिभाननम्
verses.transliteration: tatronmadābhiḥ kāntābhirbhojanairbhogasaṃcayaiḥ | janako lālayāmāsa śukaṃ śaśinibhānanam
verses.translation: There Janaka entertained Shuka, whose face shone like the moon, with intoxicated beautiful women, with meals and heaps of pleasures.

verses.sanskrit: ते भोगास्तानि भोज्यानि व्यासपुत्रस्य तन्मनः । नाजह्वुर्मन्दपवनो बद्धपीठमिवाचलम्
verses.transliteration: te bhogāstāni bhojyāni vyāsaputrasya tanmanaḥ | nājahvurmandapavano baddhapīṭhamivācalam
verses.translation: Those pleasures and those foods did not carry away the mind of Vyasa's son, as a gentle breeze does not move a fixed mountain.

verses.sanskrit: केवलं सुसमः स्वच्छो मौनी मुदितमानसः । सम्पूर्ण इव शीतांशुरतिष्ठदमलः शुकः
verses.transliteration: kevalaṃ susamaḥ svaccho maunī muditamānasaḥ | sampūrṇa iva śītāṃśuratiṣṭhadamalaḥ śukaḥ
verses.translation: He remained only perfectly even, clear, silent, joyful in mind, spotless like the full moon, Shuka.

verses.sanskrit: परिज्ञातस्वभावं तं शुकं स जनको नृपः । आनीय मुदितात्मानमवलोक्य ननाम ह
verses.transliteration: parijñātasvabhāvaṃ taṃ śukaṃ sa janako nṛpaḥ | ānīya muditātmānamavalokya nanāma ha
verses.translation: King Janaka, having perceived the nature of Shuka, brought him in, saw him with a joyful heart, and bowed to him.

verses.sanskrit: निःशेषितजगत्कार्यः प्राप्ताखिलमनोरथः । किमीप्सितं तवेत्याह कृतस्वागत आह तम्
verses.transliteration: niḥśeṣitajagatkāryaḥ prāptākhilamanorathaḥ | kimīpsitaṃ tavetyāha kṛtasvāgata āha tam
verses.translation: Having completed the world's tasks and attained every desire, he welcomed him and said: "What do you wish?"

verses.sanskrit: संसाराडम्बरमिदं कथमभ्युत्थितं गुरो । कथं प्रशममायाति यथावत्कथयाशु मे
verses.transliteration: saṃsārāḍambaramidaṃ kathamabhyutthitaṃ guro | kathaṃ praśamamāyāti yathāvatkathayāśu me
verses.translation: "O master, how has this pageantry of the world arisen? How does it come to rest? Tell me properly and quickly."

verses.sanskrit: यथावदखिलं प्रोक्तं जनकेन महात्मना । तदेव तत्पुरा प्रोक्तं तस्य पित्रा महाधिया
verses.transliteration: yathāvadakhilaṃ proktaṃ janakena mahātmanā | tadeva tatpurā proktaṃ tasya pitrā mahādhiyā
verses.translation: The great Janaka told him everything exactly; that was the very thing his wise father had said earlier.

verses.sanskrit: स्वयमेव मया पूर्वमभिज्ञातं विशेषतः । एतदेव हि पृष्टेन पित्रा मे समुदाहृतम्
verses.transliteration: svayameva mayā pūrvamabhijñātaṃ viśeṣataḥ | etadeva hi pṛṣṭena pitrā me samudāhṛtam
verses.translation: "I myself had known this in particular before; when asked, my father said just this to me.

verses.sanskrit: भवताप्येष एवार्थः कथितो वाग्विदां वर । एष एव हि वाक्यार्थः शास्त्रेषु परिदृश्यते
verses.transliteration: bhavatāpyeṣa evārthaḥ kathito vāgvidāṃ vara | eṣa eva hi vākyārthaḥ śāstreṣu paridṛśyate
verses.translation: "You too, best of the eloquent, have told me this same meaning; this alone is seen as the meaning of the scriptures.

verses.sanskrit: मनोविकल्पसंजातं तद्विकल्पपरिक्षयात् । क्षीयते दग्धसंसारो निःसार
verses.transliteration: manovikalpasaṃjātaṃ tadvikalpaparikṣayāt | kṣīyate dagdhasaṃsāro niḥsāra
verses.translation: "Born of the mind's imagining, with the end of that imagining the burnt-out world, without essence, is destroyed.

verses.sanskrit: तत्किमेतन्महाभाग सत्यं ब्रूहि ममाचलम् । त्वत्तो विश्रममाप्नोमि चेतसा भ्रमता जगत्
verses.transliteration: tatkimetanmahābhāga satyaṃ brūhi mamācalam | tvatto viśramamāpnomi cetasā bhramatā jagat
verses.translation: "Then is this so, O fortunate one? Tell me the unshakable truth; from you I attain rest, with a mind that wanders through the world."

verses.sanskrit: श्रुणु तावदिदानीं त्वं कथ्यमानमिदं मया । श्रीशुकं ज्ञानविस्तारं बुद्धिसारान्तरान्तरम्
verses.transliteration: śruṇu tāvadidānīṃ tvaṃ kathyamānamidaṃ mayā | śrīśukaṃ jñānavistāraṃ buddhisārāntarāntaram
verses.translation: Listen now to this which I tell you, O Shuka — the expanse of knowledge, the inmost essence of intellect.

verses.sanskrit: यद्विज्ञानात्पुमान्सद्यो जीवन्मुक्तत्वमाप्नुयात्
verses.transliteration: yadvijñānātpumānsadyo jīvanmuktatvamāpnuyāt
verses.translation: By knowing which a person at once attains liberation while living.

verses.sanskrit: दृश्यं नास्तीति बोधेन मनसो दृश्यमार्जनम् । सम्पन्नं चेत्तदुत्पन्ना परा निर्वाणनिर्वृतिः
verses.transliteration: dṛśyaṃ nāstīti bodhena manaso dṛśyamārjanam | sampannaṃ cettadutpannā parā nirvāṇanirvṛtiḥ
verses.translation: By the knowledge that "the seen does not exist," the wiping away of the mind's seen things; when this is achieved, supreme peace of liberation arises.

verses.sanskrit: अशेषेण परित्यागो वासनायां य उत्तमः । मोक्ष इत्युच्यते सद्भिः स एव विमलक्रमः
verses.transliteration: aśeṣeṇa parityāgo vāsanāyāṃ ya uttamaḥ | mokṣa ityucyate sadbhiḥ sa eva vimalakramaḥ
verses.translation: The complete abandonment of impressions is the highest; the good call it liberation, the stainless way.

verses.sanskrit: ये शुद्धवासना भूयो न जन्मानर्थभागिनः । ज्ञातज्ञेयास्त उच्यन्ते जीवन्मुक्ता महाधियः
verses.transliteration: ye śuddhavāsanā bhūyo na janmānarthabhāginaḥ | jñātajñeyāsta ucyante jīvanmuktā mahādhiyaḥ
verses.translation: Those of pure impressions who do not again partake of birth and its evils, who have known what is to be known — these great-minded are called the liberated while living.

verses.sanskrit: पदार्थभावनादार्ढ्यं बन्ध इत्यभिधीयते । वासनातानवं ब्रह्मन्मोक्ष इत्यभिधीयते
verses.transliteration: padārthabhāvanādārḍhyaṃ bandha ityabhidhīyate | vāsanātānavaṃ brahmanmokṣa ityabhidhīyate
verses.translation: Firmness in the notion of things is called bondage; the thinning of impressions, O Brahmin, is called liberation.

verses.sanskrit: तपः प्रभृतिना यस्मै हेतुनैव विना पुनः । भोगा इह न रोचन्ते स जीवन्मुक्त उच्यते
verses.transliteration: tapaḥ prabhṛtinā yasmai hetunaiva vinā punaḥ | bhogā iha na rocante sa jīvanmukta ucyate
verses.translation: He who, without any cause such as austerity, finds no delight in pleasures here — he is called liberated while living.

verses.sanskrit: आपतत्सु यथाकालं सुखदुःखेष्वनारतः । न हृष्यति ग्लायति यः स जीवन्मुक्त उच्यते
verses.transliteration: āpatatsu yathākālaṃ sukhaduḥkheṣvanārataḥ | na hṛṣyati glāyati yaḥ sa jīvanmukta ucyate
verses.translation: He who in the pleasures and pains that arrive in due time neither rejoices nor sinks — he is called liberated while living.

verses.sanskrit: हर्षामर्षभयक्रोधकामकार्पण्यदृष्टिभिः । न परामृश्यते योऽन्तः स जीवन्मुक्त उच्यते
verses.transliteration: harṣāmarṣabhayakrodhakāmakārpaṇyadṛṣṭibhiḥ | na parāmṛśyate yo'ntaḥ sa jīvanmukta ucyate
verses.translation: He who is not touched within by views of joy, anger, fear, wrath, desire or meanness — he is called liberated while living.

verses.sanskrit: अहंकारमयीं त्यक्त्वा वासनां लीलयैव यः । तिष्ठति ध्येयसंत्यागी स जीवन्मुक्त उच्यते
verses.transliteration: ahaṃkāramayīṃ tyaktvā vāsanāṃ līlayaiva yaḥ | tiṣṭhati dhyeyasaṃtyāgī sa jīvanmukta ucyate
verses.translation: He who has playfully given up impressions made of egoism and remains a renouncer of objects of meditation — he is called liberated while living.

verses.sanskrit: ईप्सितानीप्सिते न स्तो यस्यान्तर्वर्तिदृष्टिषु । सुषुप्तिवद्यश्चरति स जीवन्मुक्त उच्यते
verses.transliteration: īpsitānīpsite na sto yasyāntarvartidṛṣṭiṣu | suṣuptivadyaścarati sa jīvanmukta ucyate
verses.translation: For whom, in the views within, there are no desired or undesired things, who acts as if in deep sleep — he is called liberated while living.

verses.sanskrit: अध्यात्मरतिरासीनः पूर्णः पावनमानसः । प्राप्तानुत्तमविश्रान्तिर्न किंचिदिह वाञ्छति । यो जीवति गतस्नेहः स जीवन्मुक्त उच्यते
verses.transliteration: adhyātmaratirāsīnaḥ pūrṇaḥ pāvanamānasaḥ | prāptānuttamaviśrāntirna kiṃcidiha vāñchati | yo jīvati gatasnehaḥ sa jīvanmukta ucyate
verses.translation: Delighting in the Self, seated, full, of purified mind, having reached unsurpassed rest, wishing for nothing here, living free of attachment — he is called liberated while living.

verses.sanskrit: संवेद्येन हृदाकाशे मनागपि न लिप्यते । यस्यासावजडा संवित्स जीवन्मुक्त उच्यते
verses.transliteration: saṃvedyena hṛdākāśe manāgapi na lipyate | yasyāsāvajaḍā saṃvitsa jīvanmukta ucyate
verses.translation: He whose unclouded awareness is not tainted even slightly in the heart-space by what is known — he is called liberated while living.

verses.sanskrit: रागद्वेषौ सुखं दुःखं धर्माधर्मौ फलाफले । यः करोत्यनपेक्ष्यैव स जीवन्मुक्त उच्यते
verses.transliteration: rāgadveṣau sukhaṃ duḥkhaṃ dharmādharmau phalāphale | yaḥ karotyanapekṣyaiva sa jīvanmukta ucyate
verses.translation: He who acts without regard to love and hatred, pleasure and pain, merit and demerit, result and non-result — he is called liberated while living.

verses.sanskrit: मौनवान्निरहंभावो निर्मानो मुक्तमत्सरः । यः करोति गतोद्वेगः स जीवन्मुक्त उच्यते
verses.transliteration: maunavānnirahaṃbhāvo nirmāno muktamatsaraḥ | yaḥ karoti gatodvegaḥ sa jīvanmukta ucyate
verses.translation: Silent, free of I-ness, free of pride, free of envy, he who acts without agitation — he is called liberated while living.

verses.sanskrit: सर्वत्र विगतस्नेहो यः साक्षिवदवस्थितः । निरिच्छो वर्तते कार्ये स जीवन्मुक्त उच्यते
verses.transliteration: sarvatra vigatasneho yaḥ sākṣivadavasthitaḥ | niriccho vartate kārye sa jīvanmukta ucyate
verses.translation: He who is free of attachment everywhere, who stays like a witness, desireless in his actions — he is called liberated while living.

verses.sanskrit: येन धर्ममधर्मं च मनोमननमीहितम् । सर्वमन्तः परित्यक्तं स जीवन्मुक्त उच्यते
verses.transliteration: yena dharmamadharmaṃ ca manomananamīhitam | sarvamantaḥ parityaktaṃ sa jīvanmukta ucyate
verses.translation: He who has inwardly given up all mind-conceived merit and demerit and desire — he is called liberated while living.

verses.sanskrit: यावती दृश्यकलना सकलेयं विलोक्यते । सा येन सुष्ठु संत्यक्ता स जीवन्मुक्त उच्यते
verses.transliteration: yāvatī dṛśyakalanā sakaleyaṃ vilokyate | sā yena suṣṭhu saṃtyaktā sa jīvanmukta ucyate
verses.translation: He who has fully abandoned whatever whole imagining of the seen is perceived here — he is called liberated while living.

verses.sanskrit: कट्वम्ललवणं तिक्तममृष्टं मृष्टमेव च । सममेव च यो भुङ्क्ते स जीवन्मुक्त उच्यते
verses.transliteration: kaṭvamlalavaṇaṃ tiktamamṛṣṭaṃ mṛṣṭameva ca | samameva ca yo bhuṅkte sa jīvanmukta ucyate
verses.translation: He who eats alike the bitter, sour, salty, pungent, unsweet and sweet — he is called liberated while living.

verses.sanskrit: जरामरणमापच्च राज्यं दारिद्र्यमेव च । रम्यमित्येव यो भुङ्क्ते स जीवन्मुक्त उच्यते
verses.transliteration: jarāmaraṇamāpacca rājyaṃ dāridryameva ca | ramyamityeva yo bhuṅkte sa jīvanmukta ucyate
verses.translation: He who enjoys old age, death, calamity, kingdom and poverty alike as pleasant — he is called liberated while living.

verses.sanskrit: धर्माधर्मौ सुखं दुःखं तथा मरणजन्मनी । धिया येन सुसंत्यक्तं स जीवन्मुक्त उच्यते
verses.transliteration: dharmādharmau sukhaṃ duḥkhaṃ tathā maraṇajanmanī | dhiyā yena susaṃtyaktaṃ sa jīvanmukta ucyate
verses.translation: He by whose intellect merit and demerit, pleasure and pain, death and birth are well given up — he is called liberated while living.

verses.sanskrit: उद्वेगानन्दरहितः समया स्वच्छया धिया । न शोचते न चोदेति स जीवन्मुक्त उच्यते
verses.transliteration: udvegānandarahitaḥ samayā svacchayā dhiyā | na śocate na codeti sa jīvanmukta ucyate
verses.translation: Free of agitation and joy, with an even, clear intellect, neither grieving nor rising — he is called liberated while living.

verses.sanskrit: सर्वेच्छाः सकलाः शङ्काः सर्वेहाः सर्वनिश्चयाः । धिया येन परित्यक्ताः स जीवन्मुक्त उच्यते
verses.transliteration: sarvecchāḥ sakalāḥ śaṅkāḥ sarvehāḥ sarvaniścayāḥ | dhiyā yena parityaktāḥ sa jīvanmukta ucyate
verses.translation: He by whose intellect all desires, all doubts, all strivings and all certainties have been given up — he is called liberated while living.

verses.sanskrit: जन्मस्थितिविनाशेषु सोदयास्तमयेषु च । सममेव मनो यस्य स जीवन्मुक्त उच्यते
verses.transliteration: janmasthitivināśeṣu sodayāstamayeṣu ca | samameva mano yasya sa jīvanmukta ucyate
verses.translation: He whose mind is even in birth, continuance and destruction, in rising and setting — he is called liberated while living.

verses.sanskrit: न किंचन द्वेष्टि तथा न किंचिदपि काङ्क्षति । भुङ्क्ते यः प्रकृतान्भोगान्स जीवन्मुक्त उच्यते
verses.transliteration: na kiṃcana dveṣṭi tathā na kiṃcidapi kāṅkṣati | bhuṅkte yaḥ prakṛtānbhogānsa jīvanmukta ucyate
verses.translation: He who neither hates anything nor wishes for anything, who enjoys the pleasures that come naturally — he is called liberated while living.

verses.sanskrit: शान्तसंसारकलनः कलावानपि निष्कलः । यः सचित्तोऽपि निश्चित्तः स जीवन्मुक्त उच्यते
verses.transliteration: śāntasaṃsārakalanaḥ kalāvānapi niṣkalaḥ | yaḥ sacitto'pi niścittaḥ sa jīvanmukta ucyate
verses.translation: He for whom the world's imagining is quiet, who though having parts is partless, who though having a mind is mindless — he is called liberated while living.

verses.sanskrit: यः समस्तार्थजालेषु व्यवहार्यपि निःस्पृहः । परार्थेष्विव पूर्णात्मा स जीवन्मुक्त उच्यते
verses.transliteration: yaḥ samastārthajāleṣu vyavahāryapi niḥspṛhaḥ | parārtheṣviva pūrṇātmā sa jīvanmukta ucyate
verses.translation: He who, though acting among all the webs of objects, is free of longing, full in himself as if in others' affairs — he is called liberated while living.

verses.sanskrit: जीवन्मुक्तपदं त्यक्त्वा स्वदेहे कालसात्कृते । विशत्यदेहमुक्तत्वं पवनोऽस्पन्दतामिव
verses.transliteration: jīvanmuktapadaṃ tyaktvā svadehe kālasātkṛte | viśatyadehamuktatvaṃ pavano'spandatāmiva
verses.translation: Having left the state of liberation-while-living when his body is given over to time, he enters the liberation without body, as wind becomes motionless.

verses.sanskrit: विदेहमुक्तो नोदेति नास्तमेति न शाम्यति । न सन्नासन्न दूरस्थो न चाहं न च नेतरः
verses.transliteration: videhamukto nodeti nāstameti na śāmyati | na sannāsanna dūrastho na cāhaṃ na ca netaraḥ
verses.translation: The bodiless liberated one neither rises nor sets nor is stilled; he is neither existent nor non-existent, neither far, neither "I" nor "other."

verses.sanskrit: ततः स्तिमितगंभीरं न तेजो न तमस्ततम् । अनाख्यमनभिव्यक्तं सत्किंचिदवशिष्यते
verses.transliteration: tataḥ stimitagaṃbhīraṃ na tejo na tamastatam | anākhyamanabhivyaktaṃ satkiṃcidavaśiṣyate
verses.translation: Then there remains something, still and deep, neither light nor darkness spread, unnamed, unmanifest, merely existent.

verses.sanskrit: न शून्यं नापि चाकारो न दृश्यं नापि दर्शनम् । न च भूतपदार्थौघसदनन्ततया स्थितम्
verses.transliteration: na śūnyaṃ nāpi cākāro na dṛśyaṃ nāpi darśanam | na ca bhūtapadārthaughasadanantatayā sthitam
verses.translation: Neither void nor form, neither seen nor sight, standing endlessly, not as a mass of elements and things.

verses.sanskrit: किमप्यव्यपदेशात्मा पूर्णात्पूर्णतराकृतिः । न सन्नासन्न सदसन्न भावो भावनं न च
verses.transliteration: kimapyavyapadeśātmā pūrṇātpūrṇatarākṛtiḥ | na sannāsanna sadasanna bhāvo bhāvanaṃ na ca
verses.translation: Of an indescribable nature, fuller than full in form; neither existent nor non-existent nor both, neither being nor becoming.

verses.sanskrit: चिन्मात्रं चैत्यरहितमनन्तमजरं शिवम् । अनादिमध्यपर्यन्तं यदनादि निरामयम्
verses.transliteration: cinmātraṃ caityarahitamanantamajaraṃ śivam | anādimadhyaparyantaṃ yadanādi nirāmayam
verses.translation: Pure consciousness free of the perceived, infinite, ageless, auspicious, without beginning, middle or end, beginningless, free of disease.

verses.sanskrit: द्रष्टृदर्शनदृश्यानां मध्ये यद्दर्शनं स्मृतम् । नातः परतरं किंचिन्निश्चयोऽस्त्यपरो मुने
verses.transliteration: draṣṭṛdarśanadṛśyānāṃ madhye yaddarśanaṃ smṛtam | nātaḥ parataraṃ kiṃcinniścayo'styaparo mune
verses.translation: That vision which is held to be in the midst of seer, seeing and seen — there is nothing higher than this, O sage, no other certainty.

verses.sanskrit: स्वयमेव त्वया ज्ञातं गुरुतश्च पुनः श्रुतम् । स्वसंकल्पवशाद्बद्धो निःसंकल्पाद्विमुच्यते
verses.transliteration: svayameva tvayā jñātaṃ gurutaśca punaḥ śrutam | svasaṃkalpavaśādbaddho niḥsaṃkalpādvimucyate
verses.translation: You have known it yourself and heard it again from the teacher: bound by one's own intention, one is freed by non-intention.

verses.sanskrit: तेन स्वयं त्वया ज्ञातं ज्ञेयं यस्य महात्मनः । भोगेभ्यो ह्यरतिर्जाता दृश्याद्वा सकलादिह
verses.transliteration: tena svayaṃ tvayā jñātaṃ jñeyaṃ yasya mahātmanaḥ | bhogebhyo hyaratirjātā dṛśyādvā sakalādiha
verses.translation: Therefore the great soul has known by himself what is to be known; aversion to pleasures has arisen, or to all that is seen here.

verses.sanskrit: प्राप्तं प्राप्तव्यमखिलं भवता पूर्णचेतसा । स्वरूपे तपसि ब्रह्मन्मुक्तस्त्वं भ्रान्तिमुत्सृज
verses.transliteration: prāptaṃ prāptavyamakhilaṃ bhavatā pūrṇacetasā | svarūpe tapasi brahmanmuktastvaṃ bhrāntimutsṛja
verses.translation: You, of full mind, have obtained all that is to be obtained; in your own nature, in austerity, O Brahmin, you are free; abandon delusion.

verses.sanskrit: अतिबाह्यं तथा बाह्यमन्तराभ्यन्तरं धियः । शुक पश्यन्न पश्येस्त्वं साक्षी सम्पूर्णकेवलः
verses.transliteration: atibāhyaṃ tathā bāhyamantarābhyantaraṃ dhiyaḥ | śuka paśyanna paśyestvaṃ sākṣī sampūrṇakevalaḥ
verses.translation: Beyond the outer, the outer, and the inmost within the intellect, Shuka, you, seeing, do not see; you are the witness, full and alone.

verses.sanskrit: विशश्राम शुकस्तूष्णीं स्वस्थे परमवस्तुनि । वीतशोकभयायासो निरीहश्छिन्नसंशयः
verses.transliteration: viśaśrāma śukastūṣṇīṃ svasthe paramavastuni | vītaśokabhayāyāso nirīhaśchinnasaṃśayaḥ
verses.translation: Shuka rested silent in the supreme reality, in his own nature, free of grief, fear and effort, desireless, with doubts cut off.

verses.sanskrit: जगाम शिखरं मेरोः समाध्यर्थमखण्डितम्
verses.transliteration: jagāma śikharaṃ meroḥ samādhyarthamakhaṇḍitam
verses.translation: He went to the summit of Meru for unbroken samadhi.

verses.sanskrit: तत्र वर्षसहस्राणि निर्विकल्पसमाधिना । देशे स्थित्वा शशामासावात्मन्यस्नेहदीपवत्
verses.transliteration: tatra varṣasahasrāṇi nirvikalpasamādhinā | deśe sthitvā śaśāmāsāvātmanyasnehadīpavat
verses.translation: There, for thousands of years, in samadhi without conceptual thought, he remained in that place and became extinguished in the Self like a lamp without oil.

verses.sanskrit: व्यपगतकलनाकलङ्कशुद्धः स्वयममलात्मनि पावने पदेऽसौ । सलिलकण इवांबुधौ महात्मा विगलितवासनमेकतां जगाम
verses.transliteration: vyapagatakalanākalaṅkaśuddhaḥ svayamamalātmani pāvane pade'sau | salilakaṇa ivāṃbudhau mahātmā vigalitavāsanamekatāṃ jagāma
verses.translation: Purified of the stain of imagining, in the pure, spotless state of his own self, the great one, with impressions dissolved, attained oneness, like a drop of water in the ocean.

verses.sanskrit: इति महोपनिषत् ।
verses.transliteration: iti mahopaniṣat |
verses.translation: Thus the Mahopanishad.

verses.sanskrit: निदाघो नाम मुनिराट् प्राप्तविद्यश्च बालकः । विहृतस्तीर्थयात्रार्थं पित्रानुज्ञातवान्स्वयम्
verses.transliteration: nidāgho nāma munirāṭ prāptavidyaśca bālakaḥ | vihṛtastīrthayātrārthaṃ pitrānujñātavānsvayam
verses.translation: A young sage named Nidagha, a king among sages who had attained knowledge, having been permitted by his father, set out of his own accord on a pilgrimage to holy places.

verses.sanskrit: सार्धत्रिकोटितीर्थेषु स्नात्वा गृहमुपागतः । स्वोदन्तं कथयामास ऋभुं नत्वा महायशाः
verses.transliteration: sārdhatrikoṭitīrtheṣu snātvā gṛhamupāgataḥ | svodantaṃ kathayāmāsa ṛbhuṃ natvā mahāyaśāḥ
verses.translation: Having bathed at three and a half crore holy places, he returned home and, bowing to Ribhu, the illustrious one told his own story.

verses.sanskrit: सार्धत्रिकोटितीर्थेषु स्नानपुण्यप्रभावतः । प्रादुर्भूतोमनसि मे विचारः सोऽयमीदृशः
verses.transliteration: sārdhatrikoṭitīrtheṣu snānapuṇyaprabhāvataḥ | prādurbhūtomanasi me vicāraḥ so'yamīdṛśaḥ
verses.translation: "By the merit of bathing at three and a half crore holy places, this reflection arose in my mind:

verses.sanskrit: जायते म्रियते लोको म्रियते जननाय च । अस्थिरः सर्व एवेमे सचराचरचेष्टिताः । सर्वापदां पदं पापा भावा विभवभूमयः
verses.transliteration: jāyate mriyate loko mriyate jananāya ca | asthiraḥ sarva eveme sacarācaraceṣṭitāḥ | sarvāpadāṃ padaṃ pāpā bhāvā vibhavabhūmayaḥ
verses.translation: The world is born and dies, and dies only to be born; all these moving and unmoving activities are unstable; the glorious states of prosperity are the abodes of every calamity.

verses.sanskrit: अयःशलाकासदृशाः परस्परमसङ्गिनः । शुष्यन्ते केवला भावा मनःकल्पनयानया
verses.transliteration: ayaḥśalākāsadṛśāḥ parasparamasaṅginaḥ | śuṣyante kevalā bhāvā manaḥkalpanayānayā
verses.translation: Like iron rods, unconnected with one another, mere existences dry up through this imagination of the mind.

verses.sanskrit: भावेष्वरतिरायाता पथिकस्य मरुष्विव । शाम्यतीदं कथं दुःखमिति तप्तोऽस्मि चेतसा
verses.transliteration: bhāveṣvaratirāyātā pathikasya maruṣviva | śāmyatīdaṃ kathaṃ duḥkhamiti tapto'smi cetasā
verses.translation: Aversion to things has come upon me, like a traveler's in a desert; 'How will this sorrow be quenched?' — so my mind burns.

verses.sanskrit: चिन्तानिचयचक्राणि नानन्दाय धनानि मे । सम्प्रसूतकलत्राणि गृहाण्युग्रापदामिव
verses.transliteration: cintānicayacakrāṇi nānandāya dhanāni me | samprasūtakalatrāṇi gṛhāṇyugrāpadāmiva
verses.translation: Riches, wheels of heaped-up anxieties, give me no joy; houses with wives and children are like homes of terrible calamities.

verses.sanskrit: इयमस्मि स्थितोदारा संसारे परिपेलवा । श्रीर्मुने परिमोहाय सापि नूनं न शर्मदा
verses.transliteration: iyamasmi sthitodārā saṃsāre paripelavā | śrīrmune parimohāya sāpi nūnaṃ na śarmadā
verses.translation: Here I stand, in the world, so fragile; O sage, fortune is for delusion, and surely it too gives no peace.

verses.sanskrit: आयुः पल्लवकोणाग्रलम्बाम्बुकणभङ्गुरम् । उन्मत्त इव संत्यज्य याम्यकाण्डे शरीरकम्
verses.transliteration: āyuḥ pallavakoṇāgralambāmbukaṇabhaṅguram | unmatta iva saṃtyajya yāmyakāṇḍe śarīrakam
verses.translation: Life is as frail as a drop of water hanging on the tip of a sprout; I would abandon this body like a madman, at the hour of death.

verses.sanskrit: विषयाशी विषासङ्गपरिजर्जरचेतसाम् । अप्रौढात्मविवेकानामायुरायासकारणम्
verses.transliteration: viṣayāśī viṣāsaṅgaparijarjaracetasām | aprauḍhātmavivekānāmāyurāyāsakāraṇam
verses.translation: For those who feed on objects, whose minds are worn out by attachment to poison, who lack mature discrimination of the Self, life is a cause of toil.

verses.sanskrit: युज्यते वेष्टनं वायोराकाशस्य च खण्डनम् । ग्रन्थनं च तरङ्गाणामास्था नायुषि युज्यते
verses.transliteration: yujyate veṣṭanaṃ vāyorākāśasya ca khaṇḍanam | granthanaṃ ca taraṅgāṇāmāsthā nāyuṣi yujyate
verses.translation: It is possible to wrap up the wind, to cut the sky, to knot the waves; reliance on life is not possible.

verses.sanskrit: प्राप्यं सम्प्राप्यते येन भूयो येन न शोच्यते । पराया निर्वृतेः स्थानं यत्तज्जीवितमुच्यते
verses.transliteration: prāpyaṃ samprāpyate yena bhūyo yena na śocyate | parāyā nirvṛteḥ sthānaṃ yattajjīvitamucyate
verses.translation: That by which the attainable is attained and one grieves no more, the place of supreme peace — that is called life.

verses.sanskrit: तरवोऽपि हि जीवन्ति जीवन्ति मृगपक्षिणः । स जीवति मनो यस्य मननेनोपजीवति
verses.transliteration: taravo'pi hi jīvanti jīvanti mṛgapakṣiṇaḥ | sa jīvati mano yasya mananenopajīvati
verses.translation: Even trees live, and animals and birds live; but he truly lives whose mind lives by reflection.

verses.sanskrit: जातास्त एव जगति जन्तवः साधुजीविताः । ये पुनर्नेह जायन्ते शेषा जरठगर्दभाः
verses.transliteration: jātāsta eva jagati jantavaḥ sādhujīvitāḥ | ye punarneha jāyante śeṣā jaraṭhagardabhāḥ
verses.translation: Only those creatures in the world have been born who live good lives and are not born here again; the rest are old donkeys.

verses.sanskrit: भारो विवेकिनः शास्त्रं भारो ज्ञानं च रागिणः । अशान्तस्य मनो भारो भारोऽनात्मविदो वपुः
verses.transliteration: bhāro vivekinaḥ śāstraṃ bhāro jñānaṃ ca rāgiṇaḥ | aśāntasya mano bhāro bhāro'nātmavido vapuḥ
verses.translation: For the discriminating, scripture is a burden; for the passionate, knowledge is a burden; for the restless, the mind is a burden; for one who does not know the Self, the body is a burden.

verses.sanskrit: अहंकारवशादापदहंकाराद्दुराधयः । अहंकारवशादीहा नाहंकारात्परो रिपुः
verses.transliteration: ahaṃkāravaśādāpadahaṃkārāddurādhayaḥ | ahaṃkāravaśādīhā nāhaṃkārātparo ripuḥ
verses.translation: Under the sway of egoism come calamities; from egoism, mental anguish; under the sway of egoism comes striving; there is no greater enemy than egoism.

verses.sanskrit: अहंकारवशाद्यद्यन्मया भुक्तं चराचरम् । तत्तत्सर्वमवस्त्वेव वस्त्वहंकाररिक्तता
verses.transliteration: ahaṃkāravaśādyadyanmayā bhuktaṃ carācaram | tattatsarvamavastveva vastvahaṃkārariktatā
verses.translation: Whatever moving or unmoving thing I have enjoyed through egoism, all that is unreal; the real is emptiness of egoism.

verses.sanskrit: इतश्चेतश्च सुव्यग्रं व्यर्थमेवाभिधावति । मनो दूरतरं याति ग्रामे कौलेयको यथा
verses.transliteration: itaścetaśca suvyagraṃ vyarthamevābhidhāvati | mano dūrataraṃ yāti grāme kauleyako yathā
verses.translation: The mind runs here and there, agitated and in vain, going ever farther, like a dog in a village.

verses.sanskrit: क्रूरेण जडतां याता तृष्णाभार्यानुगामिना । वशः कौलेयकेनेव ब्रह्मन्मुक्तोऽस्मि चेतसा
verses.transliteration: krūreṇa jaḍatāṃ yātā tṛṣṇābhāryānugāminā | vaśaḥ kauleyakeneva brahmanmukto'smi cetasā
verses.translation: By cruel craving, my wife, who follows, I was rendered dull, like one ruled by a dog; O Brahmin, I am free in mind.

verses.sanskrit: अप्यब्धिपानान्महतः सुमेरून्मूलनादपि । अपि वह्न्यशनाद्ब्रह्मन्विषमश्चित्तनिग्रहः
verses.transliteration: apyabdhipānānmahataḥ sumerūnmūlanādapi | api vahnyaśanādbrahmanviṣamaścittanigrahaḥ
verses.translation: Even drinking the ocean, uprooting great Sumeru, or eating fire — O Brahmin, more difficult is the restraint of the mind.

verses.sanskrit: चित्तं कारणमर्थानां तस्मिन्सति जगत्त्रयम् । तस्मिन्क्षीणे जगत्क्षीणं तच्चिकित्स्यं प्रयत्नतः
verses.transliteration: cittaṃ kāraṇamarthānāṃ tasminsati jagattrayam | tasminkṣīṇe jagatkṣīṇaṃ taccikitsyaṃ prayatnataḥ
verses.translation: The mind is the cause of things; when it exists the three worlds exist; when it is destroyed the world is destroyed; it must be treated with effort.

verses.sanskrit: यां यामहं मुनिश्रेष्ठ संश्रयामि गुणश्रियम् । तां तां कृन्तति मे तृष्णा तन्त्रीमिव कुमूषिका
verses.transliteration: yāṃ yāmahaṃ muniśreṣṭha saṃśrayāmi guṇaśriyam | tāṃ tāṃ kṛntati me tṛṣṇā tantrīmiva kumūṣikā
verses.translation: Whatever glory of virtue I take refuge in, O best of sages, craving cuts it like a mouse cutting a string.

verses.sanskrit: पदं करोत्यलङ्घ्येऽपि तृप्ता विफलमीहते । चिरं तिष्ठति नैकत्र तृष्णा चपलमर्कटी
verses.transliteration: padaṃ karotyalaṅghye'pi tṛptā viphalamīhate | ciraṃ tiṣṭhati naikatra tṛṣṇā capalamarkaṭī
verses.translation: Satisfied, she makes a nest even on the unscalable; she strives in vain; craving, a restless monkey, does not stay long in one place.

verses.sanskrit: क्षणमायाति पातालं क्षणं याति नभस्थलम् । क्षणं भ्रमति दिक्कुञ्जे तृष्णा हृत्पद्मषट्पदी
verses.transliteration: kṣaṇamāyāti pātālaṃ kṣaṇaṃ yāti nabhasthalam | kṣaṇaṃ bhramati dikkuñje tṛṣṇā hṛtpadmaṣaṭpadī
verses.translation: In a moment she goes to the underworld, in a moment to the sky, in a moment wanders in the thickets of the quarters — craving, the bee in the lotus of the heart.

verses.sanskrit: सर्वसंसारदुःखानां तृष्णैका दीर्घदुःखदा । अन्तःपुरस्थमपि या योजयत्यतिसंकटे
verses.transliteration: sarvasaṃsāraduḥkhānāṃ tṛṣṇaikā dīrghaduḥkhadā | antaḥpurasthamapi yā yojayatyatisaṃkaṭe
verses.translation: Of all the sorrows of the world, craving alone gives long sorrow, who involves even one in the inner palace in the greatest distress.

verses.sanskrit: तृष्णाविषूचिकामन्त्रश्चिन्तात्यागो हि स द्विज । स्तोकेनानन्दमायाति स्तोकेनायाति खेदताम्
verses.transliteration: tṛṣṇāviṣūcikāmantraścintātyāgo hi sa dvija | stokenānandamāyāti stokenāyāti khedatām
verses.translation: The charm against the cholera of craving is the giving up of anxiety, O twice-born; a little brings joy, a little brings weariness.

verses.sanskrit: नास्ति देहसमः शोच्यो नीचो गुणविवर्जितः
verses.transliteration: nāsti dehasamaḥ śocyo nīco guṇavivarjitaḥ
verses.translation: There is none so pitiable as the body, low and devoid of virtues.

verses.sanskrit: कलेवरमहंकारगृहस्थस्य महागृहम् । लुठत्वभ्येतु वा स्थैर्यं किमनेन गुरो मम
verses.transliteration: kalevaramahaṃkāragṛhasthasya mahāgṛham | luṭhatvabhyetu vā sthairyaṃ kimanena guro mama
verses.translation: The body is the great house of the householder egoism; let it tumble or become steady — what is that to me, O teacher?

verses.sanskrit: पङ्क्तिबद्धेन्द्रियपशुं वल्गत्तृष्णागृहाङ्गणम् । चित्तभृत्यजनाकीर्णं नेष्टं देहगृहं मम
verses.transliteration: paṅktibaddhendriyapaśuṃ valgattṛṣṇāgṛhāṅgaṇam | cittabhṛtyajanākīrṇaṃ neṣṭaṃ dehagṛhaṃ mama
verses.translation: The house of the body, with its row of sense-animals, the courtyard where craving prances, crowded with the mind's servants, I do not want.

verses.sanskrit: जिह्वामर्कटिकाक्रान्तवदनद्वारभीषणम् । दृष्टदन्तास्थिशकलं नेष्टं देहगृहं मम
verses.transliteration: jihvāmarkaṭikākrāntavadanadvārabhīṣaṇam | dṛṣṭadantāsthiśakalaṃ neṣṭaṃ dehagṛhaṃ mama
verses.translation: The house of the body, fearful at the door of the mouth seized by the monkey of the tongue, with shards of bones for teeth, I do not want.

verses.sanskrit: रक्तमांसमयस्यास्य सबाह्याभ्यन्तरे मुने । नाशैकधर्मिणो ब्रूहि कैव कायस्य रम्यता
verses.transliteration: raktamāṃsamayasyāsya sabāhyābhyantare mune | nāśaikadharmiṇo brūhi kaiva kāyasya ramyatā
verses.translation: Of this body made of blood and flesh, outside and inside, whose only nature is destruction — tell me, O sage, what charm does it have?

verses.sanskrit: तडित्सु शरदभ्रेषु गन्धर्वनगरेषु च । स्थैर्यं येन विनिर्णीतं स विश्वसितु विग्रहे
verses.transliteration: taḍitsu śaradabhreṣu gandharvanagareṣu ca | sthairyaṃ yena vinirṇītaṃ sa viśvasitu vigrahe
verses.translation: Whoever has determined permanence in lightning, in autumn clouds, and in cities of gandharvas, may put his trust in the body.

verses.sanskrit: शैशवे गुरुतो भीतिर्मातृतः पितृतस्तथा । जनतो ज्येष्ठबालाच्च शैशवं भयमन्दिरम्
verses.transliteration: śaiśave guruto bhītirmātṛtaḥ pitṛtastathā | janato jyeṣṭhabālācca śaiśavaṃ bhayamandiram
verses.translation: In infancy there is fear of the teacher, of the mother and the father, of people, of elder children; infancy is a house of fear.

verses.sanskrit: स्वचित्तबिलसंस्थेन नानाविभ्रमकारिणा । बलात्कामपिशाचेन विवशः परिभूयते
verses.transliteration: svacittabilasaṃsthena nānāvibhramakāriṇā | balātkāmapiśācena vivaśaḥ paribhūyate
verses.translation: The helpless man is overcome by force by the demon of desire, who dwells in the cave of his own mind and makes many delusions.

verses.sanskrit: दासाः पुत्राः स्त्रियश्चैव बान्धवाः सुहृदस्तथा । हसन्त्युन्मत्तकमिव नरं वार्धककम्पितम्
verses.transliteration: dāsāḥ putrāḥ striyaścaiva bāndhavāḥ suhṛdastathā | hasantyunmattakamiva naraṃ vārdhakakampitam
verses.translation: Servants, sons, wives, kinsmen and friends laugh at the old man trembling with age as at a madman.

verses.sanskrit: दैन्यदोषमयी दीर्घा वर्धते वार्धके स्पृहा । सर्वापदामेकसखी हृदि दाहप्रदायिनी
verses.transliteration: dainyadoṣamayī dīrghā vardhate vārdhake spṛhā | sarvāpadāmekasakhī hṛdi dāhapradāyinī
verses.translation: Longing, made of misery and fault, grows long in old age, the one companion of all calamities, giving burning in the heart.

verses.sanskrit: क्वचिद्वा विद्यते यैषा संसारे सुखभावना । आयुः स्तम्बमिवासाद्य कालस्तामपि कृन्तति
verses.transliteration: kvacidvā vidyate yaiṣā saṃsāre sukhabhāvanā | āyuḥ stambamivāsādya kālastāmapi kṛntati
verses.translation: Whatever notion of happiness there is in the world, Time, taking it like a stalk of grain, cuts even that.

verses.sanskrit: तृणं पांसुं महेन्द्रं च सुवर्णं मेरुसर्षपम् । आत्मंभरितया सर्वमात्मसात्कर्तुमुद्यतः । कालोऽयं सर्वसंहारी तेनाक्रान्तं जगत्त्रयम्
verses.transliteration: tṛṇaṃ pāṃsuṃ mahendraṃ ca suvarṇaṃ merusarṣapam | ātmaṃbharitayā sarvamātmasātkartumudyataḥ | kālo'yaṃ sarvasaṃhārī tenākrāntaṃ jagattrayam
verses.translation: Time the destroyer of all, bent on making all its own, being self-filling, seizes straw, dust, great Indra, gold, Meru and mustard seed; by it the three worlds are overcome.

verses.sanskrit: मांसपाञ्चालिकायास्तु यन्त्रलोलेअङ्गपञ्जरे । स्नाय्वस्थिग्रन्थिशालिन्याः स्त्रियः किमिव शोभनम्
verses.transliteration: māṃsapāñcālikāyāstu yantraloleaṅgapañjare | snāyvasthigranthiśālinyāḥ striyaḥ kimiva śobhanam
verses.translation: What is beautiful in a woman, a doll of flesh, a cage of limbs moving by mechanism, full of sinews, bones and joints?

verses.sanskrit: त्वङ्मांसरक्तबाष्पाम्बु पृथक्कृत्वा विलोचने । समालोकय रम्यं चेत्किं मुधा परिमुह्यसि
verses.transliteration: tvaṅmāṃsaraktabāṣpāmbu pṛthakkṛtvā vilocane | samālokaya ramyaṃ cetkiṃ mudhā parimuhyasi
verses.translation: Separate the skin, flesh, blood, tears and water, and look at the eyes; if you then find it lovely, why are you vainly deluded?

verses.sanskrit: मेरुशृङ्गतटोल्लासिगङ्गाचलरयोपमा । दृष्टा यस्मिन्मुने मुक्ताहारस्योल्लासशालिता
verses.transliteration: meruśṛṅgataṭollāsigaṅgācalarayopamā | dṛṣṭā yasminmune muktāhārasyollāsaśālitā
verses.translation: The jewelled necklace, O sage, seen shining on her breast, resembles the rush of the Ganga from the slopes of Meru's peak.

verses.sanskrit: श्मशानेषु दिगन्तेषु स एव ललनास्तनः । श्वभिरास्वाद्यते काले लघुपिण्ड इवान्धसः
verses.transliteration: śmaśāneṣu diganteṣu sa eva lalanāstanaḥ | śvabhirāsvādyate kāle laghupiṇḍa ivāndhasaḥ
verses.translation: That very breast of a woman, in the cremation grounds and at the ends of the quarters, is in time tasted by dogs like a small ball of rice.

verses.sanskrit: केशकज्जलधारिण्यो दुःस्पर्शा लोचनप्रियाः । दुष्कृताग्निशिखा नार्यो दहन्ति तृणवन्नरम्
verses.transliteration: keśakajjaladhāriṇyo duḥsparśā locanapriyāḥ | duṣkṛtāgniśikhā nāryo dahanti tṛṇavannaram
verses.translation: Women with hair like black collyrium, hard to touch, dear to the eye, are flames of the fire of wrong-doing, burning a man like straw.

verses.sanskrit: ज्वलतामतिदूरेऽपि सरसा अपि नीरसाः । स्त्रियो हि नरकाग्नीनामिन्धनं चारु दारुणम्
verses.transliteration: jvalatāmatidūre'pi sarasā api nīrasāḥ | striyo hi narakāgnīnāmindhanaṃ cāru dāruṇam
verses.translation: Even from far away they burn; though juicy they are dry; women are the lovely, terrible fuel of the fires of hell.

verses.sanskrit: कामनाम्ना किरातेन विकीर्णा मुग्धचेतसः । नार्यो नरविहङ्गानामङ्गबन्धनवागुराः
verses.transliteration: kāmanāmnā kirātena vikīrṇā mugdhacetasaḥ | nāryo naravihaṅgānāmaṅgabandhanavāgurāḥ
verses.translation: Women are the nets, scattered by the hunter named Desire, binding the limbs of the birds who are men with deluded minds.

verses.sanskrit: जन्मपल्वलमत्स्यानां चित्तकर्दमचारिणाम् । पुंसां दुर्वासनारज्जुर्नारी बडिशपिण्डिका
verses.transliteration: janmapalvalamatsyānāṃ cittakardamacāriṇām | puṃsāṃ durvāsanārajjurnārī baḍiśapiṇḍikā
verses.translation: For the fish of the pond of birth that move in the mud of the mind, woman is the baited hook on the rope of evil impressions.

verses.sanskrit: सर्वेषां दोषरत्नानां सुसमुद्गिकयानया । दुःखशृङ्खलया नित्यमलमस्तु मम स्त्रिया
verses.transliteration: sarveṣāṃ doṣaratnānāṃ susamudgikayānayā | duḥkhaśṛṅkhalayā nityamalamastu mama striyā
verses.translation: Enough for me of woman, the casket of all jewels of faults, the ever-chain of sorrow.

verses.sanskrit: यस्य स्त्री तस्य भोगेच्छा निःस्त्रीकस्य क्व भोगभूः । स्त्रियं त्यक्त्वा जगत्त्यक्तं जगत्त्यक्त्वा सुखी भवेत्
verses.transliteration: yasya strī tasya bhogecchā niḥstrīkasya kva bhogabhūḥ | striyaṃ tyaktvā jagattyaktaṃ jagattyaktvā sukhī bhavet
verses.translation: He who has a wife has desire for pleasure; for the wifeless, where is the ground of pleasure? Having abandoned woman he has abandoned the world; having abandoned the world he would be happy.

verses.sanskrit: दिशोऽपि न हि दृश्यन्ते देशोऽप्यन्योपदेशकृत् । शैला अपि विशीर्यन्ते शीर्यन्ते तारका अपि
verses.transliteration: diśo'pi na hi dṛśyante deśo'pyanyopadeśakṛt | śailā api viśīryante śīryante tārakā api
verses.translation: Even the directions are not seen; even the region gives other teaching; mountains crumble and stars decay.

verses.sanskrit: शुष्यन्त्यपि समुद्राश्च ध्रुवोऽप्यध्रुवजीवनः । सिद्धा अपि विनश्यन्ति जीर्यन्ते दानवादयः
verses.transliteration: śuṣyantyapi samudrāśca dhruvo'pyadhruvajīvanaḥ | siddhā api vinaśyanti jīryante dānavādayaḥ
verses.translation: Oceans dry up; even the fixed has an unfixed life; even the perfected perish, and demons and others wear out.

verses.sanskrit: परमेष्ठ्यपि निष्ठावान्हीयते हरिरप्यजः । भावोऽप्यभावमायाति जीर्यन्ते वै दिगीश्वराः
verses.transliteration: parameṣṭhyapi niṣṭhāvānhīyate harirapyajaḥ | bhāvo'pyabhāvamāyāti jīryante vai digīśvarāḥ
verses.translation: Even the supreme, the steadfast, declines; Hari and the Unborn too; being goes to non-being; the lords of the quarters decay.

verses.sanskrit: ब्रह्मा विष्णुश्च रुद्रश्च सर्वा वा भूतजातयः । नाशमेवानुधावन्ति सलिलानीव वाडवम्
verses.transliteration: brahmā viṣṇuśca rudraśca sarvā vā bhūtajātayaḥ | nāśamevānudhāvanti salilānīva vāḍavam
verses.translation: Brahma, Vishnu and Rudra, and all classes of beings run only toward destruction, as waters toward the submarine fire.

verses.sanskrit: आपदः क्षणमायान्ति क्षणमायान्ति सम्पदः । क्षणं जन्माथ मरणं सर्वं नश्वरमेव तत्
verses.transliteration: āpadaḥ kṣaṇamāyānti kṣaṇamāyānti sampadaḥ | kṣaṇaṃ janmātha maraṇaṃ sarvaṃ naśvarameva tat
verses.translation: Calamities come in a moment, prosperity comes in a moment; birth and death in a moment — all that is perishable.

verses.sanskrit: अशूरेण हताः शूरा एकेनापि शतं हतम् । विषं विषयवैषम्यं न विषं विषमुच्यते
verses.transliteration: aśūreṇa hatāḥ śūrā ekenāpi śataṃ hatam | viṣaṃ viṣayavaiṣamyaṃ na viṣaṃ viṣamucyate
verses.translation: The brave are slain by the unbrave, a hundred by one; poison is the unevenness of sense-objects, what is called poison is not poison.

verses.sanskrit: जन्मान्तरघ्ना विषया एकजन्महरं विषम् । इति मे दोषदावाग्निदग्धे सम्प्रति चेतसि
verses.transliteration: janmāntaraghnā viṣayā ekajanmaharaṃ viṣam | iti me doṣadāvāgnidagdhe samprati cetasi
verses.translation: Objects destroy across births; poison destroys one birth. Thus now in my mind, burnt by the forest-fire of faults,

verses.sanskrit: स्फुरन्ति हि न भोगाशा मृगतृष्णासरःस्वपि । अतो मां बोधयाशु त्वं तत्त्वज्ञानेन वै गुरो
verses.transliteration: sphuranti hi na bhogāśā mṛgatṛṣṇāsaraḥsvapi | ato māṃ bodhayāśu tvaṃ tattvajñānena vai guro
verses.translation: the hope of pleasures does not stir even in the mirage-lakes. Therefore, O teacher, awaken me quickly with knowledge of truth.

verses.sanskrit: नो चेन्मौनं समास्थाय निर्मानो गतमत्सरः । भावयन्मनसा विष्णुं लिपिकर्मार्पितोपमः
verses.transliteration: no cenmaunaṃ samāsthāya nirmāno gatamatsaraḥ | bhāvayanmanasā viṣṇuṃ lipikarmārpitopamaḥ
verses.translation: Otherwise I shall take to silence, humble, free of envy, contemplating Vishnu in my mind, like a figure painted in a picture.

verses.sanskrit: इति महोपनिषत् ।
verses.transliteration: iti mahopaniṣat |
verses.translation: Thus the Mahopanishad.

verses.sanskrit: निदाघ तव नास्तन्यज्ज्ञेयं ज्ञानवतां वर । प्रज्ञया त्वं विजानासि ईश्वरानुगृहीतया । चित्तमालिन्यसंजातं मार्जयामि भ्रमं मुने
verses.transliteration: nidāgha tava nāstanyajjñeyaṃ jñānavatāṃ vara | prajñayā tvaṃ vijānāsi īśvarānugṛhītayā | cittamālinyasaṃjātaṃ mārjayāmi bhramaṃ mune
verses.translation: Nidagha, there is nothing else to be known by you, best of the knowing; with the wisdom blessed by the Lord you know. I wipe away the delusion born of the mind's impurity, O sage.

verses.sanskrit: मोक्षद्वारे द्वारपालश्चत्वारः परिकीर्तिताः । शमो विचारः सन्तोषश्चतुर्थः साधुसङ्गमः
verses.transliteration: mokṣadvāre dvārapālaścatvāraḥ parikīrtitāḥ | śamo vicāraḥ santoṣaścaturthaḥ sādhusaṅgamaḥ
verses.translation: Four gatekeepers at the door of liberation are proclaimed: peace, inquiry, contentment, and fourth, the company of the good.

verses.sanskrit: एकं वा सर्वयत्नेन सर्वमुत्सृज्य संश्रयेत् । एकस्मिन्वशगे यान्ति चत्वारोऽपि वशं गताः
verses.transliteration: ekaṃ vā sarvayatnena sarvamutsṛjya saṃśrayet | ekasminvaśage yānti catvāro'pi vaśaṃ gatāḥ
verses.translation: Or with all effort, giving up all, one should take refuge in one; when one is mastered, all four come under control.

verses.sanskrit: शास्त्रैः सज्जनसम्पर्कपूर्वकैश्च तपोदमैः । आदौ संसारमुक्त्यर्थं प्रज्ञामेवाभिवर्धयेत्
verses.transliteration: śāstraiḥ sajjanasamparkapūrvakaiśca tapodamaiḥ | ādau saṃsāramuktyarthaṃ prajñāmevābhivardhayet
verses.translation: With scriptures, with association with the good, with austerity and self-control, first for liberation from the world, one should increase wisdom itself.

verses.sanskrit: स्वानुभूतेश्च शास्त्रस्य गुरोश्चेवैकवाक्यता । यस्याभ्यासेन तेनात्म सततं चावलोक्यते
verses.transliteration: svānubhūteśca śāstrasya guroścevaikavākyatā | yasyābhyāsena tenātma satataṃ cāvalokyate
verses.translation: When one's own experience, the scripture and the teacher agree, by practicing which the Self is constantly seen.

verses.sanskrit: संकल्पाशानुसन्धानवर्जनं चेत्प्रतिक्षणम् । करोषि तदचित्तत्वं प्राप्त एवासि पावनम्
verses.transliteration: saṃkalpāśānusandhānavarjanaṃ cetpratikṣaṇam | karoṣi tadacittatvaṃ prāpta evāsi pāvanam
verses.translation: If you give up every moment the pursuit of intentions and hopes, you have attained the purifying state of mindlessness.

verses.sanskrit: चेतसो यदकर्तृत्वं तत्समाधानमीरितम् । तदेव केवलीभावं साशुभा निर्वृतिः परा
verses.transliteration: cetaso yadakartṛtvaṃ tatsamādhānamīritam | tadeva kevalībhāvaṃ sāśubhā nirvṛtiḥ parā
verses.translation: The mind's non-doership is called samadhi; that alone is aloneness, the supreme bliss that is auspicious.

verses.sanskrit: चेतसा सम्परित्यज्य सर्वभावात्मभावनाम् । यथा तिष्ठसि तिष्ठ त्वं मूकान्धबधिरोपमः
verses.transliteration: cetasā samparityajya sarvabhāvātmabhāvanām | yathā tiṣṭhasi tiṣṭha tvaṃ mūkāndhabadhiropamaḥ
verses.translation: Abandoning with the mind all contemplation of things as the Self, remain as you are, like one mute, blind and deaf.

verses.sanskrit: सर्वं प्रशान्तमजमेकमनादिमध्यमाभास्वरं स्वदनमात्रमचैत्यचिह्नम् । सर्वं प्रशान्तमिति शब्दमयी च दृष्टिर्बाधार्थमेव हि मुधैव तदोमितीदम्
verses.transliteration: sarvaṃ praśāntamajamekamanādimadhyamābhāsvaraṃ svadanamātramacaityacihnam | sarvaṃ praśāntamiti śabdamayī ca dṛṣṭirbādhārthameva hi mudhaiva tadomitīdam
verses.translation: All is quiet, unborn, one, without beginning or middle, luminous, mere self-tasting, bearing no mark of the perceived; the view made of the words "all is quiet" is only for refutation, and vain: thus this is Om.

verses.sanskrit: नित्यप्रबुद्धचित्तस्त्वं कुर्वन्वापि जगत्क्रियाम् । आत्मैकत्वं विदित्वा त्वं तिष्ठाक्षुब्धमहाब्धिवत्
verses.transliteration: nityaprabuddhacittastvaṃ kurvanvāpi jagatkriyām | ātmaikatvaṃ viditvā tvaṃ tiṣṭhākṣubdhamahābdhivat
verses.translation: You are ever awake in mind, even while performing the world's actions; knowing the oneness of the Self, remain like an unagitated great ocean.

verses.sanskrit: तत्त्वावबोध एवासौ वासनातृणपावकः । प्रोक्तः समाधिशब्देन नतु तूष्णीमवस्थितिः
verses.transliteration: tattvāvabodha evāsau vāsanātṛṇapāvakaḥ | proktaḥ samādhiśabdena natu tūṣṇīmavasthitiḥ
verses.translation: True knowledge is itself the fire for the straw of impressions; it is called samadhi, not mere silent staying.

verses.sanskrit: निरिच्छे संस्थिते रत्ने यथा लोकः प्रवर्तते । सत्तामात्रे परे तत्त्वे तथैवायं जगद्गणः
verses.transliteration: niricche saṃsthite ratne yathā lokaḥ pravartate | sattāmātre pare tattve tathaivāyaṃ jagadgaṇaḥ
verses.translation: As the world acts when a jewel stands without desire, so does this host of the world in the supreme principle of mere being.

verses.sanskrit: अतश्चात्मनि कर्तृत्वमकर्तृत्वं च वै मुने । निरिच्छत्वादकर्तासौ कर्ता संनिधिमात्रतः
verses.transliteration: ataścātmani kartṛtvamakartṛtvaṃ ca vai mune | niricchatvādakartāsau kartā saṃnidhimātrataḥ
verses.translation: Therefore, O sage, in the Self there is both doership and non-doership; being without desire it is a non-doer, by mere presence a doer.

verses.sanskrit: ते द्वे ब्रह्मणि विन्देति कर्तृताकर्तृते मुने । यत्रैवैष चमत्कारस्तमाश्रित्य स्थिरो भव
verses.transliteration: te dve brahmaṇi vindeti kartṛtākartṛte mune | yatraivaiṣa camatkārastamāśritya sthiro bhava
verses.translation: Know these two, doership and non-doership, in Brahman, O sage; take refuge in that wherein this wonder is, and be steady.

verses.sanskrit: तस्मान्नित्यमकर्ताहमिति भावनयेद्धया । परमामृतनाम्नी सा समतैवावशिष्यते
verses.transliteration: tasmānnityamakartāhamiti bhāvanayeddhayā | paramāmṛtanāmnī sā samataivāvaśiṣyate
verses.translation: Therefore contemplate with intelligence "I am ever a non-doer"; that alone remains, called supreme nectar, evenness itself.

verses.sanskrit: निदाघ शृणु सत्त्वस्था जाता भुवि महागुणाः । ते नित्यमेवाभ्युदिता मुदिताः स्व इवेन्दवः
verses.transliteration: nidāgha śṛṇu sattvasthā jātā bhuvi mahāguṇāḥ | te nityamevābhyuditā muditāḥ sva ivendavaḥ
verses.translation: Listen, Nidagha: those established in sattva, born on earth with great qualities, are ever risen and joyful, like moons of their own.

verses.sanskrit: नापदि ग्लानिमायान्ति निशि हेमाम्बुजं यथा । नेहन्ते प्रकृतादन्यद्रमन्ते शिष्टवर्त्मनि
verses.transliteration: nāpadi glānimāyānti niśi hemāmbujaṃ yathā | nehante prakṛtādanyadramante śiṣṭavartmani
verses.translation: They do not sink in calamity, like a golden lotus in the night; they strive for nothing beyond their nature and delight in the path of the good.

verses.sanskrit: आकृत्यैव विराजन्ते मैत्र्यादिगुणवृत्तिभिः । समाः समरसाः सौम्य सततं साधुवृत्तयः
verses.transliteration: ākṛtyaiva virājante maitryādiguṇavṛttibhiḥ | samāḥ samarasāḥ saumya satataṃ sādhuvṛttayaḥ
verses.translation: They shine by their very form, by conduct of friendliness and other virtues; even, of equal taste, gentle, ever of good conduct.

verses.sanskrit: अब्धिवद्धतमर्याद भवति विशदाशयाः । नियतिं न विमुञ्चन्ति महान्तो भास्करा इव
verses.transliteration: abdhivaddhatamaryāda bhavati viśadāśayāḥ | niyatiṃ na vimuñcanti mahānto bhāskarā iva
verses.translation: Like the ocean, of clear minds, they transgress no limit; the great do not abandon their law, like suns.

verses.sanskrit: कोऽहं कथमिदं चेति संसारमलमाततम् । प्रविचार्यं प्रयत्नेन प्राज्ञेन सहसाधुना
verses.transliteration: ko'haṃ kathamidaṃ ceti saṃsāramalamātatam | pravicāryaṃ prayatnena prājñena sahasādhunā
verses.translation: "Who am I, and how is this?" — the filth of the world spread out is to be examined with effort by the wise together with the good.

verses.sanskrit: नाकर्मसु नियोक्तव्यं नानार्येण सहावसेत् । द्रष्टव्यः सर्वसंहर्ता न मृत्युरवहेलया
verses.transliteration: nākarmasu niyoktavyaṃ nānāryeṇa sahāvaset | draṣṭavyaḥ sarvasaṃhartā na mṛtyuravahelayā
verses.translation: One should not be engaged in evil acts, nor dwell with the ignoble; the destroyer of all is to be seen; death is not to be scorned.

verses.sanskrit: शरीरमस्थिमांसं च त्यक्त्वा रक्ताद्यशोभनम् । भूतमुक्तावलीतन्तुं चिन्मात्रमवलोकयेत्
verses.transliteration: śarīramasthimāṃsaṃ ca tyaktvā raktādyaśobhanam | bhūtamuktāvalītantuṃ cinmātramavalokayet
verses.translation: Giving up the body as bones and flesh and the unlovely blood and the rest, one should see pure consciousness, the thread of the garland of pearls of the elements.

verses.sanskrit: उपादेयानुपतनं हेयैकान्तविसर्जनम् । यदेतन्मनसो रूपं तद्बाह्यं विद्धि नेतरत्
verses.transliteration: upādeyānupatanaṃ heyaikāntavisarjanam | yadetanmanaso rūpaṃ tadbāhyaṃ viddhi netarat
verses.translation: The inclination toward what is to be accepted and the complete dismissal of what is to be given up — know that to be the mind's form, external, and not otherwise.

verses.sanskrit: गुरुशास्त्रोक्तमार्गेण स्वानुभूत्या च चिद्घने । ब्रह्मैवाहमिति ज्ञात्वा वीतशोको भवेन्मुनिः
verses.transliteration: guruśāstroktamārgeṇa svānubhūtyā ca cidghane | brahmaivāhamiti jñātvā vītaśoko bhavenmuniḥ
verses.translation: By the path taught by teacher and scripture and by one's own experience, knowing "I am Brahman" in the mass of consciousness, the sage becomes free of sorrow.

verses.sanskrit: यत्र निशितासिशतपातनमुत्पलताडनवत्सोढव्यमग्निना दाहो हिमसेचनमिवाङ्गारवर्तनं चन्दनचर्चेव निरवधिनाराचविकिरपातो निदाघविनोदनधारागृहशीकरवर्षणमिव स्वशिरच्छेदः सुखनिद्रेव मूकीकरणमाननमुद्रेव बाधिर्यं महानुपचय इवेदं नावहेलनया भवितव्यमेवं दृढवैराग्याद्बोधो भवति ॥ गुरुवाक्यसमुद्भूतस्वानुभूत्यादिशुद्धया । यस्याभ्यासेन तेनात्मा सततं चावलोक्यते
verses.transliteration: yatra niśitāsiśatapātanamutpalatāḍanavatsoḍhavyamagninā dāho himasecanamivāṅgāravartanaṃ candanacarceva niravadhinārācavikirapāto nidāghavinodanadhārāgṛhaśīkaravarṣaṇamiva svaśiracchedaḥ sukhanidreva mūkīkaraṇamānanamudreva bādhiryaṃ mahānupacaya ivedaṃ nāvahelanayā bhavitavyamevaṃ dṛḍhavairāgyādbodho bhavati || guruvākyasamudbhūtasvānubhūtyādiśuddhayā | yasyābhyāsena tenātmā satataṃ cāvalokyate
verses.translation: Where one must endure like the falling of a hundred sharp swords and the striking of lotuses, burning by fire like sprinkling with snow, rolling on coals like smearing with sandalwood, the shower of endless arrows like the sprinkling of a fountain in a summer-house, the cutting off of one's own head like pleasant sleep, dumbness like a seal on the mouth, deafness like great gain — one should not treat this with contempt; thus from firm dispassion arises knowledge. By pure self-experience born of the teacher's words and practice, the Self is constantly seen.

verses.sanskrit: विनष्टदिग्भ्रमस्यापि यथापूर्वं विभाति दिक् । तथा विज्ञानविध्वस्तं जगन्नास्तीति भावय
verses.transliteration: vinaṣṭadigbhramasyāpi yathāpūrvaṃ vibhāti dik | tathā vijñānavidhvastaṃ jagannāstīti bhāvaya
verses.translation: Even for one whose confusion of direction is gone, the direction appears as before; so contemplate that the world, destroyed by knowledge, does not exist.

verses.sanskrit: न धनान्य्पकुर्वन्ति न मित्राणि न बान्धवाः । न कायक्लेशवैधुर्यं न तीर्थायतनाश्रयः । केवलं तन्मनोमात्रमयेनासाद्यते पदम्
verses.transliteration: na dhanānypakurvanti na mitrāṇi na bāndhavāḥ | na kāyakleśavaidhuryaṃ na tīrthāyatanāśrayaḥ | kevalaṃ tanmanomātramayenāsādyate padam
verses.translation: Neither riches nor friends nor kinsmen help; neither the lack of bodily suffering nor reliance on pilgrimage places; the state is attained only by that which is made of the mind alone.

verses.sanskrit: यानि दुःखानि या तृष्णा दुःसहा ये दुराधयः । शान्तचेतःसु तत्सर्वं तमोऽर्केष्विव नश्यति
verses.transliteration: yāni duḥkhāni yā tṛṣṇā duḥsahā ye durādhayaḥ | śāntacetaḥsu tatsarvaṃ tamo'rkeṣviva naśyati
verses.translation: All sorrows, unbearable craving, and anguish vanish in tranquil minds like darkness in the suns.

verses.sanskrit: मातरीव परं यान्ति विषमाणि मृदूनि च । विश्वासमिह भूतानि सर्वाणि शमशालिनि
verses.transliteration: mātarīva paraṃ yānti viṣamāṇi mṛdūni ca | viśvāsamiha bhūtāni sarvāṇi śamaśālini
verses.translation: As toward a mother, all beings here trust the one who has peace, both the rough and the soft.

verses.sanskrit: न रसायनपानेन न लक्ष्म्यालिङ्गितेन च । न तथा सुखमाप्नोति शमेनान्तर्यथा जनः
verses.transliteration: na rasāyanapānena na lakṣmyāliṅgitena ca | na tathā sukhamāpnoti śamenāntaryathā janaḥ
verses.translation: A man attains happiness not by drinking elixirs nor by Lakshmi's embrace as he does by inner peace.

verses.sanskrit: श्रुत्वा स्पृष्ट्वा च भुक्त्वा च दृष्ट्वा ज्ञात्वा शुभाशुभम् । न हृष्यति ग्लायति यः स शान्त
verses.transliteration: śrutvā spṛṣṭvā ca bhuktvā ca dṛṣṭvā jñātvā śubhāśubham | na hṛṣyati glāyati yaḥ sa śānta
verses.translation: He who, having heard, touched, eaten, seen, known good or bad, neither rejoices nor sinks, is tranquil.

verses.sanskrit: तुषारकरबिंबाच्छं मनो यस्य निराकुलम् । मरणोत्सवयुद्धेषु स शान्त
verses.transliteration: tuṣārakarabiṃbācchaṃ mano yasya nirākulam | maraṇotsavayuddheṣu sa śānta
verses.translation: He whose mind, clear like the moon's disc, is unperturbed in death, festivals and battles is tranquil.

verses.sanskrit: तपस्विषु बहुज्ञेषु याजकेषु नृपेषु च । बलवत्सु गुणाढ्येषु शमवानेव राजते
verses.transliteration: tapasviṣu bahujñeṣu yājakeṣu nṛpeṣu ca | balavatsu guṇāḍhyeṣu śamavāneva rājate
verses.translation: Among ascetics, scholars, sacrificers, kings, the strong and the virtuous, only the peaceful shines.

verses.sanskrit: सन्तोषामृतपानेन ये शान्तास्तृप्तिमागताः । आत्मारामा महात्मानस्ते महापदमागताः
verses.transliteration: santoṣāmṛtapānena ye śāntāstṛptimāgatāḥ | ātmārāmā mahātmānaste mahāpadamāgatāḥ
verses.translation: Those tranquil ones who are satisfied with drinking the nectar of contentment, delighting in the Self, great souls, have attained the great state.

verses.sanskrit: अप्राप्तं हि परित्यज्य सम्प्राप्ते समतां गतः । अदृष्टखेदाखेदो यः सन्तुष्ट
verses.transliteration: aprāptaṃ hi parityajya samprāpte samatāṃ gataḥ | adṛṣṭakhedākhedo yaḥ santuṣṭa
verses.translation: He who has abandoned the unattained and is equal in what is attained, who knows neither the pain of the unseen nor lack of pain — he is contented.

verses.sanskrit: नाभिनन्दत्यसम्प्राप्तं प्राप्तं भुङ्क्ते यथेप्सितम् । यः स सौम्यसमाचारः सन्तुष्ट
verses.transliteration: nābhinandatyasamprāptaṃ prāptaṃ bhuṅkte yathepsitam | yaḥ sa saumyasamācāraḥ santuṣṭa
verses.translation: He who does not rejoice at what is not obtained, and enjoys what is obtained as he wishes, of gentle conduct — he is contented.

verses.sanskrit: रमते धीर्यताप्राप्ते साध्वीवाऽन्तःपुराजिरे । सा जीवन्मुक्ततोदेति स्वरूपानन्ददायिनी
verses.transliteration: ramate dhīryatāprāpte sādhvīvā'ntaḥpurājire | sā jīvanmuktatodeti svarūpānandadāyinī
verses.translation: The wise one delights in what is attained, like a faithful wife in the inner courtyard; that state of liberation-while-living arises, giving the bliss of one's own nature.

verses.sanskrit: यथाक्षणं यथाशास्त्रं यथादेशं यथासुखम् । यथासंभवसत्सङ्गमिमं मोक्षपथक्रमम् । तावद्विचारयेत्प्राज्ञो यावद्विश्रान्तिमात्मनि
verses.transliteration: yathākṣaṇaṃ yathāśāstraṃ yathādeśaṃ yathāsukham | yathāsaṃbhavasatsaṅgamimaṃ mokṣapathakramam | tāvadvicārayetprājño yāvadviśrāntimātmani
verses.translation: According to the moment, the scripture, the place, the comfort, as company of the good is possible — this order of the path of liberation, the wise should consider until rest is found in the Self.

verses.sanskrit: तुर्यविश्रान्तियुक्तस्य निवृत्तस्य भवार्णवात् । जीवतोऽजीवतश्चैव गृहस्थस्याथवा यतेः
verses.transliteration: turyaviśrāntiyuktasya nivṛttasya bhavārṇavāt | jīvato'jīvataścaiva gṛhasthasyāthavā yateḥ
verses.translation: For one endowed with rest in the Fourth, turned back from the ocean of becoming, living or not living, householder or ascetic;

verses.sanskrit: नाकृतेन कृतेनार्थो न श्रुतिस्मृतिविभ्रमैः । निर्मन्दर इवाम्बोधिः स तिष्ठति यथास्थितः
verses.transliteration: nākṛtena kṛtenārtho na śrutismṛtivibhramaiḥ | nirmandara ivāmbodhiḥ sa tiṣṭhati yathāsthitaḥ
verses.translation: there is no purpose in what is done or not done, nor in confusion of scripture and tradition; like an ocean without a churning-rod, he stays as he is.

verses.sanskrit: सर्वात्मवेदनं शुद्धं यदोदेति तवात्मकम् । भाति प्रसृतिदिक्कालबाह्यं चिद्रूपदेहकम्
verses.transliteration: sarvātmavedanaṃ śuddhaṃ yadodeti tavātmakam | bhāti prasṛtidikkālabāhyaṃ cidrūpadehakam
verses.translation: When the pure knowledge of the Self as all arises, your own self shines, outside of space and time, of the form of consciousness, as the body.

verses.sanskrit: एवमात्मा यथा यत्र समुल्लासमुपागतः । तिष्ठत्याशु तथा तत्र तद्रूपश्च विराजते
verses.transliteration: evamātmā yathā yatra samullāsamupāgataḥ | tiṣṭhatyāśu tathā tatra tadrūpaśca virājate
verses.translation: Thus the Self, as it manifests wherever, stays there swiftly and shines in that very form.

verses.sanskrit: यदिदं दृश्यते सर्वं जगत्स्थावरजङ्गमम् । तत्सुषुप्ताविव स्वप्नः कल्पान्ते प्रविनश्यति
verses.transliteration: yadidaṃ dṛśyate sarvaṃ jagatsthāvarajaṅgamam | tatsuṣuptāviva svapnaḥ kalpānte pravinaśyati
verses.translation: All this world that is seen, moving and unmoving, perishes at the end of the cosmic age like a dream in deep sleep.

verses.sanskrit: ऋतमात्मा परंब्रह्म सत्यमित्यादिका बुधैः । कल्पिता व्यवहारार्थं यस्य संज्ञा महात्मनः
verses.transliteration: ṛtamātmā paraṃbrahma satyamityādikā budhaiḥ | kalpitā vyavahārārthaṃ yasya saṃjñā mahātmanaḥ
verses.translation: "Truth," "Self," "Supreme Brahman," "Reality" and the like are names imagined by the wise for the sake of usage for that great one.

verses.sanskrit: यथा कटकशब्दार्थः पृथग्भावो न काञ्चनात् । न हेमकटकात्तद्वज्जगच्छब्दार्थता परा
verses.transliteration: yathā kaṭakaśabdārthaḥ pṛthagbhāvo na kāñcanāt | na hemakaṭakāttadvajjagacchabdārthatā parā
verses.translation: As the meaning of the word "bracelet" is not apart from gold, so the meaning of the word "world" is not apart from the supreme.

verses.sanskrit: तेनेयमिन्द्रजालश्रीर्जगति प्रवितन्यते । द्रष्टुदृश्यस्य सत्तान्तर्बन्ध इत्यभिधीयते
verses.transliteration: teneyamindrajālaśrīrjagati pravitanyate | draṣṭudṛśyasya sattāntarbandha ityabhidhīyate
verses.translation: By that, this splendor of magic is spread in the world; the bondage is said to be the existence of the seer within the seen.

verses.sanskrit: द्रष्टा दृश्यवशाद्बद्धो दृश्याभावे विमुच्यते । जगत्त्वमहमित्यादिसर्गात्मा दृश्यमुच्यते
verses.transliteration: draṣṭā dṛśyavaśādbaddho dṛśyābhāve vimucyate | jagattvamahamityādisargātmā dṛśyamucyate
verses.translation: The seer is bound by the seen and is freed when the seen is absent; the seen is said to be creation itself in the form "world," "I" and the like.

verses.sanskrit: मनसैवेन्द्रजालश्रीर्जगति प्रवितन्यते । यावदेतत्संभवति तावन्मोक्षो न विद्यते
verses.transliteration: manasaivendrajālaśrīrjagati pravitanyate | yāvadetatsaṃbhavati tāvanmokṣo na vidyate
verses.translation: By the mind alone the splendor of magic is spread in the world; as long as this arises, there is no liberation.

verses.sanskrit: ब्रह्मणा तन्यते विश्वं मनसैव स्वयंभुवा । मनोमयमतो विश्वं यन्नाम परिदृश्यते
verses.transliteration: brahmaṇā tanyate viśvaṃ manasaiva svayaṃbhuvā | manomayamato viśvaṃ yannāma paridṛśyate
verses.translation: The universe is spread by Brahma, the self-born, by the mind alone; therefore the universe that is seen is made of mind.

verses.sanskrit: न बाह्ये नापि हृदये सद्रूपं विद्यते मनः । यदर्थं प्रतिभानं तन्मन इत्यभिधीयते
verses.transliteration: na bāhye nāpi hṛdaye sadrūpaṃ vidyate manaḥ | yadarthaṃ pratibhānaṃ tanmana ityabhidhīyate
verses.translation: The mind has no real form either outside or in the heart; that by which an object appears is called mind.

verses.sanskrit: संकल्पनं मनो विद्धि संकल्पस्तन्न विद्यते । यत्र संकल्पनं तत्र मनोऽस्तीत्यवगम्यताम्
verses.transliteration: saṃkalpanaṃ mano viddhi saṃkalpastanna vidyate | yatra saṃkalpanaṃ tatra mano'stītyavagamyatām
verses.translation: Know the mind to be intention; the intention does not exist apart; wherever there is intention, understand that there is mind.

verses.sanskrit: संकल्पमनसी भिन्ने न कदाचन केनचित् । संकल्पजाते गलिते स्वरूपमवशिष्यते
verses.transliteration: saṃkalpamanasī bhinne na kadācana kenacit | saṃkalpajāte galite svarūpamavaśiṣyate
verses.translation: Intention and mind are never different for anyone; when what is born of intention dissolves, one's own nature remains.

verses.sanskrit: अहं त्वं जगतित्यादौ प्रशान्ते दृश्यसंभ्रमे । स्यात्तादृशी केवलता दृश्ये सत्तामुपागते
verses.transliteration: ahaṃ tvaṃ jagatityādau praśānte dṛśyasaṃbhrame | syāttādṛśī kevalatā dṛśye sattāmupāgate
verses.translation: When the confusion of the seen in the form "I," "you," "world" and the like is quieted, there will be such aloneness when the seen reaches its being.

verses.sanskrit: महाप्रलयसम्पत्तौ ह्यसत्तां समुपागते । अशेषदृश्ये सर्गादौ शान्तमेवावशिष्यते
verses.transliteration: mahāpralayasampattau hyasattāṃ samupāgate | aśeṣadṛśye sargādau śāntamevāvaśiṣyate
verses.translation: At the great dissolution, when all the seen reaches non-being, at the beginning of creation only the quiet remains.

verses.sanskrit: अस्त्यनस्तमितो भास्वानजो देवो निरामयः । सर्वदा सर्वकृत्सर्वः परमात्मेत्युदाहृतः
verses.transliteration: astyanastamito bhāsvānajo devo nirāmayaḥ | sarvadā sarvakṛtsarvaḥ paramātmetyudāhṛtaḥ
verses.translation: There is a luminous, unsetting, unborn, faultless god, ever the maker of all, all — declared the Supreme Self.

verses.sanskrit: यतो वाचो निवर्तन्ते यो मुक्तैरवगम्यते । यस्य चात्मादिकाः संज्ञाः कल्पिता न स्वभावतः
verses.transliteration: yato vāco nivartante yo muktairavagamyate | yasya cātmādikāḥ saṃjñāḥ kalpitā na svabhāvataḥ
verses.translation: From where words turn back, who is known by the liberated, whose names like "Self" are imagined and not natural.

verses.sanskrit: चित्ताकाशं चिदाकाशमाकाशं च तृतीयकम् । द्वाभ्यां शून्यतरं विद्धि चिदाकाशं महामुने
verses.transliteration: cittākāśaṃ cidākāśamākāśaṃ ca tṛtīyakam | dvābhyāṃ śūnyataraṃ viddhi cidākāśaṃ mahāmune
verses.translation: Mind-space, consciousness-space, and space as the third; know the consciousness-space, great sage, to be emptier than the other two.

verses.sanskrit: देशाद्देशान्तरप्राप्तौ संविदो मध्यमेव यत् । निमेषेण चिदाकाशं तद्विद्धि मुनिपुङ्गव
verses.transliteration: deśāddeśāntaraprāptau saṃvido madhyameva yat | nimeṣeṇa cidākāśaṃ tadviddhi munipuṅgava
verses.translation: When consciousness passes from place to place, the interval between is, in a moment, the consciousness-space; know that, best of sages.

verses.sanskrit: तस्मिन्निरस्तनिःशेषसंकल्पस्थितिमेषि चेत् । सर्वात्मकं पदं शान्तं तदा प्राप्नोष्यसंशयः
verses.transliteration: tasminnirastaniḥśeṣasaṃkalpasthitimeṣi cet | sarvātmakaṃ padaṃ śāntaṃ tadā prāpnoṣyasaṃśayaḥ
verses.translation: If you attain in it the state of all intentions cast away, then without doubt you will reach the quiet state that is the Self of all.

verses.sanskrit: उदितौदार्यसौन्दर्यवैराग्यरसगर्भिणी । आनन्दस्यन्दिनी यैषा समाधिरभिधीयते
verses.transliteration: uditaudāryasaundaryavairāgyarasagarbhiṇī | ānandasyandinī yaiṣā samādhirabhidhīyate
verses.translation: That which is pregnant with the rise of the flavor of nobility, beauty and dispassion, and streams bliss, is called samadhi.

verses.sanskrit: दृश्यासंभवबोधेन रागद्वेषादितानवे । रतिर्बलोदिता यासौ समाधिरभिधीयते
verses.transliteration: dṛśyāsaṃbhavabodhena rāgadveṣāditānave | ratirbaloditā yāsau samādhirabhidhīyate
verses.translation: The delight that arises forcibly when attachment, hatred and the like are thinned by the knowledge of the impossibility of the seen is called samadhi.

verses.sanskrit: दृश्यासंभवबोधो हि ज्ञानं ज्ञेयं चिदात्मकम् । तदेव केवलीभावं ततोऽन्यत्सकलं मृषा
verses.transliteration: dṛśyāsaṃbhavabodho hi jñānaṃ jñeyaṃ cidātmakam | tadeva kevalībhāvaṃ tato'nyatsakalaṃ mṛṣā
