verses.translation: The knowledge of the impossibility of the seen is knowledge itself, the known being of the nature of consciousness; that alone is aloneness; everything else is false.

verses.sanskrit: मत्त ऐरावतो बद्धः सर्षपीकोणकोटरे । मशकेन कृतं युद्धं सिंहौघैरेणुकोटरे
verses.transliteration: matta airāvato baddhaḥ sarṣapīkoṇakoṭare | maśakena kṛtaṃ yuddhaṃ siṃhaughaireṇukoṭare
verses.translation: A mad Airavata is tied in the hollow of a mustard seed; a mosquito wages war with herds of lions in a pollen grain.

verses.sanskrit: पद्माक्षे स्थापितो मेरुर्निगीर्णो भृङ्गसूनुना । निदाघ विद्धि तादृक्त्वं जगतेतद्भ्रमात्मकम्
verses.transliteration: padmākṣe sthāpito merurnigīrṇo bhṛṅgasūnunā | nidāgha viddhi tādṛktvaṃ jagatetadbhramātmakam
verses.translation: Meru is placed in the eye of a lotus and swallowed by a bee's child; Nidagha, know the world to be of such a nature, deluded.

verses.sanskrit: चित्तमेव हि संसारो रोगादिक्लेशदूषितम् । तदेव तैर्विनिर्मुक्तं भवान्त
verses.transliteration: cittameva hi saṃsāro rogādikleśadūṣitam | tadeva tairvinirmuktaṃ bhavānta
verses.translation: The mind alone is the world, defiled by disease and other afflictions; that same mind, freed from them, is the end of becoming.

verses.sanskrit: मनसा भाव्यमानो हि देहतां याति देहकः । देहवासनया मुक्तो देहधर्मैर्न लिप्यते
verses.transliteration: manasā bhāvyamāno hi dehatāṃ yāti dehakaḥ | dehavāsanayā mukto dehadharmairna lipyate
verses.translation: The embodied one, being contemplated by the mind, takes on a body; freed from the impression of body, he is not tainted by the body's properties.

verses.sanskrit: कल्पं क्षणीकरोत्यन्तः क्षणं नयति कल्पताम् । मनोविलाससंसार इति मे निश्चिता मतिः
verses.transliteration: kalpaṃ kṣaṇīkarotyantaḥ kṣaṇaṃ nayati kalpatām | manovilāsasaṃsāra iti me niścitā matiḥ
verses.translation: Within, one turns an age into a moment and brings a moment to an age; "the world is the play of the mind" — this is my settled conviction.

verses.sanskrit: नाविरतो दुश्चरितान्नाशान्तो नासमाहितः । नाशान्तमनसो वापि प्रज्ञानेनैनमाप्नुयात्
verses.transliteration: nāvirato duścaritānnāśānto nāsamāhitaḥ | nāśāntamanaso vāpi prajñānenainamāpnuyāt
verses.translation: One who has not turned away from wrongdoing, who is not peaceful, not concentrated, nor of unpeaceful mind, cannot attain this even by knowledge.

verses.sanskrit: तद्ब्रह्मानन्दमद्वन्द्वं निर्गुणं सत्यचिद्घनम् । विदित्वा स्वात्मनो रूपं न बिभेति कदाचन
verses.transliteration: tadbrahmānandamadvandvaṃ nirguṇaṃ satyacidghanam | viditvā svātmano rūpaṃ na bibheti kadācana
verses.translation: Having known that Brahman-bliss, without duality, without qualities, true mass of consciousness, as the form of one's own self, one never fears.

verses.sanskrit: परात्परं यन्महतो महान्तं स्वरूपतेजोमयशाश्वतं शिवम् । कविं पुराणं पुरुषं सनातनं सर्वेश्वरं सर्वदेवैरुपास्यम्
verses.transliteration: parātparaṃ yanmahato mahāntaṃ svarūpatejomayaśāśvataṃ śivam | kaviṃ purāṇaṃ puruṣaṃ sanātanaṃ sarveśvaraṃ sarvadevairupāsyam
verses.translation: The highest of the high, the greatest of the great, eternal and auspicious, made of the radiance of his own nature, the ancient seer, the eternal Person, Lord of all, worshipped by all gods.

verses.sanskrit: अहं ब्रह्मेति नियतं मोक्षहेतुर्महात्मनाम् । द्वे पदे बन्धमोक्षाय निर्ममेति ममेति च । ममेति बध्यते जन्तुर्निर्ममेति विमुच्यते
verses.transliteration: ahaṃ brahmeti niyataṃ mokṣaheturmahātmanām | dve pade bandhamokṣāya nirmameti mameti ca | mameti badhyate janturnirmameti vimucyate
verses.translation: "I am Brahman" is the sure cause of liberation for the great-souled. Two words serve for bondage and liberation: "not mine" and "mine." By "mine" a creature is bound; by "not mine" he is freed.

verses.sanskrit: जीवेश्वरादिरूपेण चेतनाचेतनात्मकम् । ईक्षणादिप्रवेशान्ता सृष्टिरीशेन कल्पिता । जाग्रदादिविमोक्षान्तः संसारो जीवकल्पितः
verses.transliteration: jīveśvarādirūpeṇa cetanācetanātmakam | īkṣaṇādipraveśāntā sṛṣṭirīśena kalpitā | jāgradādivimokṣāntaḥ saṃsāro jīvakalpitaḥ
verses.translation: In the forms of individual and Lord, sentient and insentient — creation, from seeing to entering, is imagined by the Lord; the world, from waking to liberation, is imagined by the individual.

verses.sanskrit: त्रिणाचिकादियोगान्ता ईश्वरभ्रान्तिमाश्रिताः । लोकायतादिसांख्यान्ता जीवविभ्रान्तिमाश्रिताः
verses.transliteration: triṇācikādiyogāntā īśvarabhrāntimāśritāḥ | lokāyatādisāṃkhyāntā jīvavibhrāntimāśritāḥ
verses.translation: Those from Trinaciketa to the Yoga schools rely on the illusion of the Lord; those from Lokayata to Samkhya rely on the illusion of the individual.

verses.sanskrit: तस्मान्मुमुक्षिभिर्नैव मतिर्जीवेशवादयोः । कार्या किंतु ब्रह्मतत्त्वं निश्चलेन विचार्यताम्
verses.transliteration: tasmānmumukṣibhirnaiva matirjīveśavādayoḥ | kāryā kiṃtu brahmatattvaṃ niścalena vicāryatām
verses.translation: Therefore seekers of liberation should not fix their mind on theories of individual and Lord; rather the truth of Brahman should be inquired into steadily.

verses.sanskrit: अविशेषेण सर्वं तु यः पश्यति चिदन्वयात् । स एव साक्षाद्विज्ञानी स शिवः स हरिर्विधिः
verses.transliteration: aviśeṣeṇa sarvaṃ tu yaḥ paśyati cidanvayāt | sa eva sākṣādvijñānī sa śivaḥ sa harirvidhiḥ
verses.translation: He who sees all without distinction through the connection with consciousness is truly the knower; he is Shiva, he is Hari, he is Brahma.

verses.sanskrit: दुर्लभो विषयत्यागो दुर्लभं तत्त्वदर्शनम् । दुर्लभा सहजावस्था सद्गुरोः करुणां विना
verses.transliteration: durlabho viṣayatyāgo durlabhaṃ tattvadarśanam | durlabhā sahajāvasthā sadguroḥ karuṇāṃ vinā
verses.translation: Giving up of objects is hard to obtain; vision of truth is hard to obtain; the natural state is hard to obtain without the grace of a true teacher.

verses.sanskrit: उत्पन्नशक्तिर्बोधस्य त्यक्तनिःशेषकर्मणः । योगिनः सहजावस्था स्वयमेवोपजायते
verses.transliteration: utpannaśaktirbodhasya tyaktaniḥśeṣakarmaṇaḥ | yoginaḥ sahajāvasthā svayamevopajāyate
verses.translation: For the yogi in whom the power of knowledge has risen and who has given up all actions, the natural state arises of itself.

verses.sanskrit: यदा ह्येवैष एतस्मिन्नल्पमप्यन्तरं नरः । विजानाति तदा तस्य भयं स्यान्नत्र संशयः
verses.transliteration: yadā hyevaiṣa etasminnalpamapyantaraṃ naraḥ | vijānāti tadā tasya bhayaṃ syānnatra saṃśayaḥ
verses.translation: When a man perceives even a slight difference between this and himself, then fear arises for him; there is no doubt.

verses.sanskrit: सर्वगं सच्चिदानन्दं ज्ञानचक्षुर्निरीक्षते । अज्ञानचक्षुर्नेक्षेत भास्वन्तं भानुमन्दह्वत्
verses.transliteration: sarvagaṃ saccidānandaṃ jñānacakṣurnirīkṣate | ajñānacakṣurnekṣeta bhāsvantaṃ bhānumandahvat
verses.translation: The eye of knowledge beholds the all-pervading being-consciousness-bliss; the eye of ignorance does not see the shining sun, like the blind.

verses.sanskrit: प्रज्ञानमेव तद्ब्रह्म सत्यप्रज्ञानलक्षणम् । एवं ब्रह्मपरिज्ञानादेव मर्त्याऽमृतो भवेत्
verses.transliteration: prajñānameva tadbrahma satyaprajñānalakṣaṇam | evaṃ brahmaparijñānādeva martyā'mṛto bhavet
verses.translation: Consciousness alone is that Brahman, having the mark of true consciousness; thus by knowing Brahman alone a mortal becomes immortal.

verses.sanskrit: भिद्यते हृदयग्रन्थिश्छिद्यन्ते सर्वसंशयाः । क्षीयन्ते चास्य कर्माणि तस्मिन्दृष्टे परावरे
verses.transliteration: bhidyate hṛdayagranthiśchidyante sarvasaṃśayāḥ | kṣīyante cāsya karmāṇi tasmindṛṣṭe parāvare
verses.translation: The knot of the heart is cut, all doubts are severed, and his actions are exhausted, when that Highest and Lowest is seen.

verses.sanskrit: अनात्मतां परित्यज्य निर्विकारौ जगत्स्थितौ । एकनिष्ठतयान्तस्थः संविन्मात्रपरो भव
verses.transliteration: anātmatāṃ parityajya nirvikārau jagatsthitau | ekaniṣṭhatayāntasthaḥ saṃvinmātraparo bhava
verses.translation: Abandoning the notion of non-Self, being unaffected in the world's stay, remain within in one-pointedness, devoted to pure awareness alone.

verses.sanskrit: मरुभूमौ जलं सर्वं मरुभूमात्रमेव तत् । जगत्त्रयमिदं सर्वं चिन्मात्रं स्वविचारतः
verses.transliteration: marubhūmau jalaṃ sarvaṃ marubhūmātrameva tat | jagattrayamidaṃ sarvaṃ cinmātraṃ svavicārataḥ
verses.translation: In the desert the water is all just desert; likewise these three worlds are all pure consciousness by one's own inquiry.

verses.sanskrit: लक्ष्यालक्ष्यमतिं त्यक्त्वा यस्तिष्ठेत्केवलात्मना । शिव एव स्वयं साक्षादयं ब्रह्मविदुत्तमः
verses.transliteration: lakṣyālakṣyamatiṃ tyaktvā yastiṣṭhetkevalātmanā | śiva eva svayaṃ sākṣādayaṃ brahmaviduttamaḥ
verses.translation: He who abandons the notion of the indicated and the unindicated and stays as the Self alone is Shiva himself, the best of the knowers of Brahman.

verses.sanskrit: अधिष्ठानमनौपम्यमवाङ्मनसगोचरम् । नित्यं विभुं सर्वगतं सुसूक्ष्मं च तदव्ययम्
verses.transliteration: adhiṣṭhānamanaupamyamavāṅmanasagocaram | nityaṃ vibhuṃ sarvagataṃ susūkṣmaṃ ca tadavyayam
verses.translation: The substratum, without comparison, beyond speech and mind, eternal, all-pervading, omnipresent, very subtle, imperishable.

verses.sanskrit: सर्वशक्तेर्महेशस्य विलासो हि मनो जगत् । संयमासंयमाभ्यां च संसारं शान्तिमन्वगात्
verses.transliteration: sarvaśaktermaheśasya vilāso hi mano jagat | saṃyamāsaṃyamābhyāṃ ca saṃsāraṃ śāntimanvagāt
verses.translation: The mind and the world are the play of the Great Lord who has all power; by restraint and non-restraint the world goes to peace.

verses.sanskrit: मनोव्याधेश्चिकित्सार्थमुपायं कथयामि ते । यद्यत्स्वाभिमतं वस्तु तत्त्यजन्मोक्षमश्नुते
verses.transliteration: manovyādheścikitsārthamupāyaṃ kathayāmi te | yadyatsvābhimataṃ vastu tattyajanmokṣamaśnute
verses.translation: For the cure of the mind's disease I tell you the means: giving up whatever object is dear to oneself, one attains liberation.

verses.sanskrit: स्वायत्तमेकान्तहितं स्वेप्सितत्यागवेदनम् । यस्य दुष्करतां यातं धिक्तं पुरुषकीटकम्
verses.transliteration: svāyattamekāntahitaṃ svepsitatyāgavedanam | yasya duṣkaratāṃ yātaṃ dhiktaṃ puruṣakīṭakam
verses.translation: Fie on that worm of a man for whom it is difficult — what lies in his own power, alone beneficial, the knowledge of giving up one's wishes.

verses.sanskrit: स्वपौरुषेकसाध्येन स्वेप्सितत्यागरूपिणा । मनःप्रशममात्रेण विना नास्ति शुभा गतिः
verses.transliteration: svapauruṣekasādhyena svepsitatyāgarūpiṇā | manaḥpraśamamātreṇa vinā nāsti śubhā gatiḥ
verses.translation: Without the mere quieting of the mind, accomplishable by one's own effort alone, in the form of giving up one's wishes, there is no auspicious goal.

verses.sanskrit: असंकल्पनशस्त्रेण छिन्नं चित्तमिदं यदा । सर्वं सर्वगतं शान्तं ब्रह्म सम्पद्यते तदा
verses.transliteration: asaṃkalpanaśastreṇa chinnaṃ cittamidaṃ yadā | sarvaṃ sarvagataṃ śāntaṃ brahma sampadyate tadā
verses.translation: When this mind is cut by the sword of non-intention, then everything becomes all-pervading, quiet Brahman.

verses.sanskrit: भव भावनया मुक्तो मुक्तः परमया धिया । धारयात्मानमव्यग्रो ग्रस्तचित्तं चितः पदम्
verses.transliteration: bhava bhāvanayā mukto muktaḥ paramayā dhiyā | dhārayātmānamavyagro grastacittaṃ citaḥ padam
verses.translation: Be free by contemplation, free by supreme intellect; hold the Self unagitated; the mind that is swallowed is the state of consciousness.

verses.sanskrit: परं पौरुषमाश्रित्य नीत्वा चित्तमचित्तताम् । ध्यानतो हृदयाकाशे चिति चिच्चक्रधारया
verses.transliteration: paraṃ pauruṣamāśritya nītvā cittamacittatām | dhyānato hṛdayākāśe citi ciccakradhārayā
verses.translation: Relying on supreme effort, bringing the mind to mindlessness, by meditation in the heart-space, in consciousness, with the stream of the wheel of consciousness.

verses.sanskrit: मनो मारय निःशङ्कं त्वां प्रबध्नन्ति नारयः
verses.transliteration: mano māraya niḥśaṅkaṃ tvāṃ prabadhnanti nārayaḥ
verses.translation: Kill the mind without fear; enemies do not bind you.

verses.sanskrit: अयं सोऽहमिदं तन्म एतावन्मात्रकं मनः । तदभावनमात्रेण दात्रेणेव विलीयते
verses.transliteration: ayaṃ so'hamidaṃ tanma etāvanmātrakaṃ manaḥ | tadabhāvanamātreṇa dātreṇeva vilīyate
verses.translation: "This I am, this is that of mine" — the mind is merely this much; by merely not contemplating it, it dissolves as by a sickle.

verses.sanskrit: छिन्नाभ्रमण्डलं व्योम्नि यथा शरदि धूयते । वातेन कल्पकेनैव तथान्तर्धूयते मनः
verses.transliteration: chinnābhramaṇḍalaṃ vyomni yathā śaradi dhūyate | vātena kalpakenaiva tathāntardhūyate manaḥ
verses.translation: As a mass of scattered clouds is blown away in autumn in the sky, so the mind is blown away within by the wind of the cosmic age.

verses.sanskrit: कल्पान्तपवना वान्तु यान्तु चैकत्वमर्णवाः । तपन्तु द्वादशादित्या नास्ति निर्मनसः क्षतिः
verses.transliteration: kalpāntapavanā vāntu yāntu caikatvamarṇavāḥ | tapantu dvādaśādityā nāsti nirmanasaḥ kṣatiḥ
verses.translation: Let the winds of the end of the age blow, let the oceans become one, let the twelve suns burn; for the mindless there is no harm.

verses.sanskrit: असंकल्पनमात्रैकसाध्ये सकलसिद्धिदे । असंकल्पातिसाम्राज्ये तिष्ठवष्टब्धतत्पदः
verses.transliteration: asaṃkalpanamātraikasādhye sakalasiddhide | asaṃkalpātisāmrājye tiṣṭhavaṣṭabdhatatpadaḥ
verses.translation: In the empire of non-intention, attainable by non-intention alone, which gives all accomplishments, stay firm in that state.

verses.sanskrit: न हि चञ्चलताहीनं मनः क्वचन दृश्यते । चञ्चलत्वं मनोधर्मो वह्नेर्धर्मो यथोष्णता
verses.transliteration: na hi cañcalatāhīnaṃ manaḥ kvacana dṛśyate | cañcalatvaṃ manodharmo vahnerdharmo yathoṣṇatā
verses.translation: A mind without restlessness is not seen anywhere; restlessness is the mind's property, as heat is of fire.

verses.sanskrit: एषा हि चञ्चलास्पन्दशक्तिश्चित्तत्वसंस्थिता । तां विद्धि मानसीं शक्तिं जगदाडंबरात्मिकाम्
verses.transliteration: eṣā hi cañcalāspandaśaktiścittatvasaṃsthitā | tāṃ viddhi mānasīṃ śaktiṃ jagadāḍaṃbarātmikām
verses.translation: This restless power of vibration is established in the nature of mind; know it as the mental power, of the nature of the world's pageant.

verses.sanskrit: यत्तु चञ्चलताहीनं तन्मनोऽमृतमुच्यते । तदेव च तपः शास्त्रसिद्धान्ते मोक्ष उच्यते
verses.transliteration: yattu cañcalatāhīnaṃ tanmano'mṛtamucyate | tadeva ca tapaḥ śāstrasiddhānte mokṣa ucyate
verses.translation: That which is without restlessness is called the mind's immortality; that alone in the conclusion of the scriptures is called austerity and liberation.

verses.sanskrit: तस्य चञ्चलता यैषा त्वविद्या वासनात्मिका । वासनापरनाम्नीं तां विचारेण विनाशय
verses.transliteration: tasya cañcalatā yaiṣā tvavidyā vāsanātmikā | vāsanāparanāmnīṃ tāṃ vicāreṇa vināśaya
verses.translation: Its restlessness is this ignorance of the nature of impressions; destroy it by inquiry, called by the other name of impression.

verses.sanskrit: पौरुषेण प्रयत्नेन यस्मिन्नैव पदे मनः । योज्यते तत्पदं प्राप्य निर्विकल्पो भवानघ
verses.transliteration: pauruṣeṇa prayatnena yasminnaiva pade manaḥ | yojyate tatpadaṃ prāpya nirvikalpo bhavānagha
verses.translation: By human effort and endeavor, whatever state the mind is joined to, having reached that state, be free of conceptions, O sinless one.

verses.sanskrit: अतः पौरुषमाश्रित्य चित्तमाक्रम्य चेतसा । विशोकं पदमालम्ब्य निरातङ्कः स्थिरो भव
verses.transliteration: ataḥ pauruṣamāśritya cittamākramya cetasā | viśokaṃ padamālambya nirātaṅkaḥ sthiro bhava
verses.translation: Therefore relying on effort, overcoming the mind with mind, taking hold of the sorrowless state, be fearless and steady.

verses.sanskrit: मन एव समर्थं हि मनसो दृढनिग्रहे । अराजकः समर्थः स्याद्राज्ञो निग्रहकर्मणि
verses.transliteration: mana eva samarthaṃ hi manaso dṛḍhanigrahe | arājakaḥ samarthaḥ syādrājño nigrahakarmaṇi
verses.translation: Only the mind is able in firmly restraining the mind, as without a king one is powerless in the work of restraining a king.

verses.sanskrit: तृष्णाग्राहगृहीतानां संसारार्णवपातिनाम् । आवर्तैरूह्यमानानां दूरं स्वमन एव नौः
verses.transliteration: tṛṣṇāgrāhagṛhītānāṃ saṃsārārṇavapātinām | āvartairūhyamānānāṃ dūraṃ svamana eva nauḥ
verses.translation: For those seized by the crocodile of craving, falling into the ocean of the world, carried far by whirlpools, one's own mind alone is the boat.

verses.sanskrit: मनसैव मनश्छित्त्वा पाशं परमबन्धनम् । भवादुत्तारयात्मानं नासावन्येन तार्यते
verses.transliteration: manasaiva manaśchittvā pāśaṃ paramabandhanam | bhavāduttārayātmānaṃ nāsāvanyena tāryate
verses.translation: Cutting the noose, the supreme bondage, with the mind alone, carry yourself across becoming; he is not carried across by another.

verses.sanskrit: या योदेति मनोनाम्नी वासना वासितान्तरा । तां तां परिहरेत्प्राज्ञस्ततोऽविद्याक्षयो भवेत्
verses.transliteration: yā yodeti manonāmnī vāsanā vāsitāntarā | tāṃ tāṃ pariharetprājñastato'vidyākṣayo bhavet
verses.translation: Whichever impression arises that is called mind, perfumed within, the wise should avoid each; then ignorance will be destroyed.

verses.sanskrit: भोगैकवासनां त्यक्त्वा त्यज त्वं भेदवासनाम् । भावाभावौ ततस्त्यक्त्या निर्विकल्पः सुखी भव
verses.transliteration: bhogaikavāsanāṃ tyaktvā tyaja tvaṃ bhedavāsanām | bhāvābhāvau tatastyaktyā nirvikalpaḥ sukhī bhava
verses.translation: Giving up the sole impression of enjoyment, give up the impression of difference; then, abandoning being and non-being, be free of conceptions and happy.

verses.sanskrit: एष एव मनोनाशस्त्वविद्यानाश एव च । यत्तत्संवेद्यते किंचित्तत्रास्थापरिवर्जनम्
verses.transliteration: eṣa eva manonāśastvavidyānāśa eva ca | yattatsaṃvedyate kiṃcittatrāsthāparivarjanam
verses.translation: This alone is the destruction of mind and of ignorance: that whatever is perceived, one avoids reliance on it.

verses.sanskrit: अनास्थैव हि निर्वाणं दुःखमास्थापरिग्रहः
verses.transliteration: anāsthaiva hi nirvāṇaṃ duḥkhamāsthāparigrahaḥ
verses.translation: Non-reliance alone is liberation; reliance and taking hold is sorrow.

verses.sanskrit: अविद्या विद्यमानैव नष्टप्रज्ञेषु दृश्यते । नाम्नैवाङ्गीकृताकारा सम्यक्प्रज्ञस्य सा कुतः
verses.transliteration: avidyā vidyamānaiva naṣṭaprajñeṣu dṛśyate | nāmnaivāṅgīkṛtākārā samyakprajñasya sā kutaḥ
verses.translation: Ignorance, though non-existent, is seen among those whose insight is destroyed; it has form accepted by name alone; how could it exist for one of right insight?

verses.sanskrit: तावत्संसारभृगुषु स्वात्मना सह देहिनम् । आन्दोलयति नीरन्ध्रं दुःखकण्टकशालिषु
verses.transliteration: tāvatsaṃsārabhṛguṣu svātmanā saha dehinam | āndolayati nīrandhraṃ duḥkhakaṇṭakaśāliṣu
verses.translation: So long it swings the embodied one, together with himself, on the cliffs of the world, thick with thorns of sorrow.

verses.sanskrit: अविद्या यावदस्यास्तु नोत्पन्ना क्षयकारिणी । स्वयमात्मावलोकेच्छा मोहसंक्षयकारिणी
verses.transliteration: avidyā yāvadasyāstu notpannā kṣayakāriṇī | svayamātmāvalokecchā mohasaṃkṣayakāriṇī
verses.translation: As long as the destroyer of this ignorance has not arisen — the desire to see the Self oneself that destroys delusion.

verses.sanskrit: अस्याः परं प्रपश्यन्ताः स्वात्मनाशः प्रजायते । दृष्टे सर्वगते बोधे स्वयं ह्येषा विलीयते
verses.transliteration: asyāḥ paraṃ prapaśyantāḥ svātmanāśaḥ prajāyate | dṛṣṭe sarvagate bodhe svayaṃ hyeṣā vilīyate
verses.translation: For those who look beyond it, the destruction of this self-ignorance is born; when the all-pervading knowledge is seen, it dissolves by itself.

verses.sanskrit: इच्छामात्रमविद्येयं तन्नाशो मोक्ष उच्यते । स चासंकल्पमात्रेण सिद्धो भवति वै मुने
verses.transliteration: icchāmātramavidyeyaṃ tannāśo mokṣa ucyate | sa cāsaṃkalpamātreṇa siddho bhavati vai mune
verses.translation: This ignorance is mere desire; its destruction is called liberation; and it is accomplished by non-intention alone, O sage.

verses.sanskrit: मनागपि मनोव्योम्नि वासनारजनी क्षये । कालिका तनुतामेति चिदादित्याप्रकाशनात्
verses.transliteration: manāgapi manovyomni vāsanārajanī kṣaye | kālikā tanutāmeti cidādityāprakāśanāt
verses.translation: In the sky of the mind, when the night of impressions wanes, even a little, the darkness thins by the shining of the sun of consciousness.

verses.sanskrit: चैतान्युपातरहितं सामान्येन च सर्वगम् । यच्चित्तत्त्वमनाख्येयं स आत्मा परमेश्वरः
verses.transliteration: caitānyupātarahitaṃ sāmānyena ca sarvagam | yaccittattvamanākhyeyaṃ sa ātmā parameśvaraḥ
verses.translation: That principle of consciousness, free of attachment to the perceived and commonly all-pervading, indescribable — that is the Self, the Supreme Lord.

verses.sanskrit: सर्वं च खल्विदं ब्रह्म नित्यचिद्घनमक्षतम् । कल्पनान्या मनोनाम्नी विद्यते न हि काचन
verses.transliteration: sarvaṃ ca khalvidaṃ brahma nityacidghanamakṣatam | kalpanānyā manonāmnī vidyate na hi kācana
verses.translation: All this indeed is Brahman, the eternal mass of consciousness, unbroken; there is no other imagination called mind at all.

verses.sanskrit: न जायते न म्रियत्ते किंचिदत्र जगत्त्रये । न च भावविकाराणां सत्ता क्वचन विद्यते
verses.transliteration: na jāyate na mriyatte kiṃcidatra jagattraye | na ca bhāvavikārāṇāṃ sattā kvacana vidyate
verses.translation: Nothing here in the three worlds is born or dies; nor does the being of the modifications of existence exist anywhere.

verses.sanskrit: केवलं केवलाभासं सर्वसामान्यमक्षतम् । चैत्यानुपातरहितं चिन्मात्रमिह विद्यते
verses.transliteration: kevalaṃ kevalābhāsaṃ sarvasāmānyamakṣatam | caityānupātarahitaṃ cinmātramiha vidyate
verses.translation: Only the alone, shining as alone, common to all, unbroken, free of attachment to the perceived — mere consciousness exists here.

verses.sanskrit: तस्मिन्नित्ये तते शुद्धे चिन्मात्रे निरुपद्रवे । शान्ते शमसमाभोगे निर्विकारे चिदात्मनि
verses.transliteration: tasminnitye tate śuddhe cinmātre nirupadrave | śānte śamasamābhoge nirvikāre cidātmani
verses.translation: In that eternal, extended, pure, mere consciousness, undisturbed, quiet, with the enjoyment of peace, changeless, the Self of consciousness.

verses.sanskrit: यैषा स्वभावाभिमतं स्वयं संकल्प्य धावति । चिच्चैत्यं स्वयमम्लानं माननान्मन उच्यते । अतः संकल्पसिद्धेयं संकल्पेनैव नश्यति
verses.transliteration: yaiṣā svabhāvābhimataṃ svayaṃ saṃkalpya dhāvati | ciccaityaṃ svayamamlānaṃ mānanānmana ucyate | ataḥ saṃkalpasiddheyaṃ saṃkalpenaiva naśyati
verses.translation: That which runs, imagining by itself what accords with its nature — conscious perceived, itself unfading — is called mind by thinking. So this, established by intention, is destroyed by intention alone.

verses.sanskrit: नाहं ब्रह्मेति संकल्पात्सुदृढाद्बध्यते मनः । सर्वं ब्रह्मेति संकल्पात्सुदृढान्मुच्यते मनः
verses.transliteration: nāhaṃ brahmeti saṃkalpātsudṛḍhādbadhyate manaḥ | sarvaṃ brahmeti saṃkalpātsudṛḍhānmucyate manaḥ
verses.translation: By the firm intention "I am not Brahman," the mind is bound; by the firm intention "all is Brahman," the mind is freed.

verses.sanskrit: कृशोऽहं दुःखबद्धोऽहं हस्तपादादिमानहम् । इति भावानुरूपेण व्यवहारेण बध्यते
verses.transliteration: kṛśo'haṃ duḥkhabaddho'haṃ hastapādādimānaham | iti bhāvānurūpeṇa vyavahāreṇa badhyate
verses.translation: "I am thin, I am bound by sorrow, I have hands and feet" — by acting according to such notions one is bound.

verses.sanskrit: नाहं दुःखी न मे देहो बन्धः कोऽस्यात्मनि स्थितः । इति भावानुरूपेण व्यवहारेण मुच्यते
verses.transliteration: nāhaṃ duḥkhī na me deho bandhaḥ ko'syātmani sthitaḥ | iti bhāvānurūpeṇa vyavahāreṇa mucyate
verses.translation: "I am not sorrowful, the body is not mine; what bondage exists in the Self?" — by acting according to such notions one is freed.

verses.sanskrit: नाहं मांसं न चास्थीनि देहादन्यः परोऽस्म्यहम् । इति निश्चितवानन्तः क्षीणाविद्यो विमुच्यते
verses.transliteration: nāhaṃ māṃsaṃ na cāsthīni dehādanyaḥ paro'smyaham | iti niścitavānantaḥ kṣīṇāvidyo vimucyate
verses.translation: "I am not flesh and bones; I am other than the body, the supreme" — he who is thus settled within, with ignorance wasted, is freed.

verses.sanskrit: कल्पितेयमविद्येयमनात्मन्यात्मभावनात् । परं पौरुषमाश्रित्य यत्नात्परमया धिया । भोगेच्छां दूरतस्त्यक्त्वा निर्विकल्पः सुखी भव
verses.transliteration: kalpiteyamavidyeyamanātmanyātmabhāvanāt | paraṃ pauruṣamāśritya yatnātparamayā dhiyā | bhogecchāṃ dūratastyaktvā nirvikalpaḥ sukhī bhava
verses.translation: This ignorance is imagined, from the notion of Self in the non-Self. Relying on supreme effort, with effort and supreme intellect, giving up the wish for enjoyment far away, be free of conceptions and happy.

verses.sanskrit: मम पुत्रो मम धनमहं सोऽयमिदं मम । इतीयमिन्द्रजालेन वासनैव विवल्गति
verses.transliteration: mama putro mama dhanamahaṃ so'yamidaṃ mama | itīyamindrajālena vāsanaiva vivalgati
verses.translation: "My son, my wealth, I am he, this is mine" — thus an impression prances about like a magic show.

verses.sanskrit: मा भवाज्ञो भव ज्ञस्त्वं जहि संसारभावनाम् । अनात्मन्यात्मभावेन किमज्ञ इव रोदिषि
verses.transliteration: mā bhavājño bhava jñastvaṃ jahi saṃsārabhāvanām | anātmanyātmabhāvena kimajña iva rodiṣi
verses.translation: Do not be ignorant; be knowing; abandon the contemplation of the world; why do you weep like the ignorant, by the notion of Self in the non-Self?

verses.sanskrit: कस्तवायं जडो मूको देहो मांसमयोऽशुचिः । यदर्थं सुखदुःखाभ्यामवशः परिभूयसे
verses.transliteration: kastavāyaṃ jaḍo mūko deho māṃsamayo'śuciḥ | yadarthaṃ sukhaduḥkhābhyāmavaśaḥ paribhūyase
verses.translation: What is this body of yours, dull, mute, made of flesh, impure, for whose sake you are helplessly overcome by pleasure and pain?

verses.sanskrit: अहो नु चित्रं यत्सत्यं ब्रह्म तद्विस्मृतं नृणाम् । तिष्ठतस्तव कार्येषु मास्तु रागानुरञ्जना
verses.transliteration: aho nu citraṃ yatsatyaṃ brahma tadvismṛtaṃ nṛṇām | tiṣṭhatastava kāryeṣu māstu rāgānurañjanā
verses.translation: Oh, how strange that men have forgotten the Brahman that is truth! While you stand in your tasks, let there be no coloring of attachment.

verses.sanskrit: अहो नु चित्रं पद्मोत्थैर्बद्धास्तन्तुभिरद्रयः । अविद्यमान या विद्या तया विश्वं खिलीकृतम्
verses.transliteration: aho nu citraṃ padmotthairbaddhāstantubhiradrayaḥ | avidyamāna yā vidyā tayā viśvaṃ khilīkṛtam
verses.translation: Oh, how strange that mountains are bound by threads from a lotus! By that knowledge which does not exist, the world is laid waste.

verses.sanskrit: इदं तद्वज्रतां यातं तृणमात्रं जगत्त्रयम्
verses.transliteration: idaṃ tadvajratāṃ yātaṃ tṛṇamātraṃ jagattrayam
verses.translation: This three-world has become like a thunderbolt, a mere blade of grass.

verses.sanskrit: इत्युपनिषत्
verses.transliteration: ityupaniṣat
verses.translation: Thus the Upanishad.

verses.sanskrit: ऋभुः ॥ अथापरं प्रवक्ष्यामि शृणु तात यथायथम् । अज्ञानभूः सप्तपदा ज्ञभूः सप्तपदैव हि
verses.transliteration: ṛbhuḥ || athāparaṃ pravakṣyāmi śṛṇu tāta yathāyatham | ajñānabhūḥ saptapadā jñabhūḥ saptapadaiva hi
verses.translation: Ribhu said: Now I shall tell you the other; listen, dear one, as it is. The ground of ignorance has seven stages, and the ground of knowledge also seven stages.

verses.sanskrit: पदान्तराण्यसंख्यानि प्रभवन्त्यन्यथैतयोः । स्वरूपावस्थितिर्मुक्तिस्तद्भ्रंशोऽहंत्ववेदनम्
verses.transliteration: padāntarāṇyasaṃkhyāni prabhavantyanyathaitayoḥ | svarūpāvasthitirmuktistadbhraṃśo'haṃtvavedanam
verses.translation: Countless other stages arise in these two otherwise. Abiding in one's own nature is liberation; falling from it is the perception of "I-ness."

verses.sanskrit: शुद्धसन्मात्रसंवित्तेः स्वरूपान्न चलन्ति ये । रागद्वेषादयो भावास्तेषां नाज्ञत्वसंभवः
verses.transliteration: śuddhasanmātrasaṃvitteḥ svarūpānna calanti ye | rāgadveṣādayo bhāvāsteṣāṃ nājñatvasaṃbhavaḥ
verses.translation: Those in whom feelings like attachment and hatred do not move away from the awareness of pure mere being, one's own nature — in them ignorance cannot arise.

verses.sanskrit: यः स्वरूपपरिभ्रंशश्चेत्वार्थे चिति मज्जनम् । एतस्मादपरो मोहो न भूतो न भविष्यति
verses.transliteration: yaḥ svarūpaparibhraṃśaścetvārthe citi majjanam | etasmādaparo moho na bhūto na bhaviṣyati
verses.translation: The falling away from one's own nature, the immersion of consciousness in objects — no other delusion than this has been or will be.

verses.sanskrit: अर्थादर्थान्तरं चित्ते याति मध्ये तु या स्थितिः । सा ध्वस्तमननाकारा स्वरूपस्थितिरुच्यते
verses.transliteration: arthādarthāntaraṃ citte yāti madhye tu yā sthitiḥ | sā dhvastamananākārā svarūpasthitirucyate
verses.translation: The mind goes from object to object; the state in the middle, with thinking destroyed, is called abiding in one's own nature.

verses.sanskrit: संशान्तसर्वसंकल्पा या शिलावदवस्थितिः । जाग्रन्निद्राविनिर्मुक्ता सा स्वरूपस्थितिः परा
verses.transliteration: saṃśāntasarvasaṃkalpā yā śilāvadavasthitiḥ | jāgrannidrāvinirmuktā sā svarūpasthitiḥ parā
verses.translation: That state of rock-like stillness, with all intentions quieted, free of waking and sleep, is the supreme abiding in one's own nature.

verses.sanskrit: अहन्तांशे क्षते शान्ते भेदनिष्पन्दचित्तता । अजडा या प्रचलति तत्स्वरूपमितीरितम्
verses.transliteration: ahantāṃśe kṣate śānte bhedaniṣpandacittatā | ajaḍā yā pracalati tatsvarūpamitīritam
verses.translation: When the portion of ego is destroyed and quieted, the unmoving, non-inert state of mind, free of the vibration of difference, which moves — that is declared to be one's own nature.

verses.sanskrit: बीजं जाग्रत्तथा जाग्रन्महाजाग्रत्तथैव च । जाग्रत्स्वप्नस्तथा स्वप्नः स्वप्नजाग्रत्सुषुप्तिकम्
verses.transliteration: bījaṃ jāgrattathā jāgranmahājāgrattathaiva ca | jāgratsvapnastathā svapnaḥ svapnajāgratsuṣuptikam
verses.translation: The seed-waking, then waking, great waking, likewise waking-dream, then dream, dream-waking, and deep sleep.

verses.sanskrit: इति सप्तविधो मोहः पुनरेष परस्परम् । श्लिष्टो भवत्यनेकाग्र्यं श्रुणु लक्षणमस्य तु
verses.transliteration: iti saptavidho mohaḥ punareṣa parasparam | śliṣṭo bhavatyanekāgryaṃ śruṇu lakṣaṇamasya tu
verses.translation: Thus delusion is sevenfold, and again these cling to one another; it becomes of many aspects; now hear its characteristics.

verses.sanskrit: प्रथमं चेतनं यत्स्यादनाख्यं निर्मलं चितः । भविष्यच्चित्तजीवादिनामशब्दार्थभाजनम्
verses.transliteration: prathamaṃ cetanaṃ yatsyādanākhyaṃ nirmalaṃ citaḥ | bhaviṣyaccittajīvādināmaśabdārthabhājanam
verses.translation: First is the consciousness that is nameless, the stainless of the Self; the vessel of the future names and meanings such as mind and individual.

verses.sanskrit: बीजरूपस्थितं जाग्रद्बीजजाग्रत्तदुच्यते । एषा ज्ञप्तेर्नवावस्था त्वजाग्रत्संस्थितिं श्रुणु
verses.transliteration: bījarūpasthitaṃ jāgradbījajāgrattaducyate | eṣā jñapternavāvasthā tvajāgratsaṃsthitiṃ śruṇu
verses.translation: The waking that stays in seed-form is called seed-waking. This is the ninefold state of awareness; hear now the state of non-waking.

verses.sanskrit: नवप्रसूतस्य परादयं चाहमिदं मम । इति यः प्रत्ययः स्वस्थस्तज्जाग्रत्प्रागभावनात्
verses.transliteration: navaprasūtasya parādayaṃ cāhamidaṃ mama | iti yaḥ pratyayaḥ svasthastajjāgratprāgabhāvanāt
verses.translation: For one newly born, the conviction "I am this, this is mine," abiding in itself, from the prior contemplation, is that waking.

verses.sanskrit: अयं सोऽहमिदं तन्म इति जन्मान्तरोदितः । पीवरः प्रत्ययः प्रोक्तो महाजाग्रदिति स्फुटम्
verses.transliteration: ayaṃ so'hamidaṃ tanma iti janmāntaroditaḥ | pīvaraḥ pratyayaḥ prokto mahājāgraditi sphuṭam
verses.translation: The conviction arisen from another birth, "this I am, this is that of mine," robust, is clearly called great waking.

verses.sanskrit: अरूढमथवा रूढं सर्वथा तन्मयात्मकम् । यज्जाग्रतो मनोराज्यं यज्जाग्रत्स्वप्न उच्यते
verses.transliteration: arūḍhamathavā rūḍhaṃ sarvathā tanmayātmakam | yajjāgrato manorājyaṃ yajjāgratsvapna ucyate
verses.translation: Whether unfixed or fixed, wholly made of it, the waking mind-kingdom of daydreams is called waking-dream.

verses.sanskrit: द्विचन्द्रशुक्तिकारूप्यमृगतृष्णादिभेदतः । अभ्यासं प्राप्य जाग्रत्तत्स्वप्नो नानाविधो भवेत्
verses.transliteration: dvicandraśuktikārūpyamṛgatṛṣṇādibhedataḥ | abhyāsaṃ prāpya jāgrattatsvapno nānāvidho bhavet
verses.translation: By the distinction of the double moon, silver in shell, mirage and the like, waking dream, through practice, becomes many-sorted.

verses.sanskrit: अल्पकालं मया दृष्टमेतन्नोदेति यत्र हि । परामर्षः प्रबुद्धस्य स स्वप्न
verses.transliteration: alpakālaṃ mayā dṛṣṭametannodeti yatra hi | parāmarṣaḥ prabuddhasya sa svapna
verses.translation: "I saw this for a short time," where it does not arise — the reflection of one awakened — is the dream.

verses.sanskrit: चिरं संदर्शनाभावादप्रफुल्लं बृहद्वचः । चिरकालानुवृत्तिस्तु स्वप्नो जाग्रदिवोदितः
verses.transliteration: ciraṃ saṃdarśanābhāvādapraphullaṃ bṛhadvacaḥ | cirakālānuvṛttistu svapno jāgradivoditaḥ
verses.translation: Because of the absence of long observation, a great utterance not bloomed; but a long-continued dream appears like waking.

verses.sanskrit: स्वप्नजाग्रदिति प्रोक्तं जाग्रत्यपि परिस्फुरत् । षडवस्था परित्यागो जडा जीवस्य या स्थितिः
verses.transliteration: svapnajāgraditi proktaṃ jāgratyapi parisphurat | ṣaḍavasthā parityāgo jaḍā jīvasya yā sthitiḥ
verses.translation: "Dream-waking" is said to be what flashes even in waking. The abandonment of six states, the dull state of the individual.

verses.sanskrit: भविष्यद्दुःखबोधाढ्या सौषुप्तिः सोच्यते गतिः । जगत्तस्यामवस्थायामन्तस्तमसि लीयते
verses.transliteration: bhaviṣyadduḥkhabodhāḍhyā sauṣuptiḥ socyate gatiḥ | jagattasyāmavasthāyāmantastamasi līyate
verses.translation: Rich in the perception of future suffering, that is called deep sleep; in that state the world dissolves into inner darkness.

verses.sanskrit: सप्तावस्था इमाः प्रोक्ता मया ज्ञानस्य वै द्विज । एकैका शतसंख्यात्र नानाविभवरूपिणी
verses.transliteration: saptāvasthā imāḥ proktā mayā jñānasya vai dvija | ekaikā śatasaṃkhyātra nānāvibhavarūpiṇī
verses.translation: These seven states of knowledge have been told by me, O twice-born; each is here hundredfold, with various expressions.

verses.sanskrit: इमां सप्तपदां ज्ञानभूमिमाकर्णयानघ । नानया ज्ञातया भूयो मोहपङ्के निमज्जति
verses.transliteration: imāṃ saptapadāṃ jñānabhūmimākarṇayānagha | nānayā jñātayā bhūyo mohapaṅke nimajjati
verses.translation: Hear this sevenfold ground of knowledge, sinless one; having known this, one does not again sink into the mire of delusion.

verses.sanskrit: वदन्ति बहुभेदेन वादिनो योगभूमिकाः । मम त्वभिमता नूनमिमा एव शुभप्रदाः
verses.transliteration: vadanti bahubhedena vādino yogabhūmikāḥ | mama tvabhimatā nūnamimā eva śubhapradāḥ
verses.translation: Debaters speak of the grounds of yoga in many ways; to me, these alone are approved and give good.

verses.sanskrit: अवबोधं विदुर्ज्ञानं तदिदं साप्तभूमिकम् । मुक्तिस्तु ज्ञेयमित्युक्ता भूमिकासप्तकात्परम्
verses.transliteration: avabodhaṃ vidurjñānaṃ tadidaṃ sāptabhūmikam | muktistu jñeyamityuktā bhūmikāsaptakātparam
verses.translation: They know awareness as knowledge, that which has seven grounds; liberation is called the known, beyond the seven grounds.

verses.sanskrit: ज्ञानभूमिः शुभेच्छाख्या प्रथमा समुदाहृता । विचारणा द्वितीया तु तृतीया तनुमानसी
verses.transliteration: jñānabhūmiḥ śubhecchākhyā prathamā samudāhṛtā | vicāraṇā dvitīyā tu tṛtīyā tanumānasī
verses.translation: The ground of knowledge called Good Desire is declared first; the second is Inquiry; the third, Thinning of Mind.

verses.sanskrit: सत्त्वापत्तिश्चतुर्थी स्यात्ततोऽसंसक्तिनामिका । पदार्थभावना षष्ठी सप्तमी तुर्यगा स्मृता
verses.transliteration: sattvāpattiścaturthī syāttato'saṃsaktināmikā | padārthabhāvanā ṣaṣṭhī saptamī turyagā smṛtā
verses.translation: The fourth is Attainment of Sattva, then the one named Non-attachment; the sixth is Contemplation of Things; the seventh is called Turya-gaa.

verses.sanskrit: आसामन्तस्थिता मुक्तिर्यस्यां भूयो न शोचति । एतासां भूमिकानां त्वमिदं निर्वचनं श्रुणु
verses.transliteration: āsāmantasthitā muktiryasyāṃ bhūyo na śocati | etāsāṃ bhūmikānāṃ tvamidaṃ nirvacanaṃ śruṇu
verses.translation: Within these abides liberation, in which one no longer grieves. Now hear the explanation of these grounds.

verses.sanskrit: स्थितः किं मूढ एवास्मि प्रेक्षेऽहं शास्त्रसज्जनैः । वैराग्यपूर्वमिच्छेति शुभेच्छेत्युच्यते बुधैः
verses.transliteration: sthitaḥ kiṃ mūḍha evāsmi prekṣe'haṃ śāstrasajjanaiḥ | vairāgyapūrvamiccheti śubhecchetyucyate budhaiḥ
verses.translation: "Why do I remain a fool? I shall look to scriptures and the good" — desire preceded by dispassion is called Good Desire by the wise.

verses.sanskrit: शास्त्रसज्जनसम्पर्कवैराग्याभ्यासपूर्वकम् । सदाचारप्रवृत्तिर्या प्रोच्यते सा विचारणा
verses.transliteration: śāstrasajjanasamparkavairāgyābhyāsapūrvakam | sadācārapravṛttiryā procyate sā vicāraṇā
verses.translation: The practice of right conduct preceded by contact with scripture and the good and by practice of dispassion is called Inquiry.

verses.sanskrit: विचारणाशुभेच्छाभ्यामिन्द्रियार्थेषु रक्तता । यत्र सा तनुतामेति प्रोच्यते तनुमानसी
verses.transliteration: vicāraṇāśubhecchābhyāmindriyārtheṣu raktatā | yatra sā tanutāmeti procyate tanumānasī
verses.translation: Where by inquiry and good desire attachment to sense-objects grows thin, that is called Thinning of Mind.

verses.sanskrit: भूमिकात्रितयाभ्यासाच्चित्ते तु विरतेर्वशात् । सत्त्वात्मनि स्थिते शुद्धे सत्त्वापत्तिरुदाहृता
verses.transliteration: bhūmikātritayābhyāsāccitte tu viratervaśāt | sattvātmani sthite śuddhe sattvāpattirudāhṛtā
verses.translation: By practice of the three grounds, through the sway of detachment, when the mind stands in pure sattva, Attainment of Sattva is declared.

verses.sanskrit: दशाचतुष्टयाभ्यासादसंसर्गकला तु या । रूढसत्त्वचमत्कारा प्रोक्ता संसक्तिनामिका
verses.transliteration: daśācatuṣṭayābhyāsādasaṃsargakalā tu yā | rūḍhasattvacamatkārā proktā saṃsaktināmikā
verses.translation: By practice of the four stages, the art of non-contact, with the wonder of firm sattva, is called Non-attachment.

verses.sanskrit: भूमिकापञ्चकाभ्यासात्स्वात्मारामतया दृढम् । आभ्यन्तराणां बाह्यानां पदार्थानामभावनात्
verses.transliteration: bhūmikāpañcakābhyāsātsvātmārāmatayā dṛḍham | ābhyantarāṇāṃ bāhyānāṃ padārthānāmabhāvanāt
verses.translation: By practice of the five grounds, with firm delight in one's own Self, through non-contemplation of inner and outer things;

verses.sanskrit: परप्रयुक्तेन चिरं प्रयत्नेनावबोधनम् । पदार्थभावना नाम षष्ठी भवति भूमिका
verses.transliteration: paraprayuktena ciraṃ prayatnenāvabodhanam | padārthabhāvanā nāma ṣaṣṭhī bhavati bhūmikā
verses.translation: awakening by long effort directed by another — the sixth ground is called Contemplation of Things.

verses.sanskrit: भूमिषट्कचिराभ्यासाद्भेदस्यानुपलम्बनात् । यत्स्वभावैकनिष्ठत्वं सा ज्ञेया तुर्यगा गतिः
verses.transliteration: bhūmiṣaṭkacirābhyāsādbhedasyānupalambanāt | yatsvabhāvaikaniṣṭhatvaṃ sā jñeyā turyagā gatiḥ
verses.translation: By long practice of the six grounds, by non-perception of difference, that steadfastness in one's own nature alone is to be known as the Turya-gati.

verses.sanskrit: एषा हि जीवन्मुक्तेषु तुर्यावस्थेति विद्यते । विदेहमुक्तिविषयं तुर्यातीतमतः परम्
verses.transliteration: eṣā hi jīvanmukteṣu turyāvastheti vidyate | videhamuktiviṣayaṃ turyātītamataḥ param
verses.translation: This is known among the liberated-while-living as the fourth state; the state beyond Turiya concerns bodiless liberation.

verses.sanskrit: ये निदाघ महाभागाः साप्तमीं भूमिमाश्रिताः । आत्मारामा महात्मानस्ते महत्पदमागताः
verses.transliteration: ye nidāgha mahābhāgāḥ sāptamīṃ bhūmimāśritāḥ | ātmārāmā mahātmānaste mahatpadamāgatāḥ
verses.translation: Nidagha, those fortunate ones who have taken refuge in the seventh ground, delighting in the Self, great-souled, have reached the great state.

verses.sanskrit: जीवन्मुक्ता न मज्जन्ति सुखदुःखरसस्थिते । प्रकृतेनाथ कार्येण किंचित्कुर्वन्ति वा न वा
verses.transliteration: jīvanmuktā na majjanti sukhaduḥkharasasthite | prakṛtenātha kāryeṇa kiṃcitkurvanti vā na vā
verses.translation: The liberated-while-living do not sink in the taste of pleasure and pain; they do or do not do something according to the occasion.

verses.sanskrit: पार्श्वस्थबोधिताः सन्तः पूर्वाचरक्रमागतम् । आचारमाचरत्येव सुप्तबुद्धवदुत्थिताः
verses.transliteration: pārśvasthabodhitāḥ santaḥ pūrvācarakramāgatam | ācāramācaratyeva suptabuddhavadutthitāḥ
verses.translation: Awakened by those at their side, they just follow the conduct handed down from earlier practice, like one risen from sleep.

verses.sanskrit: भूमिकासप्तकं चैतद्धीमतामेव गोचरम् । प्राप्य ज्ञानदशामेतां पशुम्लेच्छादयोऽपि ये
verses.transliteration: bhūmikāsaptakaṃ caitaddhīmatāmeva gocaram | prāpya jñānadaśāmetāṃ paśumlecchādayo'pi ye
verses.translation: These seven grounds are the domain of the wise alone; even animals and barbarians, having reached this state of knowledge,

verses.sanskrit: सदेहा वाप्यदेहा वा ते मुक्ता नात्र संशयः । ज्ञप्तिर्हि ग्रन्थिविच्छेदस्तस्मिन्सति विमुक्तता
verses.transliteration: sadehā vāpyadehā vā te muktā nātra saṃśayaḥ | jñaptirhi granthivicchedastasminsati vimuktatā
verses.translation: whether embodied or bodiless, are liberated — there is no doubt. Knowledge is the cutting of the knot, and when it exists, there is freedom.

verses.sanskrit: मृगतृष्णाम्बुबुद्ध्य्यादिशान्तिमात्रात्मकस्त्वसौ । ये तु मोहार्णवात्तीर्णास्तैः प्राप्तं परमं पदम्
verses.transliteration: mṛgatṛṣṇāmbubuddhyyādiśāntimātrātmakastvasau | ye tu mohārṇavāttīrṇāstaiḥ prāptaṃ paramaṃ padam
verses.translation: It is of the nature of mere cessation of mirage-water notions and the like. Those who have crossed the ocean of delusion have attained the supreme state.

verses.sanskrit: ते स्थिता भूमिकास्वासु स्वात्मलाभपरायणाः । मनःप्रशमनोपायो योग इत्यभिधीयते
verses.transliteration: te sthitā bhūmikāsvāsu svātmalābhaparāyaṇāḥ | manaḥpraśamanopāyo yoga ityabhidhīyate
verses.translation: They abide in these grounds, devoted to attaining their own Self. The means of quieting the mind is called yoga.

verses.sanskrit: सप्तभूमिः स विज्ञेयः कथितास्ताश्च भूमिकाः । एतासां भूमिकानां तु गमं ब्रह्माभिधं पदम्
verses.transliteration: saptabhūmiḥ sa vijñeyaḥ kathitāstāśca bhūmikāḥ | etāsāṃ bhūmikānāṃ tu gamaṃ brahmābhidhaṃ padam
verses.translation: It is to be known as sevenfold, and those grounds have been told. The goal of these grounds is the state called Brahman.

verses.sanskrit: त्वत्ताहन्तात्मता यत्र परता नास्ति काचन । न क्वचिद्भावकलना न भावाभाव गोचरा
verses.transliteration: tvattāhantātmatā yatra paratā nāsti kācana | na kvacidbhāvakalanā na bhāvābhāva gocarā
verses.translation: Where there is no "you-ness" or "I-ness," no otherness at all; no imagining of things anywhere, no domain of being and non-being.

verses.sanskrit: सर्वं शान्तं निरालम्बं व्योमस्थं शाश्वतं शिवम् । अनामयमनाभासमनामकमकारणम्
verses.transliteration: sarvaṃ śāntaṃ nirālambaṃ vyomasthaṃ śāśvataṃ śivam | anāmayamanābhāsamanāmakamakāraṇam
verses.translation: All quiet, without support, abiding in space, eternal, auspicious, free of disease, without appearance, nameless, causeless.

verses.sanskrit: न सन्नसन्न मध्यान्तं न सर्वं सर्वमेव च । मनोवचोभिरग्राह्यं पूर्णात्पूर्णं सुखात्सुखम्
verses.transliteration: na sannasanna madhyāntaṃ na sarvaṃ sarvameva ca | manovacobhiragrāhyaṃ pūrṇātpūrṇaṃ sukhātsukham
verses.translation: Neither existent nor non-existent, without middle or end, neither all nor not all; ungraspable by mind and speech; fuller than full, happier than happy.

verses.sanskrit: असंवेदनमाशान्तमात्मवेदनमाततम् । सत्ता सर्वपदार्थानां नान्या संवेदनादृते
verses.transliteration: asaṃvedanamāśāntamātmavedanamātatam | sattā sarvapadārthānāṃ nānyā saṃvedanādṛte
verses.translation: Without cognition, wholly quiet, extended as self-awareness; the being of all things is nothing other than awareness.

verses.sanskrit: संबन्धे द्रष्टृदृश्यानां मध्ये दृष्टिर्हि यद्वपुः । द्रष्टृदर्शनदृश्यादिवर्जितं तदिदं पदम्
verses.transliteration: saṃbandhe draṣṭṛdṛśyānāṃ madhye dṛṣṭirhi yadvapuḥ | draṣṭṛdarśanadṛśyādivarjitaṃ tadidaṃ padam
verses.translation: In the relation of seer and seen, the vision in the middle is the form; this state is free of seer, seeing and seen.

verses.sanskrit: देशाद्देशं गते चित्ते मध्ये यच्चेतसो वओउः । अजाड्यसंविन्मननं तन्मयो भव सर्वदा
verses.transliteration: deśāddeśaṃ gate citte madhye yaccetaso vaouḥ | ajāḍyasaṃvinmananaṃ tanmayo bhava sarvadā
verses.translation: When the mind goes from place to place, the interval of the mind in the middle — contemplate the undull awareness, and be of that nature always.

verses.sanskrit: अजाग्रत्स्वप्ननिद्रस्य यत्ते रूपं सनातनम् । अचेतनं चाजडं च तन्मयो भव सर्वदा
verses.transliteration: ajāgratsvapnanidrasya yatte rūpaṃ sanātanam | acetanaṃ cājaḍaṃ ca tanmayo bhava sarvadā
verses.translation: For one not in waking, dream or sleep, whatever is your eternal form, insentient yet not dull — be of that nature always.

verses.sanskrit: जडतां वर्जयित्वैकां शिलाया हृदयं हि तत् । अमनस्कस्वरूपं यत्तन्मयो भव सर्वदा । चित्तं दूरे परित्यज्य योऽसि सोऽसि स्थिरो भव
verses.transliteration: jaḍatāṃ varjayitvaikāṃ śilāyā hṛdayaṃ hi tat | amanaskasvarūpaṃ yattanmayo bhava sarvadā | cittaṃ dūre parityajya yo'si so'si sthiro bhava
verses.translation: Setting aside only the dullness, that which is the heart of a rock, the nature of no-mind — be of that nature always. Abandoning the mind far away, whatever you are, you are; be steady.

verses.sanskrit: पूर्वं मनः समुदितं परमात्मतत्त्वात्तेनाततं जगदिदं सविकल्पजालम् । शून्येन शून्यमपि विप्र यथाम्बरेण नीलत्वमुल्लसति चारुतराभिधानम्
verses.transliteration: pūrvaṃ manaḥ samuditaṃ paramātmatattvāttenātataṃ jagadidaṃ savikalpajālam | śūnyena śūnyamapi vipra yathāmbareṇa nīlatvamullasati cārutarābhidhānam
verses.translation: First the mind arose from the principle of the Supreme Self; by it this world, a net of conceptions, is spread. Even the void, with the void, O Brahmin, as with the sky, the blueness shines, a lovelier name.

verses.sanskrit: संकल्पसंक्षयद्गलिते तु चित्ते संसारमोहमिहिका गलिता भवन्ति । स्वच्छं विभाति शरदीव खमागतायां चिन्मात्रमेकमजमाद्यमनन्तमन्तः
verses.transliteration: saṃkalpasaṃkṣayadgalite tu citte saṃsāramohamihikā galitā bhavanti | svacchaṃ vibhāti śaradīva khamāgatāyāṃ cinmātramekamajamādyamanantamantaḥ
verses.translation: When the mind has melted by the destruction of intention, the mist of the world's delusion dissolves. Clear it shines, as the sky when autumn has come, mere consciousness, one, unborn, primal, infinite within.

verses.sanskrit: अकर्तृकमरङ्गं च गगने चित्रमुत्थितम् । अद्रष्टृकं स्वानुभवमनिद्रस्वप्नदर्शनम्
verses.transliteration: akartṛkamaraṅgaṃ ca gagane citramutthitam | adraṣṭṛkaṃ svānubhavamanidrasvapnadarśanam
verses.translation: A picture without maker or canvas has arisen in the sky; the self-experience without seer, the sight without sleep or dream.

verses.sanskrit: साक्षिभूते समे स्वच्छे निर्विकल्पे चिदात्मनि । निरिच्छं प्रतिबिम्बन्ति जगन्ति मुकुरे यथा
verses.transliteration: sākṣibhūte same svacche nirvikalpe cidātmani | niricchaṃ pratibimbanti jaganti mukure yathā
verses.translation: In the witness, even, clear, free of conceptions, the Self of consciousness, worlds are reflected without desire, as in a mirror.

verses.sanskrit: एकं ब्रह्म चिदाकाशं सर्वात्मकमखण्डितम् । इति भावय यत्नेन चेतश्चाञ्चल्यशान्तये
verses.transliteration: ekaṃ brahma cidākāśaṃ sarvātmakamakhaṇḍitam | iti bhāvaya yatnena cetaścāñcalyaśāntaye
verses.translation: Contemplate with effort, for the quieting of the mind's restlessness: Brahman is one, the space of consciousness, the Self of all, unbroken.

verses.sanskrit: रेखोपरेखावलिता यथैका पीवरी शिला । तथा त्रैलोक्यवलितं ब्रह्मैकमिह दृश्यताम्
verses.transliteration: rekhoparekhāvalitā yathaikā pīvarī śilā | tathā trailokyavalitaṃ brahmaikamiha dṛśyatām
verses.translation: As a single thick rock is covered with lines and sublines, so see here one Brahman covered by the three worlds.

verses.sanskrit: द्वितीयकारणाभावादनुत्पन्नमिदं जगत् । ज्ञातं ज्ञातव्यमधुना दृष्टं द्रष्टव्यमद्भुतम्
verses.transliteration: dvitīyakāraṇābhāvādanutpannamidaṃ jagat | jñātaṃ jñātavyamadhunā dṛṣṭaṃ draṣṭavyamadbhutam
verses.translation: For lack of a second cause, this world is unborn; what was to be known is now known, the wonder to be seen has been seen.

verses.sanskrit: विश्रान्तोऽस्मि चिरं श्रान्तश्चिन्मात्रान्नास्ति किंचन । पश्य विश्रान्तसन्देहं विगताशेषकौतुकम्
verses.transliteration: viśrānto'smi ciraṃ śrāntaścinmātrānnāsti kiṃcana | paśya viśrāntasandehaṃ vigatāśeṣakautukam
verses.translation: I am at rest, long tired; nothing exists apart from pure consciousness. See me with doubts at rest, with all curiosity gone.

verses.sanskrit: निरस्तकल्पनाजालमचित्तत्वं परं पदम् । त एव भूमतां प्राप्ताः संशान्ताशेषकिल्बिषाः
verses.transliteration: nirastakalpanājālamacittatvaṃ paraṃ padam | ta eva bhūmatāṃ prāptāḥ saṃśāntāśeṣakilbiṣāḥ
verses.translation: The state of no-mind, the supreme state, with the net of imagination cast away; those alone have reached greatness, with all sins quieted.

verses.sanskrit: महाधियः शान्तधियो ये याता विमनस्कताम् । जन्तोः कृतविचारस्य विगलद्वृत्तिचेतसः
verses.transliteration: mahādhiyaḥ śāntadhiyo ye yātā vimanaskatām | jantoḥ kṛtavicārasya vigaladvṛtticetasaḥ
verses.translation: The great-minded, of quiet mind, who have attained mindlessness; of the creature who has inquired, whose mind's modifications have melted away;

verses.sanskrit: मननं त्यजतो नित्यं किंचित्परिणतं मनः । दृश्यं सन्त्यजतो हेयमुपादेयमुपेयुषः
verses.transliteration: mananaṃ tyajato nityaṃ kiṃcitpariṇataṃ manaḥ | dṛśyaṃ santyajato heyamupādeyamupeyuṣaḥ
verses.translation: who ever gives up thinking, whose mind has somehow matured, who abandons the seen, who has reached what is to be given up and what to be accepted;

verses.sanskrit: द्रष्टारं पश्यतो नित्यमद्रष्टारमपश्यतः । विज्ञातव्ये परे तत्त्वे जागरूकस्य जीवतः
verses.transliteration: draṣṭāraṃ paśyato nityamadraṣṭāramapaśyataḥ | vijñātavye pare tattve jāgarūkasya jīvataḥ
verses.translation: who ever sees the seer, who does not see the non-seer, who is wakeful in the supreme principle to be known, while alive;

verses.sanskrit: सुप्तस्य धनसंमोहमये संसारवर्त्मनि । अत्यन्तपक्ववैराग्यादरसेषु रसेष्वपि
verses.transliteration: suptasya dhanasaṃmohamaye saṃsāravartmani | atyantapakvavairāgyādaraseṣu raseṣvapi
verses.translation: for the sleeper on the path of the world, made of delusion by wealth, through utterly ripe dispassion, even in tasteless and tasty things;

verses.sanskrit: संसारवासनाजाले खगजाल इवाधुना । त्रोटिते हृदयग्रन्थौ श्लथे वैराग्यरंहसा
verses.transliteration: saṃsāravāsanājāle khagajāla ivādhunā | troṭite hṛdayagranthau ślathe vairāgyaraṃhasā
verses.translation: now that the net of worldly impressions, like a bird-net, is broken, the knot of the heart loosened by the force of dispassion;

verses.sanskrit: कातकं फलमासाद्य यथा वारि प्रसीदति । तथा विज्ञानवशतः स्वभावः सम्प्रसीदति
verses.transliteration: kātakaṃ phalamāsādya yathā vāri prasīdati | tathā vijñānavaśataḥ svabhāvaḥ samprasīdati
verses.translation: as water becomes clear on getting the Katakā fruit, so by virtue of knowledge one's nature becomes serene.

verses.sanskrit: नीरागं निरुपासङ्गं निर्द्वन्द्वं निरुपाश्रयम् । विनिर्याति मनो मोहाद्विहङ्गः पञ्जरादिव
verses.transliteration: nīrāgaṃ nirupāsaṅgaṃ nirdvandvaṃ nirupāśrayam | viniryāti mano mohādvihaṅgaḥ pañjarādiva
verses.translation: Without attachment, without contact, without duality, without support, the mind goes forth from delusion like a bird from a cage.

verses.sanskrit: शान्तसन्देहदौरात्म्यं गतकौतुकविभ्रमम् । परिपूर्णान्तरं चेतः पूर्णेन्दुरिव राजते
verses.transliteration: śāntasandehadaurātmyaṃ gatakautukavibhramam | paripūrṇāntaraṃ cetaḥ pūrṇenduriva rājate
verses.translation: With doubts and evil nature quieted, with curiosity and confusion gone, the mind, filled within, shines like the full moon.

verses.sanskrit: नाहं न चान्यदस्तीह ब्रह्मैवास्मि निरामयम् । इत्थं सदस्तोर्मध्याद्यः पश्यति स पश्यति
verses.transliteration: nāhaṃ na cānyadastīha brahmaivāsmi nirāmayam | itthaṃ sadastormadhyādyaḥ paśyati sa paśyati
verses.translation: "I am not, nor is there anything else here; I am only Brahman, free of disease" — thus whoever sees from the middle of being and non-being, he sees.

verses.sanskrit: अयत्नोपतेष्वक्षिदृग्दृश्येषु यथा मनः । नीरागमेव पतति तद्वत्कार्येषु धीरधीः
verses.transliteration: ayatnopateṣvakṣidṛgdṛśyeṣu yathā manaḥ | nīrāgameva patati tadvatkāryeṣu dhīradhīḥ
verses.translation: As the mind falls without effort on what the eye sees, without attachment, so the steady-minded act in their works.

verses.sanskrit: परिज्ञायोपभुक्तो हि भोगो भवति तुष्टये । विज्ञाय सेवितश्चोरो मैत्रीमेति न चोरताम्
verses.transliteration: parijñāyopabhukto hi bhogo bhavati tuṣṭaye | vijñāya sevitaścoro maitrīmeti na coratām
verses.translation: Enjoyment, after being understood, brings contentment; a thief, known and served, becomes a friend, not a thief.

verses.sanskrit: अशङ्कितापि सम्प्राप्ता ग्रामयात्रा यथाध्वगैः । प्रेक्ष्यते तद्वदेव ज्ञैर्भोगश्रीरवलोक्यते
verses.transliteration: aśaṅkitāpi samprāptā grāmayātrā yathādhvagaiḥ | prekṣyate tadvadeva jñairbhogaśrīravalokyate
verses.translation: As a village-journey met without expectation is looked at by travelers, so the wise regard the splendor of pleasures.

verses.sanskrit: मनसो निगृहीतस्य लीलाभोगोऽल्पकोऽपि यः । तमेवालब्धविस्तारं क्लिष्टत्वाद्बहु मन्यते
verses.transliteration: manaso nigṛhītasya līlābhogo'lpako'pi yaḥ | tamevālabdhavistāraṃ kliṣṭatvādbahu manyate
verses.translation: Of the restrained mind, even a slight playful enjoyment, as it has no extension, he esteems greatly because of its pain.

verses.sanskrit: बद्धमुक्तो महीपालो ग्रासमात्रेण तुष्यति । परैरबद्धो नाक्रान्तो न राष्ट्रं बहु मन्यते
verses.transliteration: baddhamukto mahīpālo grāsamātreṇa tuṣyati | parairabaddho nākrānto na rāṣṭraṃ bahu manyate
verses.translation: A king freed from bondage is satisfied with a mouthful; not bound by others, not attacked, he does not value a kingdom much.

verses.sanskrit: हस्तं हतेन सम्पीड्य दन्तैर्दन्तान्विचूर्ण्य च । अङ्गान्यङ्गैरिवाक्रम्य जयेदादौ स्वकं मनः
verses.transliteration: hastaṃ hatena sampīḍya dantairdantānvicūrṇya ca | aṅgānyaṅgairivākramya jayedādau svakaṃ manaḥ
verses.translation: Pressing hand with hand, crushing teeth with teeth, overcoming limbs with limbs, one should first conquer one's own mind.

verses.sanskrit: मनसो विजयान्नान्या गतिरस्ति भवार्णवे । महानरकसाम्राज्ये मत्तदुष्कृतवारणाः
verses.transliteration: manaso vijayānnānyā gatirasti bhavārṇave | mahānarakasāmrājye mattaduṣkṛtavāraṇāḥ
verses.translation: There is no other way across the ocean of existence than the conquest of the mind; in the empire of great hell, elephants of wrong-doing are in rut.

verses.sanskrit: आशाशरशलाकाढ्या दुर्जया हीन्द्रियारयः । प्रक्षीणचित्तदर्पस्य निगृहीतेन्द्रियद्विषः
verses.transliteration: āśāśaraśalākāḍhyā durjayā hīndriyārayaḥ | prakṣīṇacittadarpasya nigṛhītendriyadviṣaḥ
verses.translation: Rich in arrows and spikes of hope, the enemies of the senses are hard to conquer; for one whose mind's pride has been wasted, who has restrained the foes of the senses,

verses.sanskrit: पद्मिन्य इव हेमन्ते क्षीयन्ते भोगवासनाः । तावन्निशीव वेताला वसन्ति हृदि वासनाः । एकतत्त्वदृढाभ्यासाद्यावन्न विजितं मनः
verses.transliteration: padminya iva hemante kṣīyante bhogavāsanāḥ | tāvanniśīva vetālā vasanti hṛdi vāsanāḥ | ekatattvadṛḍhābhyāsādyāvanna vijitaṃ manaḥ
verses.translation: impressions of enjoyment fade like lotuses in winter. As long as the mind is not conquered by firm practice of the one truth, impressions dwell in the heart like ghouls in the night.

verses.sanskrit: भृत्योऽभिमतकर्तृत्वान्मन्त्री सर्वार्थकारणात् । सामन्तश्चेन्द्रियाक्रान्तेर्मनो मन्ये विवेकिनः
verses.transliteration: bhṛtyo'bhimatakartṛtvānmantrī sarvārthakāraṇāt | sāmantaścendriyākrāntermano manye vivekinaḥ
verses.translation: I regard the mind of the discerning as a servant for doing what is wished, a minister for accomplishing all aims, a vassal for the senses' conquests.

verses.sanskrit: लालनात्स्निग्धललना पालानात्पालकः पिता । सुहृदुत्तमविन्यासान्मनो मन्ये मनीषिणः
verses.transliteration: lālanātsnigdhalalanā pālānātpālakaḥ pitā | suhṛduttamavinyāsānmano manye manīṣiṇaḥ
verses.translation: I regard the mind of the wise as a loving woman for caressing, a father for protecting, a friend for best counsel.

verses.sanskrit: स्वालोकतः शास्त्रदृशा स्वबुद्ध्या स्वानुभावतः । प्रयच्छति परां सिद्धिं त्यक्त्वात्मानं मनःपिता
verses.transliteration: svālokataḥ śāstradṛśā svabuddhyā svānubhāvataḥ | prayacchati parāṃ siddhiṃ tyaktvātmānaṃ manaḥpitā
verses.translation: By one's own light, by the vision of scripture, by one's own intellect, by one's own experience, the mind-father gives the supreme accomplishment, abandoning himself.

verses.sanskrit: सुहृष्टः सुदृढः स्वच्छः सुक्रान्तः सुप्रबोधितः । स्वगुणेनोर्जितो भाति हृदि हृद्यो मनोमणिः
verses.transliteration: suhṛṣṭaḥ sudṛḍhaḥ svacchaḥ sukrāntaḥ suprabodhitaḥ | svaguṇenorjito bhāti hṛdi hṛdyo manomaṇiḥ
verses.translation: Very glad, very firm, clear, well-advanced, well awakened, the jewel of the mind shines pleasing in the heart, strong by its own quality.

verses.sanskrit: एनं मनोमणिं ब्रह्मन्बहुपङ्ककलङ्कितम् । विवेकवारिणा सिद्ध्यै प्रक्षाल्यालोकवान्भव
verses.transliteration: enaṃ manomaṇiṃ brahmanbahupaṅkakalaṅkitam | vivekavāriṇā siddhyai prakṣālyālokavānbhava
verses.translation: O Brahmin, this jewel of the mind, stained by much mud — wash it with the water of discrimination for success, and be one who sees light.

verses.sanskrit: विवेकं परमाश्रित्य बुद्ध्या सत्यमवेक्ष्य च । इन्द्रियारीनलं छित्त्वा तीर्णो भव भवार्णवात्
verses.transliteration: vivekaṃ paramāśritya buddhyā satyamavekṣya ca | indriyārīnalaṃ chittvā tīrṇo bhava bhavārṇavāt
verses.translation: Relying on the highest discrimination and seeing truth by intellect, cut down the enemies of the senses, and cross the ocean of becoming.

verses.sanskrit: आस्थामात्रमनन्तानां दुःखानामाकरं विदुः । अनास्थामात्रमभितः सुखानामालयं विदुः
verses.transliteration: āsthāmātramanantānāṃ duḥkhānāmākaraṃ viduḥ | anāsthāmātramabhitaḥ sukhānāmālayaṃ viduḥ
verses.translation: They know mere reliance as the mine of endless sorrows; they know mere non-reliance as the abode of all happiness.

verses.sanskrit: वासनातन्तुबद्धोऽयं लोको विपरिवर्तते । सा प्रसिद्धातिदुःखाय सुखायोच्छेदमागता
verses.transliteration: vāsanātantubaddho'yaṃ loko viparivartate | sā prasiddhātiduḥkhāya sukhāyocchedamāgatā
verses.translation: This world turns round bound by the thread of impressions; that, famed for great sorrow, becomes happiness when it is cut off.

verses.sanskrit: धीरोऽप्यतिबहुज्ञोऽपि कुलजोऽपि महानपि । तृष्णया बध्यते जन्तुः सिंहः शृङ्खलया यथा
verses.transliteration: dhīro'pyatibahujño'pi kulajo'pi mahānapi | tṛṣṇayā badhyate jantuḥ siṃhaḥ śṛṅkhalayā yathā
verses.translation: Even the steady, even the very learned, even the high-born, even the great, a creature is bound by craving, as a lion by a chain.

verses.sanskrit: परमं पौरुषं यत्नमास्थादाय सृद्यमम् । यथाशास्त्रमनुद्वेगमाचरन्को न सिद्धिभाक्
verses.transliteration: paramaṃ pauruṣaṃ yatnamāsthādāya sṛdyamam | yathāśāstramanudvegamācaranko na siddhibhāk
verses.translation: Taking up supreme human effort and ready exertion, acting according to scripture without agitation, who would not reach success?

verses.sanskrit: अहं सर्वमिदं विश्वं परमात्माहमच्युतः । नान्यदस्तीति संवित्त्या परमा सा ह्यहङ्कृतिः
verses.transliteration: ahaṃ sarvamidaṃ viśvaṃ paramātmāhamacyutaḥ | nānyadastīti saṃvittyā paramā sā hyahaṅkṛtiḥ
verses.translation: "I am all this universe, I am the Supreme Self, the undying; there is nothing else" — that awareness is the supreme I-sense.

verses.sanskrit: सर्वस्माद्व्यतिरिक्तोऽहं वालाग्रादप्यहं तनुः । इति या संविदो ब्रह्मन्द्वितीयाहङ्कृतिः शुभा
verses.transliteration: sarvasmādvyatirikto'haṃ vālāgrādapyahaṃ tanuḥ | iti yā saṃvido brahmandvitīyāhaṅkṛtiḥ śubhā
verses.translation: "I am distinct from all; I am subtler than a hair's tip" — that second I-sense of awareness, O Brahmin, is auspicious.

verses.sanskrit: मोक्षायैषा न बन्धाय जीवन्मुक्तस्य विद्यते
verses.transliteration: mokṣāyaiṣā na bandhāya jīvanmuktasya vidyate
verses.translation: This is for liberation, not for bondage, for the liberated-while-living.

verses.sanskrit: पाणिपादादिमात्रोऽयमहमित्येष निश्चयः । अहंकारस्तृतीयोऽसौ लैकिकस्तुच्छ एव सः
verses.transliteration: pāṇipādādimātro'yamahamityeṣa niścayaḥ | ahaṃkārastṛtīyo'sau laikikastuccha eva saḥ
verses.translation: "I am only hands, feet and the like" — this conviction is egoism, the third, worldly and petty.

verses.sanskrit: जीव एव दुरात्मासौ कन्दः संसारदुस्तरोः । अनेनाभिहतो जन्तुरधोऽधः परिधावति
verses.transliteration: jīva eva durātmāsau kandaḥ saṃsāradustaroḥ | anenābhihato janturadho'dhaḥ paridhāvati
verses.translation: This is the individual, the evil-natured, the bulb of the hard-to-cross tree of the world; struck by it a creature runs ever lower.

verses.sanskrit: अनया दुरहंकृत्या भावात्संत्यक्तया चिरम् । शिष्टाहंकारवाञ्जन्तुः शमवान्याति मुक्तताम्
verses.transliteration: anayā durahaṃkṛtyā bhāvātsaṃtyaktayā ciram | śiṣṭāhaṃkāravāñjantuḥ śamavānyāti muktatām
verses.translation: By this evil egoism long abandoned in its being, the creature with the remaining egoism and peace goes to liberation.

verses.sanskrit: प्रथमौ द्वावहंकारावङ्गीकृत्य त्वलौकिकौ । तृतीयाहंकृतिस्त्याज्या लौकिकी दुःखदायिनी
verses.transliteration: prathamau dvāvahaṃkārāvaṅgīkṛtya tvalaukikau | tṛtīyāhaṃkṛtistyājyā laukikī duḥkhadāyinī
verses.translation: Accepting the first two egoisms as unworldly, the third egoism, worldly and giving pain, is to be abandoned.

verses.sanskrit: अथ ते अपि संत्यज्य सर्वाहंकृतिवर्जितः । स तिष्ठति तथात्युच्चैः परमेवाधिरोहति
verses.transliteration: atha te api saṃtyajya sarvāhaṃkṛtivarjitaḥ | sa tiṣṭhati tathātyuccaiḥ paramevādhirohati
verses.translation: Then, abandoning those too, free of all ego-sense, he stays thus most high and ascends to the supreme.

verses.sanskrit: भोगेच्छामात्रको बन्धस्तत्त्यागो मोक्ष उच्यते । मनसोऽभ्युदयो नाशो मनोनाशो महोदयः
verses.transliteration: bhogecchāmātrako bandhastattyāgo mokṣa ucyate | manaso'bhyudayo nāśo manonāśo mahodayaḥ
verses.translation: Bondage is mere desire for enjoyment; its renunciation is called liberation. The rise of the mind is destruction; the destruction of the mind is a great rise.

verses.sanskrit: ज्ञमनो नाशमभ्येति मनोऽज्ञस्य हि शृङ्खला । नानन्दं न निरानन्दं न चलं नाचलं स्थिरम् । न सन्नासन्न चैतेषां मध्यं ज्ञानिमनो विदुः
verses.transliteration: jñamano nāśamabhyeti mano'jñasya hi śṛṅkhalā | nānandaṃ na nirānandaṃ na calaṃ nācalaṃ sthiram | na sannāsanna caiteṣāṃ madhyaṃ jñānimano viduḥ
verses.translation: The mind of the knower goes to destruction; the mind of the ignorant is a chain. Neither bliss nor non-bliss, neither moving nor unmoving, steady, neither existent nor non-existent, nor the middle of these — thus they know the mind of the wise.

verses.sanskrit: यथा सौक्ष्म्याच्चिदाभास्य आकाशो नोपलक्ष्यते । तथा निरंशश्चिद्भावः सर्वगोऽपि न लक्ष्यते
verses.transliteration: yathā saukṣmyāccidābhāsya ākāśo nopalakṣyate | tathā niraṃśaścidbhāvaḥ sarvago'pi na lakṣyate
verses.translation: As the sky, being subtle, is not noticed as a reflection of consciousness, so the partless state of consciousness, though all-pervading, is not noticed.

verses.sanskrit: सर्वसंकल्परहिता सर्वसंज्ञाविवर्जिता । सैषा चिदविनाशात्मा स्वात्मेत्यादिकृताभिधा
verses.transliteration: sarvasaṃkalparahitā sarvasaṃjñāvivarjitā | saiṣā cidavināśātmā svātmetyādikṛtābhidhā
verses.translation: Free of all intention, devoid of all names, this indestructible consciousness is given names such as "Self" and the like.

verses.sanskrit: आकाशशतभागाण्छा ज्ञेषु निष्कलरूपिणी । सकलामलसंसारस्वरूपैकात्मदर्शिनी
verses.transliteration: ākāśaśatabhāgāṇchā jñeṣu niṣkalarūpiṇī | sakalāmalasaṃsārasvarūpaikātmadarśinī
verses.translation: A hundredth part of space, in the knowers of a partless form, seeing the one Self as the whole nature of the pure world.

verses.sanskrit: नास्तमेति न चोदेति नोत्तिष्ठति न तिष्ठति । न च याति न चायाति न च नेह न चेह चित्
verses.transliteration: nāstameti na codeti nottiṣṭhati na tiṣṭhati | na ca yāti na cāyāti na ca neha na ceha cit
verses.translation: It neither sets nor rises, neither stands up nor stays; neither goes nor comes; consciousness is neither here nor not here.

verses.sanskrit: सैषा चियमलाकारा निर्विकल्पा निरास्पदा
verses.transliteration: saiṣā ciyamalākārā nirvikalpā nirāspadā
verses.translation: This consciousness has a spotless form, free of conceptions, without support.

verses.sanskrit: आदौ शमदमप्रायैर्गुणैः शिष्यं विशोधयेत् । पश्चात्सर्वमिदं ब्रह्म शुद्धस्त्वमिति बोधयेत्
verses.transliteration: ādau śamadamaprāyairguṇaiḥ śiṣyaṃ viśodhayet | paścātsarvamidaṃ brahma śuddhastvamiti bodhayet
verses.translation: At first one should purify the disciple by qualities such as calm and self-control; afterward one should teach: "All this is Brahman, you are pure."

verses.sanskrit: अज्ञस्यार्धप्रबुद्धस्य सर्वं ब्रह्मेति यो वदेत् । महानरकजालेषु स तेन विनियोजितः
verses.transliteration: ajñasyārdhaprabuddhasya sarvaṃ brahmeti yo vadet | mahānarakajāleṣu sa tena viniyojitaḥ
verses.translation: Whoever says "all is Brahman" to the ignorant or half-awakened is thereby bound to nets of great hell.

verses.sanskrit: प्रबुद्धबुद्धेः प्रक्षीणभोगेच्छस्य निराशिषः । नास्त्यविद्यामलमिति प्राज्ञस्तूपदिशेद्गुरुः
verses.transliteration: prabuddhabuddheḥ prakṣīṇabhogecchasya nirāśiṣaḥ | nāstyavidyāmalamiti prājñastūpadiśedguruḥ
verses.translation: To one of awakened intellect, whose desire for pleasure is exhausted, without hope, the wise teacher should teach: "There is no stain of ignorance."

verses.sanskrit: सति दीप इवालोकः सत्यर्क इव वासरः । सति पुष्प इवामोदश्चिति सत्यं जगत्तथा
verses.transliteration: sati dīpa ivālokaḥ satyarka iva vāsaraḥ | sati puṣpa ivāmodaściti satyaṃ jagattathā
verses.translation: As light exists when there is a lamp, day when there is a sun, fragrance when there is a flower, so the world exists as truth in consciousness.

verses.sanskrit: प्रतिभासत एवेदं न जगत्परमार्थतः । ज्ञानदृष्टौ प्रसन्नायां प्रबोधविततोदये
verses.transliteration: pratibhāsata evedaṃ na jagatparamārthataḥ | jñānadṛṣṭau prasannāyāṃ prabodhavitatodaye
verses.translation: This appears only; the world is not ultimately real. When the eye of knowledge is clear and the arising of awakening spreads,

verses.sanskrit: यथावज्ज्ञास्यसि स्वस्थो मद्वाग्वृष्टिबलाबलम् । अविद्ययैवोत्तमया स्वार्थनाशोद्यमार्थया
verses.transliteration: yathāvajjñāsyasi svastho madvāgvṛṣṭibalābalam | avidyayaivottamayā svārthanāśodyamārthayā
verses.translation: You will rightly know, in your own nature, the strength and weakness of my rain of words; by that supreme ignorance itself, whose purpose is the destruction of self-interest,

verses.sanskrit: विद्या सम्प्राप्यते ब्रह्मन्सर्वदोषापहारिणी । शाम्यति ह्यस्त्रमस्त्रेण मलेन क्षाल्यते मलम्
verses.transliteration: vidyā samprāpyate brahmansarvadoṣāpahāriṇī | śāmyati hyastramastreṇa malena kṣālyate malam
verses.translation: knowledge is attained, O Brahmin, which removes all faults; a weapon is quelled by a weapon, a stain is washed by a stain.

verses.sanskrit: शमं विषं विषेणैति रिपुणा हन्यते रिपुः । ईदृशी भूतमायेयं या स्वनाशेन हर्षदा
verses.transliteration: śamaṃ viṣaṃ viṣeṇaiti ripuṇā hanyate ripuḥ | īdṛśī bhūtamāyeyaṃ yā svanāśena harṣadā
verses.translation: Poison is neutralized by poison, an enemy is slain by an enemy; such is this illusion of beings, which gives joy by its own destruction.

verses.sanskrit: न लक्ष्यते स्वभावोऽस्या वीक्ष्यमाणैव नश्यति । नास्त्येषा परमार्थेनेत्येवं भावनयेद्धया
verses.transliteration: na lakṣyate svabhāvo'syā vīkṣyamāṇaiva naśyati | nāstyeṣā paramārthenetyevaṃ bhāvanayeddhayā
verses.translation: Its nature is not perceived; it perishes just when looked at; "it does not exist in ultimate truth" — contemplate thus with intelligence.

verses.sanskrit: सर्वं ब्रह्मेति यस्यान्तर्भावना सा हि मुक्तिदा । भेददृष्टिरविद्येयं सर्वथा तां विसर्जयेत्
verses.transliteration: sarvaṃ brahmeti yasyāntarbhāvanā sā hi muktidā | bhedadṛṣṭiravidyeyaṃ sarvathā tāṃ visarjayet
verses.translation: The inner contemplation "all is Brahman" gives liberation; the vision of difference is this ignorance; abandon it wholly.

verses.sanskrit: मुने नासाद्यते तद्धि पदमक्षयमुच्यते । कुतो जातेयमिति ते द्विज मास्तु विचारणा
verses.transliteration: mune nāsādyate taddhi padamakṣayamucyate | kuto jāteyamiti te dvija māstu vicāraṇā
verses.translation: That state, O sage, is called imperishable, not obtained; let there be no inquiry on your part, O twice-born, "from where was this born?"

verses.sanskrit: इमां कथमहं हन्मीत्येषा तेऽस्तु विचारणा । अस्तं गतायां क्षीणायामस्यां ज्ञास्यसि तत्पदम्
verses.transliteration: imāṃ kathamahaṃ hanmītyeṣā te'stu vicāraṇā | astaṃ gatāyāṃ kṣīṇāyāmasyāṃ jñāsyasi tatpadam
verses.translation: Let your inquiry be "how shall I kill it?" When it has set and dwindled, you will know that state.

verses.sanskrit: यत एषा यथा चैषा यथा नष्टेत्यखण्डितम् । तदस्या रोगशालाया यत्नं कुरु चिकित्सने
verses.transliteration: yata eṣā yathā caiṣā yathā naṣṭetyakhaṇḍitam | tadasyā rogaśālāyā yatnaṃ kuru cikitsane
verses.translation: "Whence is this, how is this, how is it destroyed?" — in unbroken fashion, make effort for the cure of this house of disease.

verses.sanskrit: यथैषा जन्मदुःखेषु न भूयस्त्वां नियोक्ष्यति । स्वात्मनि स्वपरिस्पन्दैः स्फुरत्यच्छैश्चिदर्णवः
verses.transliteration: yathaiṣā janmaduḥkheṣu na bhūyastvāṃ niyokṣyati | svātmani svaparispandaiḥ sphuratyacchaiścidarṇavaḥ
verses.translation: So that it will not again bind you in the sorrows of birth. In its own self, by its own vibrations, the clear ocean of consciousness shines.

verses.sanskrit: एकात्मकमखण्डं तदित्यन्तर्भाव्यतां दृढम् । किंचित्क्षुभितरूपा सा चिच्छक्तिश्चिन्मयार्णवे
verses.transliteration: ekātmakamakhaṇḍaṃ tadityantarbhāvyatāṃ dṛḍham | kiṃcitkṣubhitarūpā sā cicchaktiścinmayārṇave
verses.translation: Contemplate firmly within: "that is one-natured and undivided." The power of consciousness, slightly stirred in the ocean of consciousness,

verses.sanskrit: तन्मयैव स्फुरत्यच्छा तत्रैवोर्मिरिवार्णवे । आत्मन्येवात्मना व्योम्नि यथा सरसि मारुतः
verses.transliteration: tanmayaiva sphuratyacchā tatraivormirivārṇave | ātmanyevātmanā vyomni yathā sarasi mārutaḥ
verses.translation: shines clear, made of it alone, there as a wave in the ocean; in itself, by itself, in space, as the wind in a lake;

verses.sanskrit: तथैवात्मात्मशक्त्यैव स्वात्मन्येवैति लोलताम् । क्षणं स्फुरति सा देवी सर्वशक्तितया तथा
verses.transliteration: tathaivātmātmaśaktyaiva svātmanyevaiti lolatām | kṣaṇaṃ sphurati sā devī sarvaśaktitayā tathā
verses.translation: so the Self by its own power alone moves about in its own Self; for a moment that goddess shines in the form of all powers.

verses.sanskrit: देशकालक्रियाशक्तिर्न यस्याः सम्प्रकर्षणे । स्वस्वभावं विदित्वोच्चैरप्यनन्तपदे स्थिता
verses.transliteration: deśakālakriyāśaktirna yasyāḥ samprakarṣaṇe | svasvabhāvaṃ viditvoccairapyanantapade sthitā
verses.translation: In whose attainment there is no power of place, time or action, knowing her own nature, though established in the endless state,

verses.sanskrit: रूपं परिमितेनासौ भावयत्यविभाविता । यदैवं भावितं रूपं तया परमकान्तया
verses.transliteration: rūpaṃ parimitenāsau bhāvayatyavibhāvitā | yadaivaṃ bhāvitaṃ rūpaṃ tayā paramakāntayā
verses.translation: she, unperceived, imagines her form as limited; when thus the form is imagined by that supreme beloved,

verses.sanskrit: तदैवैनामनुगता नामसंख्यादिका दृशः । विकल्पकलिताकारं देशकालक्रियास्पदम्
verses.transliteration: tadaivaināmanugatā nāmasaṃkhyādikā dṛśaḥ | vikalpakalitākāraṃ deśakālakriyāspadam
verses.translation: then follow after her the views of name, number and the like; a form shaped by conceptions, the seat of place, time and action.

verses.sanskrit: चितो रूपमिदं ब्रह्मन्क्षेत्रज्ञ इति कथ्यते । वासनाः कल्पयन्सोऽपि यात्यहंकारतां पुनः
verses.transliteration: cito rūpamidaṃ brahmankṣetrajña iti kathyate | vāsanāḥ kalpayanso'pi yātyahaṃkāratāṃ punaḥ
verses.translation: This form of consciousness, O Brahmin, is called the knower of the field; he, imagining impressions, again becomes ego.

verses.sanskrit: अहङ्कारो विनिर्णेता कलङ्की बुद्धिरुच्यते । बुद्धिः संकल्पिताकारा प्रयाति मननास्पदम्
verses.transliteration: ahaṅkāro vinirṇetā kalaṅkī buddhirucyate | buddhiḥ saṃkalpitākārā prayāti mananāspadam
verses.translation: Egoism is the decider, the stained intellect is called buddhi; the intellect, shaped by intention, goes to the seat of thought.

verses.sanskrit: मनो घनविकल्पं तु गच्छतीन्द्रियतां शनैः । पाणिपादमयं देहमिन्द्रियाणि विदुर्बुधाः
verses.transliteration: mano ghanavikalpaṃ tu gacchatīndriyatāṃ śanaiḥ | pāṇipādamayaṃ dehamindriyāṇi vidurbudhāḥ
verses.translation: The mind, dense with conceptions, slowly becomes the senses; the wise know the body, made of hands and feet, and the senses.

verses.sanskrit: एवं जीवो हि संकल्पवासनारज्जुवेष्टितः । दुःखजालपरीतात्मा क्रमादायाति नीचताम्
verses.transliteration: evaṃ jīvo hi saṃkalpavāsanārajjuveṣṭitaḥ | duḥkhajālaparītātmā kramādāyāti nīcatām
verses.translation: Thus the individual, wrapped in the rope of intention and impressions, with a self enveloped in nets of sorrow, gradually comes to lowness.

verses.sanskrit: इति शक्तिमयं चेतो घनाहंकारतां गतम् । कोशकारक्रिमिरिव स्वेच्छया याति बन्धनम्
verses.transliteration: iti śaktimayaṃ ceto ghanāhaṃkāratāṃ gatam | kośakārakrimiriva svecchayā yāti bandhanam
verses.translation: Thus the mind of the nature of power, having become dense egoism, enters bondage by its own will, like a silkworm in its cocoon.

verses.sanskrit: स्वयं कल्पित तन्मात्राजालभ्यन्तरवर्ति च । परां विवशतामेति शृङ्खलाबद्धसिंहवत्
verses.transliteration: svayaṃ kalpita tanmātrājālabhyantaravarti ca | parāṃ vivaśatāmeti śṛṅkhalābaddhasiṃhavat
verses.translation: Dwelling within the net of subtle elements imagined by itself, it falls into utter helplessness like a lion bound in chains.

verses.sanskrit: क्वचिन्मनः क्वचिद्बुद्धिः क्वचिज्ज्ञानं क्वचित्क्रिया । क्वचिदेतदहंकारः क्वचिच्चित्तमिति स्मृतम्
verses.transliteration: kvacinmanaḥ kvacidbuddhiḥ kvacijjñānaṃ kvacitkriyā | kvacidetadahaṃkāraḥ kvaciccittamiti smṛtam
verses.translation: In one place it is called mind, in another intellect, in another knowledge, in another action, in another egoism, in another thought.

verses.sanskrit: क्वचित्प्रकृतिरित्युक्तं क्वचिन्मायेति कल्पितम् । क्वचिन्मलमिति प्रोक्तं क्वचित्कर्मेति संस्मृतम्
verses.transliteration: kvacitprakṛtirityuktaṃ kvacinmāyeti kalpitam | kvacinmalamiti proktaṃ kvacitkarmeti saṃsmṛtam
verses.translation: In one place it is called nature, in another imagined as illusion, in another it is called stain, in another remembered as karma.

verses.sanskrit: क्वचिद्बन्ध इति ख्यातं क्वचित्पुर्यष्टकं स्मृतम् । प्रोक्तं क्वचिदविद्येति क्वचिदिच्छेति संमतम्
verses.transliteration: kvacidbandha iti khyātaṃ kvacitpuryaṣṭakaṃ smṛtam | proktaṃ kvacidavidyeti kvacidiccheti saṃmatam
verses.translation: In one place it is known as bondage, in another recalled as the subtle body of eight, in another called ignorance, in another accepted as desire.

verses.sanskrit: इअमं संसारमखिलमाशापाशविधायकम् । दधदन्तःफलैर्हीनं वटधाना वटं यथा
verses.transliteration: iamaṃ saṃsāramakhilamāśāpāśavidhāyakam | dadhadantaḥphalairhīnaṃ vaṭadhānā vaṭaṃ yathā
verses.translation: Bearing this whole world that makes the noose of hope, empty of inner fruit like a banyan stripped of seed,

verses.sanskrit: चिन्तानलशिखादग्धं कोपाजगरचर्वितम् । कामाब्धिकल्लोलरतं विस्मृतात्मपितामहम्
verses.transliteration: cintānalaśikhādagdhaṃ kopājagaracarvitam | kāmābdhikallolarataṃ vismṛtātmapitāmaham
verses.translation: burnt by the flames of the fire of anxiety, chewed by the python of anger, delighting in the waves of the ocean of desire, forgetful of its Self, the grandfather —

verses.sanskrit: समुद्धर मनो ब्रह्मन्मातङ्गमिव कर्दमात् । एवं जीवाश्रिता भावा भवभावनयाहिताः
verses.transliteration: samuddhara mano brahmanmātaṅgamiva kardamāt | evaṃ jīvāśritā bhāvā bhavabhāvanayāhitāḥ
verses.translation: lift up the mind, O Brahmin, like an elephant from mud. Thus states resting on the individual, set by contemplation of becoming,

verses.sanskrit: ब्रह्मणा कल्पिताकारा लक्षशोऽप्यथ कोटिशः । संख्यातीताः पुरा जाता जायन्तेऽद्यापि चाभितः
verses.transliteration: brahmaṇā kalpitākārā lakṣaśo'pyatha koṭiśaḥ | saṃkhyātītāḥ purā jātā jāyante'dyāpi cābhitaḥ
verses.translation: fashioned by Brahma, by the lakh and by the crore, countless, were born before and are still born all around.

verses.sanskrit: उत्पत्स्यन्तेऽपि चैवान्ये कणौघा इव निर्झरात् । केचित्प्रथमजन्मानः केचिज्जन्मशताधिकाः
verses.transliteration: utpatsyante'pi caivānye kaṇaughā iva nirjharāt | kecitprathamajanmānaḥ kecijjanmaśatādhikāḥ
verses.translation: And others will be born, like streams of drops from a waterfall; some in their first birth, some beyond a hundred births,

verses.sanskrit: केचिच्चासंख्यजन्मानः केचिद्द्वित्रिभवान्तराः । केचित्किन्नरगन्धर्वविद्याधरमहोरगाः
verses.transliteration: keciccāsaṃkhyajanmānaḥ keciddvitribhavāntarāḥ | kecitkinnaragandharvavidyādharamahoragāḥ
verses.translation: some of countless births, some two or three lives apart; some Kinnaras, Gandharvas, Vidyadharas and great serpents;

verses.sanskrit: केचिदर्केन्दुवरुणास्त्र्यक्षाधोक्षजपद्मजाः । केचिद्ब्रह्मणभूपालवैश्यशूद्रगणाः स्थिताः
verses.transliteration: kecidarkenduvaruṇāstryakṣādhokṣajapadmajāḥ | kecidbrahmaṇabhūpālavaiśyaśūdragaṇāḥ sthitāḥ
verses.translation: some suns, moons, Varunas, Shiva, Vishnu, Brahma; some stand as hosts of Brahmins, kings, merchants and servants;

verses.sanskrit: केचित्तृणौषधीवृक्षफलमूलपतङ्गकाः । केचित्कदम्बजम्बीरसालतालतमालकाः
verses.transliteration: kecittṛṇauṣadhīvṛkṣaphalamūlapataṅgakāḥ | kecitkadambajambīrasālatālatamālakāḥ
verses.translation: some grasses, herbs, trees, fruits, roots and insects; some Kadamba, Jambira, Sala, Tala and Tamala trees;

verses.sanskrit: केचिन्महेन्द्रमलयसह्यमन्दरमेरवः । केचित्क्षारोदधिक्षीरघृतेक्षुजलराशयः
verses.transliteration: kecinmahendramalayasahyamandarameravaḥ | kecitkṣārodadhikṣīraghṛtekṣujalarāśayaḥ
verses.translation: some Mahendra, Malaya, Sahya, Mandara and Meru mountains; some oceans of salt, milk, ghee, sugarcane juice;

verses.sanskrit: केचिद्विशालाः कुकुभः केचिन्नद्यो महारयाः । विहायस्युच्चकैः केचिन्निपतन्त्युत्पतन्ति च
verses.transliteration: kecidviśālāḥ kukubhaḥ kecinnadyo mahārayāḥ | vihāyasyuccakaiḥ kecinnipatantyutpatanti ca
verses.translation: some vast quarters, some mighty rivers; some in the sky fall and rise high up,

verses.sanskrit: कन्तुका इव हस्तेन मृत्युनाऽविरतं हताः । भुक्त्वा जन्मसहस्राणि भूयः संसारसंकटे
verses.transliteration: kantukā iva hastena mṛtyunā'virataṃ hatāḥ | bhuktvā janmasahasrāṇi bhūyaḥ saṃsārasaṃkaṭe
verses.translation: struck unceasingly by death like balls by a hand; having enjoyed thousands of births, again in the strait of the world,

verses.sanskrit: पतन्ति केचिदबुधाः सम्प्राप्यापि विवेकताम् । दिक्कालाद्यनवच्छिन्नमात्मतत्त्वं स्वशक्तितः
verses.transliteration: patanti kecidabudhāḥ samprāpyāpi vivekatām | dikkālādyanavacchinnamātmatattvaṃ svaśaktitaḥ
verses.translation: some ignorant fall even after attaining discrimination. The principle of the Self, unlimited by place and time, by its own power

verses.sanskrit: लीलयैव यदादत्ते दिक्कालकलितं वपुः । तदेव जीवपर्यायवासनावेशतः परम्
verses.transliteration: līlayaiva yadādatte dikkālakalitaṃ vapuḥ | tadeva jīvaparyāyavāsanāveśataḥ param
verses.translation: playfully takes a body marked by place and time; that same, through absorption in the impression of individuality, afterwards

verses.sanskrit: मनः सम्पद्यते लोलं कलनाकलनोन्मुखम् । कलयन्ती मनःशक्तिरादौ भावयति क्षणात्
verses.transliteration: manaḥ sampadyate lolaṃ kalanākalanonmukham | kalayantī manaḥśaktirādau bhāvayati kṣaṇāt
verses.translation: becomes the mind, restless, turned toward imagining; the mind-power, imagining, first contemplates in a moment

verses.sanskrit: आकाशभावनामच्छां शब्दबीजरसोन्मुखीम् । ततस्तद्घनतां यातं घनस्पन्दक्रमान्मनः
verses.transliteration: ākāśabhāvanāmacchāṃ śabdabījarasonmukhīm | tatastadghanatāṃ yātaṃ ghanaspandakramānmanaḥ
